title.zh: 卷一百八十七下 列傳第一百三十七下: 忠義下
title.raw: 卷一百八十七下 列傳第一百三十七下: 忠義下 Volume 187 Biographies 137: Loyal and Righteous 2

sentences.zh: ○突厥之始，啟民之前，《隋書》載之備矣，只以入國之事而述之。

translations.literal: ○ On the origins of the Turks, before Qimin Khan, the Sui History records them in full; here I shall relate only their entry into our realm.
translations.idiomatic: ○ The origins of the Turks down to the time before Qimin Khan are fully treated in the History of the Sui; the present account confines itself to their coming into the Tang state.

sentences.zh: 始畢可汗咄吉者，啟民可汗子也。

translations.literal: Shibi Khan, named Tujie, was a son of Qimin Khan.
translations.idiomatic: Shibi Khan, whose personal name was Tujie, was a son of Qimin Khan.

sentences.zh: 隋大業中嗣位，值天下大亂，中國人奔之者眾。

translations.literal: He succeeded to the throne in the Daye era of Sui; the realm was in great turmoil, and many Chinese fled to join him.
translations.idiomatic: He came to the throne during the Sui emperor Yang's Daye reign, when the empire was collapsing and great numbers of Chinese took refuge with him.

sentences.zh: 其族強盛，東自契丹、室韋，西盡吐谷渾、高昌諸國，皆臣屬焉。

translations.literal: His tribe grew powerful; from the Khitan and Shiwei in the east to the Tuyuhun, Gaochang, and other states in the west, all became his subjects.
translations.idiomatic: His people grew so strong that from the Khitan and Shiwei in the east to the Tuyuhun, Gaochang, and the other western states, all acknowledged his rule.

sentences.zh: 控弦百餘萬，北狄之盛，未之有也。

translations.literal: He commanded more than a million bowmen; never had a northern barbarian realm been so great.
translations.idiomatic: He could field more than a million archers—a height of power among the northern peoples never seen before.

sentences.zh: 高視陰山，有輕中夏之志。

translations.literal: Looking down from the Yin Mountains, he harbored contempt for Central China.
translations.idiomatic: From his seat beyond the Yin Mountains he looked south with disdain upon the Chinese heartland.

sentences.zh: 可汗者，猶古之單于；

translations.literal: The title khan was the same as the ancient chanyu;
translations.idiomatic: The khan was the counterpart of the ancient chanyu;

sentences.zh: 妻號可賀敦，猶古之閼氏也。

translations.literal: his consort was styled kehudun, as the ancient yanzhi had been.
translations.idiomatic: his chief wife was called kehudun, the equivalent of the old title yanzhi.

sentences.zh: 其子弟謂之特勒，別部領兵者皆謂之設。

translations.literal: His sons and younger kinsmen were called tegin; leaders of separate divisions who commanded troops were all called shad.
translations.idiomatic: Princes of the royal line were termed tegin, while chiefs of detached divisions who held military command were all known as shad.

sentences.zh: 其大官屈律啜，次阿波，次頡利發，次吐屯，次俟斤，並代居其官而無員數，父兄死則子弟承襲。

translations.literal: Their great offices were, in order, qu'lüchuo, abo, jielifa, tutun, and houjin; men of each line held these posts in succession without fixed quotas, and when father or elder brother died, sons or younger brothers inherited.
translations.idiomatic: The chief offices were qu'lüchuo, then abo, jielifa, tutun, and houjin—each held in hereditary rotation without a set number of incumbents, passing from elder to younger kinsmen on death.

sentences.zh: 高祖起義太原，遣大將軍府司馬劉文靜聘於始畢，引以為援。

translations.literal: When Gaozu raised the army at Taiyuan, he sent Grand General's Staff Marshal Liu Wenjing as envoy to Shibi to secure him as an ally.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu rose in arms at Taiyuan, he dispatched Liu Wenjing, marshal of the grand general's staff, to Shibi Khan to enlist Turkish support.

sentences.zh: 始畢遣其特勒康稍利等獻馬千匹，會於絳郡。

translations.literal: Shibi sent his tegin Kang Shaoli and others to present a thousand horses, joining forces at Jiang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Shibi sent the tegin Kang Shaoli and others with a gift of a thousand horses, and they joined Gaozu's forces at Jiang.

sentences.zh: 又遣二千騎助軍，從平京城。

translations.literal: He also sent two thousand horsemen to aid the army in pacifying the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He further sent two thousand cavalry to help take the capital.

sentences.zh: 及高祖即位，前後賞賜，不可勝紀。

translations.literal: After Gaozu took the throne, rewards and gifts bestowed before and after were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Once Gaozu had ascended the throne, the rewards lavished on the Turks in successive years were beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 始畢自恃其功，益驕踞；

translations.literal: Shibi, relying on his services, grew ever more arrogant and overbearing;
translations.idiomatic: Shibi, confident in what he had done for the new dynasty, grew increasingly arrogant;

sentences.zh: 每遣使者至長安，頗多橫恣。

translations.literal: whenever he sent envoys to Chang'an, they were often insolent and arbitrary.
translations.idiomatic: and his envoys to Chang'an were frequently high-handed and abusive.

sentences.zh: 高祖以中原未定，每優容之。

translations.literal: Gaozu, because the central plains were not yet settled, always treated them with forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu, with the heartland still unsettled, indulged them each time.

sentences.zh: 武德元年，始畢使骨咄祿特勒來朝，宴於太極殿，奏《九部樂》，賚錦彩布絹各有差。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wude, Shibi sent the tegin Kutlug to court; he was feasted in the Hall of Supreme Pole, the Nine Department Music was performed, and brocades, silks, and cloth were bestowed in graded amounts.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude 1 (618), Shibi sent the tegin Kutlug to court. Gaozu entertained him in the Hall of Supreme Pole with the Nine Department Music and gave graded gifts of brocade, silk, and cloth.

sentences.zh: 二年二月，始畢帥兵渡河，至夏州，賊帥梁師都出兵會之，謀入抄掠。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year, Shibi led troops across the river to Xia Prefecture; the rebel chief Liang Shidu marched out to join him, planning raids and plunder.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Wude 2, Shibi crossed the Yellow River with an army as far as Xia Prefecture, where the rebel Liang Shidu joined him with troops for a planned raid into Tang territory.

sentences.zh: 授馬邑賊帥劉武周兵五百餘騎，遣入句註，又追兵大集，欲侵太原。

translations.literal: He gave the Mayi rebel chief Liu Wuzhou more than five hundred horsemen and sent them into Gouzhu; he also gathered a great host in pursuit, intending to invade Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He furnished the Mayi rebel Liu Wuzhou with more than five hundred cavalry and sent them through Gouzhu Pass, while massing a larger force with the aim of striking Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 是月，始畢卒，其子什缽苾以年幼不堪嗣位，立為泥步設，使居東偏，直幽州之北。

translations.literal: That month Shibi died. His son Shiboni, being too young to succeed, was installed as niboshi and placed in the eastern wing, directly north of You Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: That same month Shibi died. His son Shiboni was judged too young to rule and was made niboshi, stationed in the eastern wing just north of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 立其弟俟利弗設，是為處羅可汗。

translations.literal: His younger brother Heli was made shad and became Elu Khan.
translations.idiomatic: Shibi's younger brother Heli was enthroned as Elu Khan.

sentences.zh: 處羅可汗嗣位，又以隋義成公主為妻，遣使入朝告喪。

translations.literal: Elu Khan succeeded to the throne, again took Princess Yicheng of Sui as his wife, and sent envoys to court to announce the death.
translations.idiomatic: On succeeding, Elu Khan again married the Sui princess Yicheng and sent envoys to Chang'an to announce Shibi's death.

sentences.zh: 高祖為之舉哀，廢朝三日，詔百官就館吊其使者，又遣內史舍人鄭德挺往吊處羅，賜物三萬段。

translations.literal: Gaozu mourned for him, suspended court for three days, ordered the officials to call at the lodge to condole with his envoys, and also sent Palace Secretariat drafting secretary Zheng Deting to condole with Elu, bestowing thirty thousand rolls of goods.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu observed mourning, closed court for three days, and ordered the bureaucracy to offer condolences to the Turkish envoys at their lodge. He also sent Zheng Deting to condole with Elu Khan and gave thirty thousand rolls of goods.

sentences.zh: 處羅此後頻遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: Thereafter Elu frequently sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: After that Elu sent tribute missions repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 先是，隋煬帝蕭後及齊王暕之子政道，陷於竇建德。

translations.literal: Earlier, Empress Xiao of Sui emperor Yang and Yang Zhengdao, son of Prince of Qi Yang Gao, had fallen into the hands of Dou Jiande.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Sui empress Xiao and Yang Zhengdao, son of the executed Prince of Qi Yang Gao, had been held by the rebel Dou Jiande.

sentences.zh: 三年二月，處羅迎之，至於牙所，立政道為隋王。

translations.literal: In the second month of the third year, Elu welcomed them to his royal camp and installed Zhengdao as King of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Wude 3, Elu received them at his headquarters and set up Zhengdao as king of a restored Sui.

sentences.zh: 隋末中國人在虜庭者，悉隸於政道，行隋正朔，置百官，居於定襄城，有徒一萬。

translations.literal: All Chinese who at the end of Sui were in the barbarian court were placed under Zhengdao; they used the Sui calendar, established the full bureaucracy, dwelt at Dingxiang city, and numbered ten thousand followers.
translations.idiomatic: Every Chinese still in the Turkish camp was placed under Zhengdao's authority. They kept the Sui calendar, staffed a full court, and lived at Dingxiang with a following of ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 時太宗在籓，受詔討劉武周，師次太原，處羅遣其弟步利設率二千騎與官軍會。

translations.literal: At that time the Prince of Qin, receiving orders to campaign against Liu Wuzhou, halted his army at Taiyuan; Elu sent his younger brother Bujia Shad with two thousand horsemen to join the imperial forces.
translations.idiomatic: While the future Taizong, still prince of Qin, was campaigning against Liu Wuzhou and encamped at Taiyuan, Elu sent his brother Bujia Shad with two thousand cavalry to join the Tang army.

sentences.zh: 六月，處羅至并州，總管李仲文出迎勞之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Elu came to Bing Prefecture; the regional commander Li Zhongwen went out to welcome and entertain him.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Elu came to Bingzhou, where Regional Commander Li Zhongwen went out to welcome and feast him.

sentences.zh: 留三日，城中美婦人多為所掠，仲文不能制。

translations.literal: He stayed three days; many beautiful women in the city were seized by his men, and Zhongwen could not restrain them.
translations.idiomatic: He remained three days, during which his men abducted many of the city's women; Li Zhongwen was powerless to stop them.

sentences.zh: 俄而，處羅卒，義成公主以其子奧射設醜弱，廢不立之，遂立處羅之弟咄苾，是為頡利可汗。

translations.literal: Soon Elu died. Princess Yicheng, because her son Aoshe Shad was ugly and weak, set him aside and did not enthrone him; she then installed Elu's younger brother Tujie, who became Jieli Khan.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Elu died. Princess Yicheng refused to enthrone her son Aoshe Shad as weak and unfit, and instead raised Elu's brother Tujie as Jieli Khan.

sentences.zh: 頡利可汗者，啟民可汗第三子也。

translations.literal: Jieli Khan was the third son of Qimin Khan.
translations.idiomatic: Jieli Khan was Qimin Khan's third son.

sentences.zh: 初為莫賀咄設，牙直五原之北。

translations.literal: He had first been Moheduo Shad, his headquarters directly north of Wuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He had earlier held the title Moheduo Shad, with his camp just north of Wuyuan.

sentences.zh: 高祖入長安，薛舉猶據隴右，遣其將宗羅攻陷平涼郡，北與頡利連結。

translations.literal: When Gaozu entered Chang'an, Xue Ju still held Longyou and sent his general Zong Luo to capture Pingliang Commandery, linking with Jieli in the north.
translations.idiomatic: After Gaozu entered Chang'an, Xue Ju still held the Longyou region and sent Zong Luo to take Pingliang, whereupon he allied with Jieli to the north.

sentences.zh: 高祖患之，遣光祿卿宇文歆賫金帛以賂頡利。

translations.literal: Gaozu was troubled by this and sent Director of the Imperial Household Yuwen Xin with gold and silks to bribe Jieli.
translations.idiomatic: Alarmed, Gaozu sent Yuwen Xin, director of the imperial household, with gold and silks to win Jieli over.

sentences.zh: 歆說之，令絕交於薛舉。

translations.literal: Xin persuaded him to break relations with Xue Ju.
translations.idiomatic: Xin persuaded Jieli to break with Xue Ju.

sentences.zh: 初，隋五原太守張長遜，因亂以其所部五原城隸於突厥。

translations.literal: Earlier, Sui's prefect of Wuyuan, Zhang Changsun, because of the turmoil had submitted his district and Wuyuan city to the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Zhang Changsun, Sui prefect of Wuyuan, had in the chaos placed his command and Wuyuan city under Turkish rule.

sentences.zh: 歆又說頡利遣長遜入朝，以五原地歸於我。

translations.literal: Xin also persuaded Jieli to send Changsun to court and return the territory of Wuyuan to us.
translations.idiomatic: Xin further persuaded Jieli to send Zhang Changsun to court and restore Wuyuan to Tang.

sentences.zh: 頡利並從之，因發突厥兵及長遜之眾，並會於太宗軍所。

translations.literal: Jieli agreed to both; he then sent Turkish troops and Changsun's forces, all joining the Prince of Qin's army.
translations.idiomatic: Jieli agreed to both proposals and dispatched Turkish troops together with Zhang's men to join the prince of Qin's camp.

sentences.zh: 武德三年，頡利又納義城公主為妻，以始畢之子什缽苾為突利可汗，遣使入朝，告處羅死。

translations.literal: In the third year of Wude, Jieli again took Princess Yicheng as wife, installed Shiboni, son of Shibi, as Tuli Khan, and sent envoys to court to announce Elu's death.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude 3, Jieli again married Princess Yicheng, made Shiboni, Shibi's son, Tuli Khan, and sent envoys to announce Elu's death.

sentences.zh: 高祖為之罷朝一日，詔百官就館吊其使。

translations.literal: Gaozu suspended court for one day on his account and ordered the officials to call at the lodge to condole with his envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu closed court for a day of mourning and ordered officials to offer condolences to the envoys at their lodge.

sentences.zh: 頡利初嗣立，承父兄之資，兵馬強盛。

translations.literal: When Jieli first succeeded, he inherited the resources of his father and elder brothers; his troops and horses were powerful.
translations.idiomatic: On first taking the throne, Jieli inherited the strength his father and brothers had built up, and his armies were formidable.

sentences.zh: 有憑陵中國之志。

translations.literal: He harbored the ambition to dominate China.
translations.idiomatic: He aimed to dominate the Chinese realm.

sentences.zh: 高祖以中原初定，不遑外略，每優容之，賜與不可勝計。

translations.literal: Gaozu, because the central plains had only just been pacified and he had no leisure for external campaigns, always indulged him; gifts were beyond reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: With the heartland only newly pacified, Gaozu had no margin for foreign war and indulged him repeatedly, lavishing gifts beyond count.

sentences.zh: 頡利言辭悖傲，求請無厭。

translations.literal: Jieli's words were insolent and defiant; his demands were insatiable.
translations.idiomatic: Jieli spoke with insolent defiance and never ceased demanding more.

sentences.zh: 四年四月，頡利自率萬餘騎，與馬邑賊苑君璋將兵六千人共攻雁門。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fourth year, Jieli personally led more than ten thousand horsemen; with the Mayi rebel Yuan Junzhang commanding six thousand troops, they jointly attacked Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Wude 4, Jieli led more than ten thousand cavalry himself, and together with the Mayi rebel Yuan Junzhang's six thousand men attacked Yanmen.

sentences.zh: 定襄王李大恩擊走之。

translations.literal: Prince of Dingxiang Li Da'en struck and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Dingxiang Li Da'en routed them.

sentences.zh: 先是漢陽公蘇瑰、太常卿鄭元璹、左驍衛大將軍長孫順德等各使於突厥，頡利並拘之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Duke of Hanyang Su Gui, Minister of Ceremonies Zheng Yuanshu, and Left Yao-wei General Changsun Shunde and others had been envoys to the Turks; Jieli had detained them all.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Su Gui, duke of Hanyang; Zheng Yuanshu, minister of ceremonies; and Changsun Shunde, general of the Left Yao-wei Guard, among others, had been sent as envoys to the Turks, and Jieli had held them all.

sentences.zh: 我亦留其使，前後數輩。

translations.literal: We too retained their envoys, several missions in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Tang, in turn, had detained several successive Turkish missions.

sentences.zh: 至是為大恩所挫，於是乃懼，仍放順德還，更請和好。

translations.literal: Now, having been checked by Da'en, he grew afraid, released Shunde to return, and again sought peace.
translations.idiomatic: Checked by Li Da'en's victory, Jieli took fright, released Changsun Shunde, and renewed his plea for peace.

sentences.zh: 獻魚膠數十斤，欲充二國同於此膠。

translations.literal: He presented several tens of jin of fish glue, wishing the two states to be as one in this glue.
translations.idiomatic: He sent several tens of pounds of fish glue, proposing that the two realms be bonded as inseparably as the adhesive.

sentences.zh: 高祖嘉之，放其使者特勒熱寒、阿史德等還蕃，賜以金帛。

translations.literal: Gaozu commended this, released his envoys the tegin Remen and Ashide and others to their lands, and bestowed gold and silks.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu approved and sent back the tegin Remen, Ashide, and the other envoys with gifts of gold and silk.

sentences.zh: 五年春，李大恩奏言突厥饑荒，馬邑可圖。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fifth year, Li Da'en memorialized that the Turks were suffering famine and Mayi could be taken.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Wude 5, Li Da'en reported that famine had weakened the Turks and that Mayi could be seized.

sentences.zh: 詔大恩與殿內少監獨孤晟帥師討苑君璋，期以二月會於馬邑。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Da'en and Palace Attendant Director Dugu Sheng to lead troops against Yuan Junzhang, with a rendezvous at Mayi in the second month.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Li Da'en and Dugu Sheng, director of palace attendants, to campaign against Yuan Junzhang, with a joint rendezvous at Mayi in the second month.

sentences.zh: 晟後期不至，大恩不能獨進，頓兵新城以待之。

translations.literal: Sheng arrived late and did not come; Da'en could not advance alone and halted his army at Xincheng to await him.
translations.idiomatic: Dugu Sheng failed to arrive on time, so Li Da'en could not advance alone and encamped at Xincheng to wait.

sentences.zh: 頡利遣數萬騎與劉黑闥合軍，進圍大恩。

translations.literal: Jieli sent tens of thousands of horsemen to join Liu Heita's army and advanced to besiege Da'en.
translations.idiomatic: Jieli sent tens of thousands of cavalry to unite with Liu Heita and surround Li Da'en.

sentences.zh: 王師敗績，大恩歿於陣，死者數千人。

translations.literal: The imperial army was defeated; Da'en perished in battle, and several thousand died.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial force was crushed; Li Da'en fell in battle and several thousand men were killed.

sentences.zh: 六月，劉黑闥又引突厥萬餘騎入抄河北。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Liu Heita again led more than ten thousand Turkish horsemen in raids into Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Liu Heita again brought more than ten thousand Turkish cavalry on raids into Hebei.

sentences.zh: 頡利復自率五萬騎南侵，至於汾州。

translations.literal: Jieli again personally led fifty thousand horsemen south in invasion, reaching Fen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Jieli himself led fifty thousand cavalry south as far as Fenzhou.

sentences.zh: 又遣數千騎西入靈、原等州，詔隱太子出豳州道，太宗出蒲州道以討之。

translations.literal: He also sent several thousand horsemen west into Ling, Yuan, and other prefectures; an edict ordered the Hidden Crown Prince to march by the Binzhou route and the Prince of Qin by the Puzhou route to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent several thousand horsemen west into Ling and Yuan prefectures. The court ordered the crown prince out by the Binzhou road and the prince of Qin by the Puzhou road to counter them.

sentences.zh: 時頡利攻圍并州，又分兵入汾、潞等州，掠男女五千餘口，聞太宗兵至蒲州，乃引兵出塞。

translations.literal: At that time Jieli was besieging Bing Prefecture and also divided his forces to enter Fen, Lu, and other prefectures, seizing more than five thousand men and women; on hearing that the Prince of Qin's army had reached Puzhou, he withdrew beyond the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Jieli was then besieging Bingzhou while detachments raided Fen, Lu, and neighboring prefectures, carrying off more than five thousand people. When he learned that the prince of Qin had reached Puzhou, he withdrew beyond the border.

sentences.zh: 七年八月，頡利、突利二可汗舉國入寇，道自原州，連營南上。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the seventh year, the two khans Jieli and Tuli led the whole nation in invasion, marching from Yuan Prefecture with encampments linked as they moved south.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Wude 7, Jieli and Tuli Khan led the whole nation in invasion, advancing south from Yuanzhou in a chain of camps.

sentences.zh: 太宗受詔北討，齊王元吉隸焉。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qin received orders for a northern campaign; Prince of Qi Yuanji was subordinate to him.
translations.idiomatic: The prince of Qin took command of the northern campaign with Prince of Qi Li Yuanji under him.

sentences.zh: 初，關中霖雨，糧運阻絕，太宗頗患之，諸將憂見於色，頓兵於豳州。

translations.literal: At first, in Guanzhong there was incessant rain; grain transport was cut off; the Prince of Qin was much troubled, and the generals' worry showed on their faces as they halted the army at Bin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy rains in Guanzhong had cut supply lines, and the prince of Qin was deeply worried; dismay showed on his generals' faces as the army halted at Binzhou.

sentences.zh: 頡利、突利率萬餘騎奄至城西，乘高而陣，將士大駭。

translations.literal: Jieli and Tuli led more than ten thousand horsemen in a sudden arrival west of the city, forming battle lines on the heights; officers and men were greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Jieli and Tuli suddenly appeared west of the city with more than ten thousand horsemen and drew up on the high ground, throwing the Tang army into alarm.

sentences.zh: 太宗乃親率百騎馳詣虜陣，告之曰：「國家與可汗誓不相負，何為背約深入吾地？

translations.literal: The Prince of Qin then personally led a hundred horsemen in a gallop to the barbarian lines and told them: "The state and the khan swore not to betray each other—why do you break the pact and penetrate deep into our land?
translations.idiomatic: The prince of Qin then rode at the head of a hundred men straight to the Turkish lines and called out: "Our realms swore not to betray one another—why have you broken the treaty and marched deep into our territory?

sentences.zh: 我秦王也，故來一決。

translations.literal: I am the Prince of Qin; I have come for a single decision.
translations.idiomatic: I am the Prince of Qin, and I have come to settle this between us.

sentences.zh: 可汗若自來，我當與可汗兩人獨戰；

translations.literal: If the khan comes in person, I shall fight the khan alone, just the two of us;
translations.idiomatic: If the khan will face me himself, let the two of us fight alone;

sentences.zh: 若欲兵馬總來，我唯百騎相禦耳。」

translations.literal: if you wish all your troops to come, I have only these hundred horsemen to meet them."
translations.idiomatic: if you mean to bring all your forces, these hundred horsemen are all I need to meet them."

sentences.zh: 頡利弗之測，笑而不對。

translations.literal: Jieli could not fathom him; he smiled and made no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Jieli could not read him; he only smiled and said nothing.

sentences.zh: 太宗又前，令騎告突利曰：「爾往與我盟，急難相救；

translations.literal: The Prince of Qin advanced again and had a rider tell Tuli: "You once swore alliance with me, to aid each other in urgent need;
translations.idiomatic: The prince advanced again and sent a rider to tell Tuli: "You once swore alliance with me to help in distress;

sentences.zh: 爾今將兵來，何無香火之情也？

translations.literal: now you bring troops—where is the bond of sworn brotherhood?
translations.idiomatic: yet now you march against me—where is the bond of sworn brotherhood?

sentences.zh: 亦宜早出，一決勝負。」

translations.literal: You too should come out early for a single contest of victory and defeat."
translations.idiomatic: Come out yourself and let us settle it."

sentences.zh: 突利亦不對。

translations.literal: Tuli also made no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Tuli likewise held his tongue.

sentences.zh: 太宗前，將渡溝水，頡利見太宗輕出，又聞香火之言，乃陰猜突利。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qin advanced and was about to cross the gully; Jieli, seeing how lightly the prince had come forth and hearing the words about sworn brotherhood, secretly suspected Tuli.
translations.idiomatic: As the prince moved forward to cross the ditch, Jieli, struck by his bold appearance and by the talk of sworn brotherhood, began to suspect Tuli in secret.

sentences.zh: 因遣使曰：「王不須渡，我無惡意，更欲共王自斷當耳。」

translations.literal: He therefore sent a messenger saying: "Prince, you need not cross; I have no ill intent—I only wish to settle matters with the prince in person."
translations.idiomatic: He sent a messenger saying: "Prince, do not cross—I mean no harm; I only wish to settle this with you face to face."

sentences.zh: 於是稍引卻，各斂軍而退。

translations.literal: Thereupon he gradually drew back, and each side gathered its troops and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Both sides then drew back and withdrew their forces.

sentences.zh: 太過因縱反間於突利，突利悅而歸心焉，遂不欲戰。

translations.literal: The emperor then set discord between them toward Tuli; Tuli was pleased and gave his heart to the Tang, and thus did not wish to fight.
translations.idiomatic: The prince then sowed distrust between the khans; Tuli was won over and lost all will to fight.

sentences.zh: 其叔侄內離，頡利欲戰不可，因遣突利及夾畢特勒阿史那思摩奉見請和，許之。

translations.literal: Uncle and nephew were divided within; Jieli wished to fight but could not, and therefore sent Tuli and the Jabiy tegin Ashina Simo to present themselves and seek peace; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: With uncle and nephew estranged, Jieli could not bring himself to fight and sent Tuli and the Jabiy tegin Ashina Simo to sue for peace, which was granted.

sentences.zh: 突利因自托於太宗，願結為兄弟。

translations.literal: Tuli thereupon placed himself under the prince's protection and wished to become sworn brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Tuli placed himself under the prince's protection and asked to become sworn brothers.

sentences.zh: 思摩初奉見，高祖引升禦榻，頓顙固辭。

translations.literal: When Simo first had audience, Gaozu drew him up onto the imperial couch; he knocked his head on the ground and firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: At Simo's first audience Gaozu drew him onto the imperial couch; he kowtowed and firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 高祖謂曰：「頡利誠心遣特勒朝拜，今見特勒，如見頡利。」

translations.literal: Gaozu said to him: "Jieli sent the tegin in sincere homage; now that I see the tegin, it is as if I see Jieli."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said: "Jieli sent you in good faith; to see the tegin is to see Jieli himself."

sentences.zh: 固引之，乃就坐，尋封思摩為和順王。

translations.literal: He insisted on drawing him up, and Simo then took his seat; soon Simo was enfeoffed as Prince of Heshun.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu insisted, and Simo took his seat; soon afterward he was enfeoffed as prince of Heshun.

sentences.zh: 八年七月，頡利集兵十餘萬，大掠朔州，又襲將軍張瑾於太原。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the eighth year, Jieli gathered more than a hundred thousand troops, raided Shuo Prefecture on a great scale, and also attacked General Zhang Jin at Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Wude 8, Jieli massed more than a hundred thousand men, ravaged Shuo Prefecture, and struck General Zhang Jin at Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 瑾全軍並沒，脫身奔於李靖。

translations.literal: Jin's entire army was destroyed; he escaped in person and fled to Li Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jin's whole force was wiped out; he alone escaped to Li Jing.

sentences.zh: 出師拒戰，頡利不得進，屯於并州。

translations.literal: When troops marched out to resist, Jieli could not advance and encamped at Bing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial troops marched out to block him; unable to advance, Jieli encamped at Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 太宗帥師討之，次蒲州；

translations.literal: The Prince of Qin led troops against him and halted at Puzhou;
translations.idiomatic: The prince of Qin marched against him and halted at Puzhou;

sentences.zh: 頡利引兵而去，太宗旋師。

translations.literal: Jieli withdrew his troops and left; the prince turned his army back.
translations.idiomatic: Jieli withdrew, and the prince marched home.

sentences.zh: 九年七月，頡利自率十餘萬騎進寇武功，京師戒嚴。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the ninth year, Jieli personally led more than a hundred thousand horsemen in invasion against Wugong; the capital was placed under martial alert.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Wude 9, Jieli led more than a hundred thousand cavalry against Wugong, and the capital went on alert.

sentences.zh: 己卯，進寇高陵，行軍總管左武候大將軍尉遲敬德與之戰於涇陽，大破之，獲俟斤阿史德烏沒啜，斬首千餘級。

translations.literal: On the day jimao he advanced against Gaoling; campaigning commander and General of the Left Martial Guard Yuchi Jingde fought him at Jingyang, routed him greatly, captured the houjin Ashide Wumochuo, and took more than a thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao day he pressed on to Gaoling. Yuchi Jingde, campaigning commander and general of the Left Martial Guard, met him at Jingyang and won a great victory, capturing the houjin Ashide Wumochuo and more than a thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 癸未，頡利遣其腹心執失思力入朝為覘，自張形勢云：「二可汗總兵百萬，今已至矣。」

translations.literal: On the day guwei Jieli sent his trusted follower Zhishi Sili to court as a spy; he exaggerated their strength, saying: "The two khans command a million troops—they have already arrived."
translations.idiomatic: On guwei day Jieli sent his confidant Zhishi Sili to court on reconnaissance, boasting: "The two khans command a million men—they are already here."

sentences.zh: 太宗謂之曰：「我與突厥面自和親，汝則背之，我實無愧。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qin said to him: "I personally made peace with the Turks face to face, while you betray it—I truly have no cause for shame.
translations.idiomatic: The prince of Qin told him: "I made peace with the Turks in person, and you broke it—I have nothing to be ashamed of.

sentences.zh: 又義軍入京之初，爾父子並親從，我賜汝玉帛，前後極多，何故輒將兵入我畿縣？

translations.literal: Moreover, when the righteous army first entered the capital, your father and son both followed in person; I bestowed jade and silks on you, a great amount before and after—why do you rashly lead troops into my metropolitan districts?
translations.idiomatic: When our army first entered the capital, your father and you both followed in person, and I lavished jade and silk on you again and again—why do you now march troops into the capital districts?

sentences.zh: 爾雖突厥，亦須頗有人心，何故全忘大恩，自誇強盛？

translations.literal: Though you are Turks, you must still have some human feeling—why do you utterly forget great kindness and boast of your strength?
translations.idiomatic: Even a Turk ought to have some sense of gratitude—why forget our kindness and boast of your power?

sentences.zh: 我當先戮爾矣！」

translations.literal: I ought to execute you first!"
translations.idiomatic: I ought to execute you on the spot!"

sentences.zh: 思力懼而請命，太宗不許，縶之於門下省。

translations.literal: Sili was afraid and begged for his life; the prince would not consent and had him bound in the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Sili pleaded for his life in terror; the prince refused and had him imprisoned in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 太宗與侍中高士廉、中書令房玄齡、將軍周範馳六騎幸渭水之上，與頡利隔津而語，責以負約。

translations.literal: The prince, with Attendant-in-ordinary Gao Shilian, Chief Secretariat Director Fang Xuanling, and General Zhou Fan, galloped on six horses to the Wei River, spoke with Jieli across the ford, and rebuked him for breaking the pact.
translations.idiomatic: With Gao Shilian, Fang Xuanling, and General Zhou Fan, the prince rode six horses to the Wei River, confronted Jieli across the ford, and rebuked him for breaking the treaty.

sentences.zh: 其酋帥大驚，皆下馬羅拜。

translations.literal: Their chieftains were greatly alarmed; all dismounted and bowed in ranks.
translations.idiomatic: The Turkish chiefs were stunned; they all dismounted and bowed in ranks.

sentences.zh: 俄而，眾軍繼至，頡利見軍容大盛，又知思力就拘，由是大懼。

translations.literal: Soon the main armies arrived in succession; Jieli saw how grand the military array was and also learned that Sili had been seized—thereupon he was greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the main armies came up; seeing their strength and learning that Sili was a prisoner, Jieli was thoroughly frightened.

sentences.zh: 太宗獨與頡利臨水交言，麾諸軍卻而陣焉。

translations.literal: Taizong alone with Jieli exchanged words facing the water, and waved the armies to fall back and array in formation.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong went alone to parley with Jieli across the water, then ordered the armies to withdraw and form battle lines.

sentences.zh: 蕭瑀以輕敵固諫於馬前，上曰：「吾已籌之，非卿所知也。

translations.literal: Xiao Yu urgently remonstrated before the horse about treating the enemy lightly. The Emperor said: "I have already calculated this—it is not something you would understand.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yu, fearing they underestimated the foe, pleaded with the Emperor from horseback. Taizong replied, "I have already weighed this matter. It lies beyond what you can see.

sentences.zh: 突厥所以掃其境內，直入渭濱，應是聞我國家初有內難，朕又新登九五，將謂不敢拒之。

translations.literal: The reason the Turks swept their territory clean and came straight to the banks of the Wei should be that they heard our state had just suffered internal troubles, and that I had newly ascended the throne—they would suppose we would not dare resist.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks had swept through their own lands and marched straight to the Wei River because they had heard that the empire was newly torn by civil strife and that I had only just taken the throne. They assumed we would not dare stand against them.

sentences.zh: 朕若閉門，虜必大掠，強弱之勢，在今一舉。

translations.literal: If I shut the gates, the barbarians would surely plunder on a great scale; the balance of strength and weakness hangs on this one move.
translations.idiomatic: Had I barred the gates, the invaders would have looted without restraint. The question of who was strong and who was weak would have been settled in a single stroke.

sentences.zh: 朕故獨出，以示輕之；

translations.literal: Therefore I came out alone, to show that I held them lightly;
translations.idiomatic: So I went out alone—to show that I did not fear them;

sentences.zh: 又耀軍容，使知必戰。

translations.literal: and also displayed our military bearing, to let them know we would surely fight.
translations.idiomatic: and at the same time displayed the full might of our armies, so they would know we were ready to fight.

sentences.zh: 事出不意，乖其本圖，虜入既深，理當自懼。

translations.literal: The affair arose against their expectation, contrary to their original plan; the barbarians having entered so deep, it was only right they should fear.
translations.idiomatic: Events took them by surprise and overturned their plans. Having penetrated so far, they could not but begin to fear.

sentences.zh: 與戰則必克，與和則必固，制服匈奴，自茲始矣！」

translations.literal: If we fought we would surely prevail; if we made peace we would surely secure it—subduing the Xiongnu begins from this!"
translations.idiomatic: Fight, and we would surely win; treat, and the peace would surely hold. The subjugation of the northern horsemen begins here!"

sentences.zh: 是日，頡利請和，詔許焉。

translations.literal: That day, Jieli requested peace, and an edict granted it.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Jieli sued for peace, and the Emperor granted it.

sentences.zh: 車駕即日還宮。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage returned to the palace the same day.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor returned to the palace that very day.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，又幸城西，刑白馬與頡利同盟於便橋之上，頡利引兵而退。

translations.literal: On yiyou day, he again visited the west of the city, sacrificed a white horse, and formed an alliance with Jieli atop Bianqiao Bridge; Jieli led his troops and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: On the day yiyou, Taizong again went to the western suburbs, sacrificed a white horse, and swore alliance with Jieli on Bianqiao Bridge. Jieli then led his army away.

sentences.zh: 蕭瑀進曰：「初，頡利之未和也，謀臣猛將多請戰，而陛下不納，臣以為疑。

translations.literal: Xiao Yu advanced and said: "At first, before Jieli had made peace, strategists and fierce generals repeatedly asked to fight, but Your Majesty did not accept—I was perplexed.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yu stepped forward and said, "When Jieli had not yet agreed to peace, your counselors and generals urged battle again and again, yet Your Majesty refused. I confess I was baffled.

sentences.zh: 既而虜自退，其策安在？」

translations.literal: Yet afterward the barbarians withdrew on their own—where lay Your Majesty's strategy?"
translations.idiomatic: Then the enemy withdrew of their own accord. Where, I wondered, lay Your Majesty's design?

sentences.zh: 上曰：「我觀突厥之兵，雖眾而不整，君臣之計，唯財利是視。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "I observed the Turk forces—though numerous, they were not disciplined; lord and ministers in their plans looked only to profit.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said, "I saw that though the Turk army was large, it was not orderly. Khan and chiefs alike cared for nothing but gain.

sentences.zh: 可汗獨在水西，酋帥皆來謁我，我因而襲擊其眾，勢同拉朽。

translations.literal: The khan alone was west of the water; the chiefs and commanders all came to pay court to me—I could thus strike their mass, the momentum like pulling down rotten wood.
translations.idiomatic: The khan stood alone on the west bank while his chieftains came forward to pay me homage. Had I struck then, their host would have collapsed like rotten timber.

sentences.zh: 然我已令無忌、李靖設伏於幽州以待之，虜若奔還，伏兵邀其前，大軍躡其後，覆之如反掌矣！

translations.literal: Yet I had already ordered Wuji and Li Jing to set ambushes at Youzhou to await them; if the barbarians fled back, the ambush would intercept their front, the main army would follow their rear, and overturning them would be like turning the hand!
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, I had already ordered Changsun Wuji and Li Jing to lay ambushes in Youzhou. If the Turks fled homeward, the hidden troops would block their path while our main force fell upon them from behind. Their destruction would have been as easy as turning one's palm.

sentences.zh: 我所以不戰者，即位日淺，為國之道，安靜為務，一與虜戰，必有死傷；

translations.literal: The reason I did not fight: my accession had been recent; in governing a state, tranquility is the priority—a single battle with the barbarians would surely bring deaths and wounds;
translations.idiomatic: I chose not to fight because I had only lately taken the throne. A ruler's first duty is peace. One battle with the barbarians would have meant many dead and wounded;

sentences.zh: 又匈虜一敗，或當懼而修德，結怨於我，為患不細。

translations.literal: furthermore, if the Hun barbarians suffered one defeat, they might in fear cultivate virtue and harbor resentment against us—the harm would not be slight.
translations.idiomatic: and if the northern tribes suffered defeat, they might in fear mend their ways yet nurse a lasting grudge against us. The harm would not be small.

sentences.zh: 我今卷甲韜戈，陷以玉帛，頑虜驕恣，必自此始，破亡之漸，其在茲乎！

translations.literal: Now I sheathe armor and hide blades, entrap them with jade and silk—the stubborn barbarians' arrogance and indulgence will surely begin from this; the gradual progress toward destruction—is it not here!
translations.idiomatic: Now I sheathe our swords and lay aside our armor, luring them with gifts of jade and silk. From this their pride and excess will surely grow—and with them the first steps toward ruin.

sentences.zh: 將欲取之，必固與之，此之謂也！」

translations.literal: To take something, one must first firmly give it—this is what is meant!"
translations.idiomatic: To take what one desires, one must first give generously. That is the meaning of my policy!

sentences.zh: 九月，頡利獻馬三千匹，羊萬口，上不受；

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Jieli presented three thousand horses and ten thousand sheep; the Emperor did not accept them;
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Jieli offered three thousand horses and ten thousand sheep. Taizong refused the gift;

sentences.zh: 詔頡利所掠中國戶口者悉令歸之。

translations.literal: an edict ordered all Chinese households Jieli had seized to be returned.
translations.idiomatic: and issued an edict that all Chinese subjects Jieli had carried off were to be sent home.

sentences.zh: 貞觀元年，陰山已北薛延陀、回紇、拔也古等部皆相率背叛，擊走其欲谷設。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenguan, north of Yinshan the Xueyantuo, Huihe, Bayegu and other tribes all in succession rebelled, routing his yehu she.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Zhenguan reign, the Xueyantuo, Huihe, Bayegu, and other tribes north of Yinshan rose in succession against Jieli and drove off his yehu she.

sentences.zh: 頡利遣突利討之，師又敗績，輕騎奔還。

translations.literal: Jieli sent Tuli to suppress them; the army again suffered defeat, and light cavalry fled back.
translations.idiomatic: Jieli dispatched Tuli to punish them, but the campaign failed again and only a few horsemen escaped back.

sentences.zh: 頡利怒，拘之十餘日；

translations.literal: Jieli was angry and detained him for more than ten days;
translations.idiomatic: Jieli flew into a rage and held him prisoner for more than ten days;

sentences.zh: 突利由是怨望，內欲背之。

translations.literal: Tuli thereby harbored resentment and inwardly wished to renounce him.
translations.idiomatic: whereupon Tuli nursed a grievance and inwardly resolved to break with him.

sentences.zh: 其國大雪，平地數尺，羊馬皆死，人大饑，乃懼我師出乘其弊。

translations.literal: Their state had heavy snow—several feet on level ground; sheep and horses all died, and the people suffered great famine; they then feared our armies would emerge to take advantage of their weakness.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy snow fell across the Turk lands until the open country lay several feet deep. Sheep and horses perished, the people starved, and Jieli grew afraid that Tang armies would march out to exploit his weakness.

sentences.zh: 引兵入朔州，揚言會獵，實設備焉。

translations.literal: He led troops into Shuozhou, proclaiming a hunting gathering, but in fact making preparations.
translations.idiomatic: He led troops into Shuozhou, claiming he came to hunt, but in truth was making ready for war.

sentences.zh: 侍臣咸曰：「夷狄無信，先自猜疑，盟後將兵，忽踐疆境。

translations.literal: The attendant ministers all said: "The barbarians are faithless—they had suspicions from the start; after the alliance they led troops and suddenly trampled our borders.
translations.idiomatic: The courtiers all said, "These barbarians cannot be trusted. They were suspicious from the first, and now, scarcely after our treaty, they have brought troops across our border.

sentences.zh: 可乘其便，數以背約，因而討之。」

translations.literal: We can seize this opportunity, repeatedly cite their breach of covenant, and thereby attack them.
translations.idiomatic: We should seize the moment, hold their broken oath against them, and strike while we may.

sentences.zh: 太宗曰：「匹夫一言，尚須存信，何況天下主乎！

translations.literal: Taizong said: "A common man's word must still be kept in faith—how much more the ruler of all under Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said, "If even a common man must keep his word, how much more must the Son of Heaven!

sentences.zh: 豈有親與之和，利其災禍而乘危迫險以滅之耶？

translations.literal: How could one personally make peace with them, then profit from their calamity and seize upon danger and peril to destroy them?
translations.idiomatic: How could I make peace with them in person, then turn their disaster to my advantage and destroy them in their hour of peril?

sentences.zh: 諸公為可，朕不為也。

translations.literal: You gentlemen may deem it acceptable—I will not do it.
translations.idiomatic: You may think it permissible. I do not.

sentences.zh: 縱突厥部落叛盡，六畜皆死，朕終示以信，不妄討之；

translations.literal: Even if Turk tribes rebelled to the last and all livestock died, I would ultimately show them faith and not attack recklessly;
translations.idiomatic: Even if every Turk tribe deserted Jieli and every head of livestock perished, I would still honor my word and not strike without cause;

sentences.zh: 待其無禮，方擒取耳。」

translations.literal: wait until they are without propriety, then seize them."
translations.idiomatic: I will wait until they give me just cause, and only then take them."

sentences.zh: 二年，突利遣使奏言與頡利有隙，奏請擊之，詔秦武通以并州兵馬隨便應接。

translations.literal: In the second year, Tuli sent envoys memorializing that he had a rift with Jieli and requesting to attack him; an edict ordered Qin Wutong with Bingzhou troops and horses to respond as circumstances permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year Tuli sent envoys to report his breach with Jieli and to ask permission to attack him. The Emperor ordered Qin Wutong to move the Bingzhou forces as needed to support him.

sentences.zh: 三年，薛延陀自稱可汗於漠北，遣使來貢方物。

translations.literal: In the third year, Xueyantuo declared himself khan in the northern deserts and sent envoys to present tribute goods.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Xueyantuo proclaimed himself khan in the northern steppe and sent tribute to the court.

sentences.zh: 頡利始稱臣，尚公主，請修婿禮。

translations.literal: Jieli for the first time declared himself vassal, was given a princess in marriage, and requested to observe son-in-law rites.
translations.idiomatic: Jieli submitted as a vassal for the first time, received an imperial princess in marriage, and asked to perform the rites due a son-in-law of the throne.

sentences.zh: 頡利每委任諸胡，疏遠族類，胡人貪冒，性多翻覆，以故法令滋彰，兵革歲動，國人患之，諸部攜貳。

translations.literal: Jieli repeatedly entrusted affairs to various Hu peoples and kept distant his own kin; the Hu were greedy and presumptuous, by nature much given to treachery; thus laws and decrees multiplied, arms were taken up year after year, the people of the state suffered, and the tribes wavered in loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Jieli constantly favored foreign Hu advisers over his own tribesmen. The Hu were greedy and fickle by nature, so edicts multiplied, war never ceased, the people groaned under the burden, and the tribes grew restless.

sentences.zh: 頻年大雪，六畜多死，國中大餒，頡利用度不給，復重斂諸部，由是下不堪命，內外多叛之。

translations.literal: Snow fell heavily year after year; much livestock died; the state suffered great famine; Jieli's expenditures could not be met, and he again heavily taxed the tribes—wherefore the lower orders could not bear the burden, and many within and without rebelled against him.
translations.idiomatic: Year after year snow buried the land and livestock died in great numbers. Famine spread through the khanate. Unable to meet his expenses, Jieli taxed the tribes ever more harshly until they could endure no more and rebellion broke out within and without.

sentences.zh: 上以其請和，後復援梁師都，詔兵部尚書李靖、代州都督張公謹出定襄道。

translations.literal: The Emperor because he had sought peace yet afterward again aided Liang Shidu, issued an edict for Minister of War Li Jing and Daizhou Military Governor Zhang Gongjin to advance by the Dingxiang route.
translations.idiomatic: Because Jieli had sued for peace and then again supported Liang Shidu, the Emperor ordered Minister of War Li Jing and Daizhou Military Governor Zhang Gongjin to march by the Dingxiang route.

sentences.zh: 并州都督李勣、右武衛將軍丘行恭出通漢道，左武衛大將軍柴紹出金河道，衛孝節出恆安道，薛萬徹出暢武道，並受靖節度以討之。

translations.literal: Bingzhou Military Governor Li Ji, Right Martial Guard General Qiu Xinggong by the Tonghan route, Left Martial Guard Grand General Chai Shao by the Jinhe route, Wei Xiaojie by the Heng'an route, Xue Wanche by the Changwu route—all under Li Jing's command to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Bingzhou Military Governor Li Ji was to advance by the Tonghan route; Right Martial Guard General Qiu Xinggong, Left Martial Guard Grand General Chai Shao by the Jinhe route; Wei Xiaojie by the Heng'an route; and Xue Wanche by the Changwu route—all under Li Jing's overall command to destroy Jieli.

sentences.zh: 十二月，突利可汗及郁射設、廕奈特勒等，並帥所部來奔。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Tuli Khan and Yushe She, Yinnai Tele and others all led their followers to come and defect.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Tuli Khan, together with Yushe She, Yinnai Tele, and others, led their tribes in flight to Tang territory.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，李靖進屯惡陽嶺，夜襲定襄，頡利驚擾，因徙牙於磧口。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year, Li Jing advanced and encamped at Eyang Ridge, raided Dingxiang by night; Jieli was alarmed and thrown into disorder, and moved his court to Qikou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year Li Jing encamped at Eyang Ridge and struck Dingxiang by night. Jieli, thrown into panic, moved his royal camp to Qikou.

sentences.zh: 胡酋康蘇密等遂以隋蕭後及楊政道來降。

translations.literal: The Hu chieftain Kang Sumi and others then brought Empress Xiao of Sui and Yang Zhengdao to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The Hu chieftain Kang Sumi and others then surrendered, bringing with them Empress Xiao of Sui and Yang Zhengdao.

sentences.zh: 二月，頡利計窘，竄於鐵山，兵尚數萬，使執失思力入朝謝罪，請舉國內附。

translations.literal: In the second month, Jieli's plans were exhausted; he fled to Mount Tie with troops still numbering tens of thousands; he sent Zhishi Sili to court to confess guilt and request that the whole state submit.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, his stratagems exhausted, Jieli fled to Mount Tie with an army still tens of thousands strong. He sent Zhishi Sili to the capital to confess his crimes and offer the submission of the entire khanate.

sentences.zh: 太宗遣鴻臚卿唐儉、將軍安修仁持節安撫之，頡利稍自安。

translations.literal: Taizong dispatched Grand Master of Ceremonies Tang Jian and General An Xiuren with credentials to pacify him; Jieli gradually regained calm.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong sent Grand Master of Ceremonies Tang Jian and General An Xiuren with imperial credentials to reassure him, and Jieli slowly regained his composure.

sentences.zh: 靖乘間襲擊，大破之，遂滅其國。

translations.literal: Li Jing seized the interval to strike, routed them thoroughly, and destroyed their state.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jing seized the moment and attacked, crushing the Turks and extinguishing their state.

sentences.zh: 頡利乘千里馬，獨騎奔於從侄沙缽羅部落。

translations.literal: Jieli mounted a thousand-li horse and alone on horseback fled to his younger cousin Shaboluo's tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Jieli fled alone on a swift horse to the camp of his cousin Shaboluo.

sentences.zh: 三月，行軍副總管張寶相率眾奄至沙缽羅營，生擒頡利送於京師。

translations.literal: In the third month, Deputy Campaign Commander Zhang Baoxiang led troops suddenly upon Shaboluo's camp, captured Jieli alive, and sent him to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Deputy Campaign Commander Zhang Baoxiang fell suddenly upon Shaboluo's camp, took Jieli alive, and sent him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 太宗謂曰：「凡有功於我者，必不能忘，有惡於我者，終亦不記。

translations.literal: Taizong said to him: "Whoever has merit toward me—I surely cannot forget; whoever has done evil toward me—I ultimately do not record it either.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said to him, "Those who have served me well I never forget. Those who have wronged me I do not forever hold in memory.

sentences.zh: 論爾之罪狀，誠為不小，但自渭水曾面為盟，從此以來，未有深犯，所以錄此，不相責耳！」

translations.literal: Speaking of your crimes, they are indeed not small; but since we once faced each other in alliance at the Wei River, from then until now you have not deeply transgressed—therefore I note this and do not hold you accountable!"
translations.idiomatic: By the measure of your offenses, your guilt is no small thing. Yet since we once met face to face and swore alliance beside the Wei River, you have not since committed any grave wrong. For that I spare you blame!

sentences.zh: 仍詔還其家口，館於太僕，稟食之。

translations.literal: An edict still ordered his family returned; they were housed at the Minister of Studs and given rations.
translations.idiomatic: An edict restored his family to him. They were lodged with the Court of the Imperial Stud and provided with provisions.

sentences.zh: 頡利郁郁不得志，與其家人或相對悲歌而泣。

translations.literal: Jieli, depressed and unfulfilled, sometimes faced his family in lamenting song and wept.
translations.idiomatic: Despondent and without purpose, Jieli would sometimes sit with his kin, singing mournful songs and weeping together.

sentences.zh: 帝見羸憊，授虢州刺史，以彼土多麞鹿，縱其畋獵，庶不失物性。

translations.literal: The Emperor, seeing him emaciated and exhausted, appointed him Governor of Guo Prefecture—since that land had many roe deer, allowing him to hunt, hoping he would not lose his natural disposition.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing how wasted and weary he had become, the Emperor appointed him governor of Guo Prefecture, where roe deer were plentiful, so that he might hunt freely and not be wholly severed from the life he had known.

sentences.zh: 頡利辭不願往，遂授右衛大將軍，賜以田宅。

translations.literal: Jieli declined and did not wish to go; he was then appointed Grand General of the Right Guard and granted fields and a residence.
translations.idiomatic: Jieli refused the post. He was instead made Grand General of the Right Guard and given lands and a house.

sentences.zh: 五年，太宗謂侍臣曰：「天道福善禍淫，事猶影響。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Taizong said to his attendants: "Heaven's way blesses the good and punishes the licentious—the matter is like shadow and echo.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Taizong told his ministers, "Heaven rewards virtue and punishes wickedness as surely as the body casts a shadow or the voice returns an echo.

sentences.zh: 昔啟民亡國奔隋，文帝不吝粟帛，大興士眾，營衛安置，乃得存立。

translations.literal: Formerly Qimin lost his state and fled to Sui; Emperor Wen did not spare grain and silk, greatly raised troops and people, established camps and guards to settle them, and thus they were preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Qimin Khan lost his realm and fled to Sui. Emperor Wen lavished grain and silk upon him, mustered soldiers and laborers, and established camps to shelter his people, so that the house of Ashina was preserved.

sentences.zh: 既而強盛，當須子子孫孫思念報德。

translations.literal: Once they grew strong, they ought generation after generation to remember and repay that kindness.
translations.idiomatic: When they grew strong again, they should have remembered that debt from generation to generation.

sentences.zh: 才至始畢，即起兵圍煬帝於雁門，及隋國將亂，又恃強深入，遂使昔安立其家國者，身及子孫，並為頡利兄弟之所屠戮。

translations.literal: But as soon as Shibi came, he raised troops and besieged Emperor Yang at Yanmen; when the Sui state was about to fall into disorder, he again relied on strength to penetrate deep—so that those who had once settled his house and state, body and descendants, were all slain by Jieli and his brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Yet no sooner had Shibi Khan come to power than he raised an army and besieged Emperor Yang at Yanmen. When Sui was near collapse he again pressed deep into China with all his strength. In the end, those very Sui emperors who had raised up his house and kin were slaughtered, they and their descendants, by Jieli and his brothers.

sentences.zh: 今頡利破亡，豈非背恩忘義所致也！」

translations.literal: Now Jieli is destroyed—is this not caused by betraying kindness and forgetting righteousness!"
translations.idiomatic: Now Jieli lies ruined. Was that not the wages of ingratitude and faithlessness?"

sentences.zh: 八年卒，詔其國人葬之，從其俗禮，焚屍於灞水之東，贈歸義王，謚曰荒。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he died; an edict ordered men of his state to bury him according to their custom—his corpse was burned east of the Ba River; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Returning Righteousness, with temple name Huang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he died. By edict his countrymen buried him according to Turk custom, burning his body east of the Ba River. He was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Returning Righteousness, with the posthumous title Reckless.

sentences.zh: 其舊臣胡祿達官吐谷渾邪自刎以殉。

translations.literal: His old minister, the Hubo official Tuyuhun Xie, slit his own throat to follow him in death.
translations.idiomatic: His former minister, the Hubo official Tuyuhun Xie, cut his own throat to die in his master's service.

sentences.zh: 渾邪者，頡利之母婆施氏之媵臣也。

translations.literal: Hunxie had been the concubine-attendant of Jieli's mother, Lady Boshi.
translations.idiomatic: Hunxie had been a handmaid of Jieli's mother, Lady Boshi.

sentences.zh: 頡利初誕，以付渾邪，至是哀慟而死。

translations.literal: When Jieli was first born, he was entrusted to Hunxie; at this point he grieved and died of sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: When Jieli was born, he had been placed in Hunxie's care. Now, stricken with grief, Hunxie died.

sentences.zh: 太宗聞而異之，贈中郎將，仍葬於頡利墓側，樹碑以紀之。

translations.literal: Taizong heard and marveled; he posthumously granted Middle Commander and had him buried beside Jieli's tomb, with a stele erected to record it.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong, moved by the deed, posthumously honored him as Middle Commander, had him buried beside Jieli's tomb, and set up a stele to commemorate his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 突利可汗什缽苾者，始畢可法之嫡子，頡利之侄也。

translations.literal: Tuli Khan Shibili was the legitimate son of Shibi Khan and Jieli's nephew.
translations.idiomatic: Tuli Khan Shibili was the eldest son of Shibi Khan and Jieli's nephew.

sentences.zh: 隋大業中，突利年數歲，始畢遣領其東牙之兵，號為泥步設。

translations.literal: During the Sui Daye era, when Tuli was still a child of several years, Shibi sent him to lead the eastern wing troops, titled Nibu She.
translations.idiomatic: During the Sui reign era Daye, while Tuli was still only a few years old, Shibi placed him in command of the eastern wing and gave him the title Nibu She.

sentences.zh: 隋淮南公主之北也，遂妻之。

translations.literal: When the Sui Huainan Princess went north, he took her in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: When the Sui princess of Huainan came north, he took her to wife.

sentences.zh: 頡利嗣位，以為突利可汗，牙直幽州之北。

translations.literal: When Jieli succeeded to the throne, he made him Tuli Khan, with his court directly north of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Jieli succeeded to the khanate, he created Tuli khan and established his camp directly north of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 突利在東偏，管奚、等數十部，征稅無度，諸部多怨之。

translations.literal: Tuli was in the eastern sector, administering the Xi, Khitan and several dozen other tribes; his levies and taxes knew no bounds, and the tribes mostly resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Tuli held the eastern territories and ruled over the Xi, Khitan, and several dozen other tribes. His exactions knew no limit, and many of the tribes came to resent him.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，奚，等並來歸附，頡利怒其失眾，遣北征延陀，又喪師，遂囚而撻焉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan, the Xi, Khitan and others all came to submit; Jieli was angry at losing his followers, sent him north to campaign against the Yantuo, he again lost his army, and was therefore imprisoned and flogged.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenguan reign the Xi, Khitan, and others defected to Tang. Enraged at the loss of his subjects, Jieli sent Tuli north against the Yantuo. Tuli was defeated again, then imprisoned and beaten.

sentences.zh: 突利初自武德時，深自結於太宗；

translations.literal: Tuli from the Wude era onward had deeply bound himself to Taizong;
translations.idiomatic: From the Wude era onward Tuli had cultivated a close bond with Taizong;

sentences.zh: 太宗亦以恩義撫之，結為兄弟，與盟而去。

translations.literal: Taizong also treated him with grace and righteousness, bound as sworn brothers, and parted after alliance.
translations.idiomatic: and Taizong in turn treated him with kindness and honor, swearing brotherhood with him before they parted.

sentences.zh: 後頡利政亂，驟征兵於突利，拒之不與，由是有隙。

translations.literal: Later when Jieli's government fell into disorder, he urgently conscripted troops from Tuli; Tuli refused to provide them—thereby arose the rift.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as Jieli's rule collapsed, he repeatedly demanded troops from Tuli, who refused. From that breach arose open enmity.

sentences.zh: 貞觀三年，表請入朝。

translations.literal: In Zhenguan year three, he memorialized requesting to enter court.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhenguan he petitioned to come to court.

sentences.zh: 上謂侍臣曰：「朕觀前代為國者，勞心以憂萬姓，世祚乃長；

translations.literal: The Emperor said to his attendants: "I observe that rulers of former ages who toiled in heart to worry for the myriad people—their dynastic fortune was long;
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor told his ministers, "Rulers of old who wore themselves out in care for the people enjoyed long reigns;

sentences.zh: 役人以奉其身，社稷必滅。

translations.literal: those who worked the people to serve themselves—their altars of soil and grain perished surely.
translations.idiomatic: those who exhausted the people to serve their own pleasure saw their dynasties fall.

sentences.zh: 今北蕃百姓喪亡。

translations.literal: Now the northern frontier peoples' common people are dying and lost.
translations.idiomatic: Now the common folk of the northern tribes are dying in vast numbers.

sentences.zh: 誠由其君不君之故也。

translations.literal: Truly it is because their ruler did not rule as a ruler ought.
translations.idiomatic: That is truly because their khan has failed to rule as a khan should.

sentences.zh: 至使突利情願入朝，若非困迫，何能至此？

translations.literal: To the point that Tuli willingly seeks to enter court—if not pressed by hardship, how could it come to this?
translations.idiomatic: Tuli now willingly seeks refuge at my court. Had he not been driven to extremity, how could matters have come to this?

sentences.zh: 夷狄弱則邊境無虞，亦甚為慰。

translations.literal: When the barbarians weaken, the borders have no worry—this is also greatly comforting.
translations.idiomatic: When the northern peoples weaken, our borders are safer—and that is cause for relief.

sentences.zh: 然見其顛狽，又不能不懼，所以然者，慮己有不逮，恐禍變亦爾。

translations.literal: Yet seeing their disarray, I cannot but also fear—the reason being, I worry I may fall short myself, and fear calamity might change for us likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Yet to see their ruin is also to feel fear, for I wonder whether I too may one day fall short—and whether such disaster may someday befall us.

sentences.zh: 朕今視不能遠見，聽不能遠聞，唯藉公等盡忠匡弼，無得惰於諫諍也。」

translations.literal: I now cannot see far nor hear afar—I rely solely on you gentlemen to devote yourselves loyally in support; do not grow slack in remonstrance."
translations.idiomatic: My eyes cannot see far and my ears cannot hear afar. I depend on you to serve me faithfully and to speak plainly when I err. Do not grow lax in your counsel."

sentences.zh: 突利尋為頡利所攻，遣使來乞師。

translations.literal: Soon after, Tuli was attacked by Jieli and sent envoys to request troops.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Jieli attacked Tuli, who sent envoys begging for aid.

sentences.zh: 太宗謂近臣曰：「朕與突利結為兄弟，不可以不救。」

translations.literal: Taizong said to his close ministers: "I bound myself as brother with Tuli—I cannot fail to rescue him."
translations.idiomatic: Taizong told his close advisers, "Tuli and I are sworn brothers. I cannot abandon him."

sentences.zh: 杜如晦進曰：「夷狄無信，其來自久，國家雖為守約，彼必背之。

translations.literal: Du Ruhui advanced and said: "The barbarians are faithless—this has been so from long ago; though the state keeps its covenants, they will surely betray them.
translations.idiomatic: Du Ruhui stepped forward and said, "The northern tribes have never been trustworthy. Even if we keep faith, they will break theirs.

sentences.zh: 不若因其亂而取之，所謂取亂侮亡之道。」

translations.literal: Better to take them amid their disorder—what is called the way of seizing disorder and despising the perishing."
translations.idiomatic: Better to strike while they are in chaos. That is the ancient principle: take advantage of disorder and strike the dying."

sentences.zh: 太宗然之。

translations.literal: Taizong assented.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong agreed.

sentences.zh: 因令將軍周範屯太原，以圖進取。

translations.literal: He therefore ordered General Zhou Fan to encamp at Taiyuan to plan an advance.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered General Zhou Fan to encamp at Taiyuan and prepare to move against Jieli.

sentences.zh: 突利乃率其眾來奔，太宗禮之甚厚，頻賜以禦膳。

translations.literal: Tuli then led his followers to defect; Taizong treated him with great honor and repeatedly granted him imperial meals.
translations.idiomatic: Tuli thereupon led his people in flight to Tang. Taizong received him with great honor and often sent him food from the imperial table.

sentences.zh: 四年，授右衛大將軍，封北平郡王，食邑封七百戶，以其下兵眾置順祐等州，帥部落還蕃。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he was appointed Grand General of the Right Guard, enfeoffed as Prince of Beiping Commandery with a fief of seven hundred households; his subordinate troops were placed in Shunyu and other prefectures, and he led his tribes back to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was made Grand General of the Right Guard and enfeoffed as Prince of Beiping with a fief of seven hundred households. His followers were settled in Shunyu and other prefectures, and he was sent back to the frontier at the head of his tribes.

sentences.zh: 太宗謂曰：「昔爾祖啟民亡失兵馬，一身投隋，隋家翌立，遂至強盛，荷隋之恩，未嘗報德。

translations.literal: Taizong said: "Formerly your ancestor Qimin lost horse and troops; alone he threw himself upon Sui; the Sui house immediately established him, until he grew strong—bearing Sui's grace, he never repaid that kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said to him, "Your ancestor Qimin lost his horses and soldiers and came alone to seek Sui's protection. The Sui court raised him up until his house grew mighty. Yet he never repaid that debt of kindness.

sentences.zh: 至爾父始畢，乃為隋家之患，自爾已後，無歲不侵擾中國。

translations.literal: When your father Shibi came, he became a trouble to the Sui house; from then on, no year passed without harassing China.
translations.idiomatic: When your father Shibi rose to power, he became a scourge to Sui. From that day forward scarcely a year passed without raids into China.

sentences.zh: 天實禍淫，大降災變，爾眾散亂，死亡略盡。

translations.literal: Heaven truly punishes the licentious—great calamities descended; your multitude scattered in disorder, death nearly complete.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven punishes wickedness. Great disasters fell upon you. Your people scattered and were all but destroyed.

sentences.zh: 既事窮後，乃來投我，我所以不立爾為可汗者，正為啟民前事故也。

translations.literal: After affairs reached extremity, you came to throw yourself upon me—the reason I do not establish you as khan is precisely because of Qimin's former affair.
translations.idiomatic: Only when all was lost did you come to me. I do not make you khan precisely because of what happened under Qimin.

sentences.zh: 改變前法，欲中國久安，爾宗族永固，是以授爾都督。

translations.literal: Changing the former method, wishing China long peace and your clan eternal stability—therefore I appoint you military governor.
translations.idiomatic: I mean to break with the old way, so that China may know lasting peace and your clan may endure. That is why I appoint you military governor instead.

sentences.zh: 當須依我國法，整齊所部，不得妄相侵掠，如有所違，當獲重罪。」

translations.literal: You must follow our state's laws, put your tribes in order, and must not rashly raid one another; if there is violation, you will incur heavy punishment."
translations.idiomatic: You must obey the laws of the empire, keep your tribes in order, and refrain from raiding one another. Any breach will bring severe punishment."

sentences.zh: 五年，征入朝，至并州，道病卒，年二十九。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was summoned to court; he reached Bingzhou, fell ill on the road, and died, aged twenty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was summoned to court. He reached Bingzhou, took ill on the road, and died at twenty-nine.

sentences.zh: 太宗為之舉哀，詔中書侍郎岑文本為其碑文。

translations.literal: Taizong mourned him and ordered Zhongshu shilang Cen Wenben to compose his epitaph.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong mourned him and ordered Vice Director of the Secretariat Cen Wenben to write his epitaph.

sentences.zh: 子賀邏鶻嗣。

translations.literal: His son Heluohe succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Heluohe succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 突利弟結社率，貞觀初入朝，歷位中郎將。

translations.literal: Tuli's younger brother Jieshelü, early in Zhenguan, entered court and served successively as zhonglangjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Tuli's younger brother Jieshelü came to court early in the Zhenguan reign and rose to the post of commandant of the palace guards.

sentences.zh: 十三年，從幸九成宮，陰結部落得四十餘人，並擁賀邏鶻，相與夜犯御營，逾第四重幕，引弓亂發，殺衛士數十人。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, accompanying the emperor to Jiucheng Palace, he secretly gathered more than forty tribesmen, all supporting Heluohe; together by night they attacked the imperial camp, passed the fourth curtain barrier, drew bows and fired at random, and killed several dozen guards.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, while accompanying the emperor to Jiucheng Palace, he secretly rallied more than forty tribesmen around Heluohe. That night they stormed the imperial camp, broke through the fourth line of tents, and loosed their bows in wild volleys, killing dozens of guards.

sentences.zh: 折沖孫武開率兵奮擊，乃退。

translations.literal: Zhechong Sun Wukai led troops in fierce attack, and they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Zhechong Sun Wukai led his men in a fierce counterattack and drove them back.

sentences.zh: 北走渡渭水，欲奔其部落。

translations.literal: They fled north, crossed the Wei River, and intended to flee to their tribe.
translations.idiomatic: They fled north across the Wei River, hoping to reach their tribesmen.

sentences.zh: 尋皆捕而斬之，詔原賀邏鶻，流於嶺外。

translations.literal: Soon all were captured and executed; an edict pardoned Heluohe and exiled him beyond the Ling Mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Soon all were captured and executed. An edict spared Heluohe but banished him beyond the Ling Mountains.

sentences.zh: 頡利之敗也，其部落或走薛延陀，或走西域，而來降者甚眾。

translations.literal: When Jieli was defeated, his tribes either fled to Xueyantuo or to the Western Regions, while those who came to surrender were very many.
translations.idiomatic: When Jieli fell, some of his tribes fled to Xueyantuo or to the Western Regions, but vast numbers came over to Tang.

sentences.zh: 詔議安邊之術。

translations.literal: An edict was issued to deliberate on methods for securing the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: The court was ordered to debate how best to secure the northern frontier.

sentences.zh: 朝士多言突厥恃強，擾亂中國，為日久矣。

translations.literal: Court officials mostly said the Turks relied on their strength and had disturbed China for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Many at court argued that the Turks had long relied on their strength to harass China.

sentences.zh: 今天實喪之，窮來歸我，本非慕義之心。

translations.literal: Now Heaven has indeed abandoned them; destitute, they come to submit to us—they fundamentally lack a heart that admires righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven has now cast them off. They come to us in desperation, not from any love of our virtue.

sentences.zh: 因其歸命，分其種落，俘之河南兗、豫之地，散居州縣，各使耕織，百萬胡虜可得化為百姓，則中國有加戶之利，塞北可常空矣。

translations.literal: Taking advantage of their submission, divide their tribes, relocate them to Henan in Yan and Yu, scatter them among prefectures and counties, have each farm and weave—millions of barbarian captives can be transformed into common people; then China gains the benefit of increased households, and the northern frontier can be permanently emptied.
translations.idiomatic: We should seize this moment of submission, break up their tribes, and resettle them south of the Yellow River in Yan and Yu, scattering them among the prefectures and counties to farm and weave. Millions of barbarians could become ordinary subjects. China would gain households; the northern marches would stand empty.

sentences.zh: 唯中書令溫彥博議請準漢建武時置降匈奴於五原塞下。

translations.literal: Only Zhongshu Ling Wen Yanbo advocated following the Han Jianwu precedent of settling surrendered Xiongnu below the Wuyuan frontier pass.
translations.idiomatic: Only Chief Minister Wen Yanbo urged following the Han precedent under Emperor Guangwu of settling surrendered Xionnu below the Wuyuan Pass.

sentences.zh: 全其部落，得為捍蔽，又不離其土俗，因而撫之，一則實空虛之地，二則示無猜心。

translations.literal: Preserve their tribes intact, have them serve as a shield, and without separating them from their native customs, thus comfort them—first, truly fill empty lands; second, show no suspicious mind.
translations.idiomatic: Keep their tribes whole and use them as a frontier shield. Do not tear them from their customs; win them by kindness. That would fill empty lands and show that we bear them no suspicion.

sentences.zh: 若遣向河南兗、豫，則乖物性，故非含育之道。

translations.literal: If sent to Henan, Yan, and Yu, it would violate their nature—thus not the way of nurturing.
translations.idiomatic: To send them to Henan, Yan, and Yu would go against their nature. That is not the way of humane rule.

sentences.zh: 太宗將從之。

translations.literal: Taizong was about to follow this.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong was inclined to accept this view.

sentences.zh: 秘書監魏征奏言：「突厥自古至今，未有如斯之破敗者也，此是上天剿絕，宗廟神武。

translations.literal: Mishu Jian Wei Zheng memorialized: "From antiquity to the present the Turks have never been so utterly broken—this is Heaven striking them down, the ancestral temples' divine martial power.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat Director Wei Zheng memorialized: "From antiquity until now the Turks have never been so utterly broken. This is Heaven's judgment upon them and the divine martial power of our ancestral temples.

sentences.zh: 且其世寇中國，百姓冤仇，陛下以其降伏，不能誅滅，即宜遣還河北，居其故土。

translations.literal: Moreover they have generation upon generation raided China; the people bear deep grievances. Your Majesty, since they have surrendered, cannot slaughter them—yet should send them back north of the He to dwell on their old lands.
translations.idiomatic: For generations they have raided China, and the people bear deep grievances against them. Your Majesty cannot simply slaughter them now that they have surrendered—but you should send them back north of the Yellow River to their old lands.

sentences.zh: 匈奴人面獸心，非我族類，強必寇盜，弱則卑服，不顧恩義，其天性也。

translations.literal: The Xiongnu have human faces but beast hearts; they are not our kind. When strong they must raid and plunder; when weak they humbly submit—they care nothing for kindness and righteousness; such is their nature.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiongnu have the faces of men and the hearts of beasts. They are not of our kind. When strong they raid; when weak they cringe. Gratitude and duty mean nothing to them. That is their nature.

sentences.zh: 秦、漢患其若是，故發猛將以擊之，收取河南，以為郡縣，陛下奈何以內地居之！

translations.literal: Qin and Han were troubled precisely because of this, so they sent fierce generals to strike them, took Henan and made it commanderies and counties—how can Your Majesty settle them in the interior!
translations.idiomatic: Qin and Han were vexed by this very problem and sent fierce generals against them, seized the region south of the Yellow River, and turned it into commanderies and counties. How can Your Majesty settle them in the heartland!

sentences.zh: 且今降者幾至十萬，數年之間，孳息百倍，居我肘腋，密邇王畿，心腹之疾，將為後患，尤不可河南處也。」

translations.literal: And now the surrendered number nearly a hundred thousand; within a few years they will multiply a hundredfold, dwelling at our elbow, close upon the imperial domain—a malady of the heart and belly, a future calamity; all the more must they not be placed in Henan."
translations.idiomatic: The surrendered now number nearly a hundred thousand. Within a few years they will multiply a hundredfold, dwelling at our very elbow, hard upon the capital—a disease of the heart and belly, a calamity in waiting. They must not be placed south of the Yellow River."

sentences.zh: 溫彥博奏曰：「天子之於物也，天覆地載，有歸我者，則必養之。

translations.literal: Wen Yanbo memorialized: "The Son of Heaven toward all things—Heaven covers, Earth bears—whoever comes to us must be nourished.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Yanbo replied: "The Son of Heaven embraces all things as Heaven covers and Earth upholds. Whoever comes to us must be sheltered and fed.

sentences.zh: 今突厥破滅之余，歸心降附，陛下不加憐湣，棄而不納，非天地之道，阻四夷之意，臣愚甚謂不可。

translations.literal: Now among the broken remnants of the Turks, hearts turned in submission—if Your Majesty adds no pity but casts them out and will not receive them, that is not the Way of Heaven and Earth, blocks the intent of the four barbarians; this minister in his folly deems it impossible.
translations.idiomatic: These are the broken remnants of the Turks, their hearts turned toward us in submission. If Your Majesty shows no pity but casts them out and refuses to receive them, that is not the way of Heaven and Earth. It would alienate the four quarters. I humbly deem that impossible.

sentences.zh: 遣居河南，所謂死而生之，亡而存之，懷我德惠，終無叛逆。」

translations.literal: Settling them in Henan—this is what is meant by 'giving life to the dead, preserving the perished'—cherishing our virtue and kindness, they will never rebel."
translations.idiomatic: Settling them south of the Yellow River is what the ancients meant by giving life to the dead and preserving what was lost. Cherishing our virtue and kindness, they will never rebel."

sentences.zh: 魏征又曰：「晉代有魏時胡落，分居近郡，平吳已後，郭欽、江統勸武帝逐出塞外；

translations.literal: Wei Zheng again said: "In Jin times there were Xiongnu remnants from Wei, scattered among neighboring commanderies; after Wu was pacified, Guo Qin and Jiang Tong urged Emperor Wu to drive them beyond the frontier;
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng answered again: "In Jin times there were Xiongnu bands left over from Wei, settled among the neighboring commanderies. After Wu was pacified, Guo Qin and Jiang Tong urged Emperor Wu to drive them beyond the frontier.

sentences.zh: 不用欽等言，數年之後，遂傾瀍、洛。

translations.literal: he did not use Guo Qin and the others' advice; within years thereafter, [the realm] toppled at Chan and Luo.
translations.idiomatic: He did not heed Guo Qin and the others. Within a few years the dynasty fell at Chan and Luo.

sentences.zh: 前代覆車，殷鑒不遠，陛下必用彥博之言，遣居河南，所謂養獸自遺患也！」

translations.literal: Former ages' overturned carts—the mirror is not far. If Your Majesty must use Yanbo's words and settle them in Henan, this is what is meant by 'raising beasts to leave yourself a calamity'!"
translations.idiomatic: The overturned cart of former ages is a mirror not far off. If Your Majesty follows Yanbo's counsel and settles them south of the Yellow River, you will be raising beasts to leave yourself a future calamity!"

sentences.zh: 彥博又曰：「聞聖人之道，無所不通，古先哲王，有教無類。

translations.literal: Yanbo again said: "I have heard the Way of the sages is without anything it cannot reach; the ancient sage kings had instruction without distinction of kind.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo replied again: "I have heard that the Way of the sages reaches everywhere, and that the ancient sage kings taught without distinction of kind.

sentences.zh: 突厥余魂，以命歸我，我援護之，收居內地，稟我指麾，教以禮法，數年之後，盡為農民。

translations.literal: The Turk remnant souls, offering their lives to us—if we aid and protect them, gather them within the realm, receive our command, teach them rites and law, within years all will become farmers.
translations.idiomatic: These Turk remnants offer their lives to us. If we aid and protect them, settle them within the realm, command them, and teach them rites and law, within a few years they will all become farmers.

sentences.zh: 選其酋首，遣居宿衛，畏威懷德，何患之有？

translations.literal: Select their chieftains, send them to dwell as palace guards—in awe of authority, cherishing virtue—what worry could there be?
translations.idiomatic: Choose their chieftains and keep them at court as palace guards. In awe of our might and grateful for our kindness—what cause for worry could there be?

sentences.zh: 光武居南單于內郡，為漢籓翰，終乎一代，不有叛逆。」

translations.literal: Guangwu settled the Southern Chanyu in inner commanderies as Han's frontier bulwark—throughout that age there was no rebellion.
