translations.idiomatic: Emperor Guangwu settled the Southern Chanyu in the inner commanderies as a bulwark for Han, and through that whole age there was no rebellion.

sentences.zh: 彥博既口給，引類百端，太宗遂用其計，於朔方之地，自幽州至靈州置順、祐、化、長四州都督府，又分頡利之地六州，左置定襄都督府，右置雲中都督府，以統其部眾。

translations.literal: Yanbo being quick with words, citing parallels by the hundred, Taizong then adopted his plan: in the Shuofang region, from Youzhou to Lingzhou established four zongdufu—Shun, You, Hua, Chang—and further divided Jieli's lands into six prefectures; on the left established Dingxiang Zongdufu, on the right Yunzhong Zongdufu, to govern their tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo was quick of tongue and cited precedents by the hundred. Taizong adopted his plan. In the Shuofang region, from Youzhou to Lingzhou, he established four area commands—Shun, You, Hua, and Chang—and further divided Jieli's lands into six prefectures, placing Dingxiang Command on the left and Yunzhong Command on the right to govern the tribes.

sentences.zh: 其酋首至者，皆拜為將軍、中郎將等官，布列朝廷，五品以上百餘人，因而入居長安者數千家。

translations.literal: Chieftains who arrived were all appointed generals, zhonglangjiang and such; arrayed in court, over a hundred of fifth rank and above; thus several thousand households entered and dwelt in Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Chieftains who came were appointed generals, commandants of the palace guards, and the like—more than a hundred of fifth rank and above filled the court—and several thousand households took up residence in Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 自結社率之反也，太宗始患之。

translations.literal: From Jieshelü's rebellion, Taizong first grew anxious.
translations.idiomatic: After Jieshelü's rebellion, Taizong first grew uneasy.

sentences.zh: 又上書者多雲處突厥於中國，殊謂非便，乃徙於河北，立右武候大將軍、化州都督、懷化郡王思摩為乙彌泥孰侯利苾可汗，賜姓李氏，率所部建牙於河北。

translations.literal: Also many who submitted memorials said settling Turks within China was quite inconvenient; therefore they were moved to Hebei, and Right Wu Hou General, Hua Zhou Dudu, Prince of Huaihua Commandery Simo was established as Ilbilish Beg Khan, given surname Li, leading his tribe to establish headquarters in Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: Many memorials also argued that settling Turks within China was ill-advised. The court therefore moved them to Hebei, installed Right Wu Hou General and Prince of Huaihua Simo as khan Ilbilish Beg, granted him the surname Li, and had him lead his tribes to establish headquarters in Hebei.

sentences.zh: 思摩者，頡利族人也。

translations.literal: Simo was of Jieli's clan.
translations.idiomatic: Simo was of Jieli's clan.

sentences.zh: 始畢、處羅以其貌似胡人，不類突厥，疑非阿史那族類，故歷處羅、頡利世，常為夾畢特勒，終不得典兵為設。

translations.literal: At first Shibi and Chuluo because his appearance resembled a Hu, unlike Turks, suspected he was not of the Ashina clan; through Chuluo's and Jieli's reigns he always served as Jabiy tegin, never obtaining command of troops as a shad.
translations.idiomatic: Shibi and Chuluo had thought his face resembled a foreigner rather than a Turk and suspected he was not truly of the Ashina line. Through the reigns of Chuluo and Jieli he always served as Jabiy tegin and never won command of troops as a shad.

sentences.zh: 武德初，數來朝貢，高祖封為和順郡王。

translations.literal: Early in Wude, repeatedly came to court with tribute; Gaozu enfeoffed him as Prince of Heshun Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Wude reign he came repeatedly to court with tribute, and Gaozu enfeoffed him as Prince of Heshun.

sentences.zh: 及其國亂，諸部多歸中國，唯思摩隨逐頡利，竟與同擒。

translations.literal: When their state fell into disorder, many tribes mostly submitted to China; only Simo followed Jieli, ultimately captured together with him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Turkish state collapsed, most tribes submitted to Tang. Only Simo stayed with Jieli and was captured along with him.

sentences.zh: 太宗嘉其忠，除右武候大將軍、化州都督，令統頡利舊部落於河南之地，尋改封懷化郡王。

translations.literal: Taizong praised his loyalty, appointed Right Wu Hou General, Hua Zhou Dudu, ordered to govern Jieli's old tribes in Henan; soon changed enfeoffment to Prince of Huaihua.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong praised his loyalty, made him Right Wu Hou General and military governor of Hua Prefecture, and ordered him to govern Jieli's old tribes south of the Yellow River. Soon afterward he was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Huaihua.

sentences.zh: 及將徙於白道之北，思摩等咸憚薛延陀，不肯出塞。

translations.literal: When about to move north of the White Road, Simo and others all feared Xueyantuo and refused to cross the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: When the court prepared to move them north of the White Road, Simo and his people all feared Xueyantuo and refused to cross the frontier.

sentences.zh: 太宗遣司農卿郭嗣本賜延陀璽書曰：

translations.literal: Taizong sent Minister of Court Revenues Guo Siben with a sealed letter to Xueyantuo, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Taizong sent Minister of Court Revenues Guo Siben to Xueyantuo with an imperial letter that read:

sentences.zh: 突厥頡利可汗未破已前，自恃強盛，抄掠中國，百姓被其殺者，不可勝紀。

translations.literal: Before the Turk khan Jieli was broken, relying on his strength he raided China; common folk slain by them cannot be reckoned.
translations.idiomatic: Before the Turk khan Jieli was overthrown, he relied on his strength and raided China year after year. The common people slain by his followers cannot be counted.

sentences.zh: 我發兵擊破之，諸部落悉歸化。

translations.literal: I raised an army, struck and shattered him; all the tribes wholly returned to allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: I raised an army, struck him down, and shattered his power. All the tribes have wholly submitted.

sentences.zh: 我略其舊過，嘉其從善，並授官爵，同我百僚，所有部落，愛之如子，與我百姓不異。

translations.literal: I overlook their old transgressions and praise their turning toward virtue; all were granted ranks and titles, same as my hundred officials—I love their tribes as sons, no different from my own people.
translations.idiomatic: I have overlooked their old crimes and praised their turn toward virtue. I have granted them ranks and titles equal to my own officials. I cherish their tribes as sons, no differently from my own people.

sentences.zh: 但中國禮義，不滅爾國，前破突厥，止為頡利一人為百姓之害，所以廢而黜之，實不貪其土地，利其人馬也。

translations.literal: But China's rites and righteousness do not extinguish your state; the former campaign against the Turks was solely because Jieli alone was the people's scourge—therefore he was deposed and removed; truly I do not covet their land or desire their people and horses.
translations.idiomatic: China's rites and righteousness do not require the extinction of your state. I broke the Turks only because Jieli alone was a scourge to the people. I deposed and removed him. I do not covet Turkish land or desire Turkish horses and men.

sentences.zh: 自黜廢頡利以後，恆欲更立可汗，是以所降部落等並置河南，任其放牧，今戶口羊馬日向滋多。

translations.literal: Since deposing Jieli I have constantly wished to establish another khan; therefore the surrendered tribes were all placed south of the He, left to pasture as they pleased—now households, sheep and horses daily multiply.
translations.idiomatic: Since deposing Jieli I have wished to establish another khan. That is why the surrendered tribes were settled south of the Yellow River and left to pasture as they pleased. Now their households, sheep, and horses grow daily.

sentences.zh: 元許冊立，不可失信，即欲遣突厥渡河，復其國土。

translations.literal: Having long ago promised to invest a khan, I cannot break faith—I intend to send the Turks across the river to restore their homeland.
translations.idiomatic: I long ago promised to invest a khan, and I cannot break faith. I mean to send the Turks back across the river and restore their homeland.

sentences.zh: 我策爾延陀，日月在前，今突厥居後，後者為小，前者為大。

translations.literal: I have measured you, Xueyantuo, and the sun and moon are before you; the Turks now dwell behind—behind is lesser, before is greater.
translations.idiomatic: I have taken your measure, Xueyantuo. The sun and moon stand before you; the Turks will stand behind. The one behind is the lesser; the one before is the greater.

sentences.zh: 爾在磧北，突厥居磧南，各守土境，鎮撫部落。

translations.literal: You in the northern desert, the Turks in the southern desert—each guard your borders and pacify your tribes.
translations.idiomatic: You will hold the northern desert; the Turks will hold the southern desert. Each side is to guard its own territory and keep its tribes in order.

sentences.zh: 若其逾越，故相抄掠，我即將兵各問其罪。

translations.literal: Should either overstep and raid the other, I shall raise troops and call each to account.
translations.idiomatic: If either side crosses the border and raids the other, I shall send troops and hold the guilty party to account.

sentences.zh: 此約既定，非但有便爾身，貽厥子孫，長守富貴也。」

translations.literal: Once this covenant is fixed, it will benefit not only you but your descendants too, who may long hold wealth and honor."
translations.idiomatic: Once this covenant is fixed, it will benefit not only you but your descendants as well, who may long enjoy wealth and honor."

sentences.zh: 於是命禮部尚書趙郡王孝恭賫書就思摩部落，築壇於河上以拜之，並賜之鼓纛。

translations.literal: Thereupon he ordered Minister of Rites Zhao Prince Xiaogong to carry the letter to Simo's tribe; an altar was built by the river to invest him, and drums and banners were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he ordered Minister of Rites Zhao Prince Li Xiaogong to carry the letter to Simo's tribe. An altar was built by the river for his investiture, and drums and banners were bestowed upon him.

sentences.zh: 突厥及胡在諸州安置者，並令渡河北，還其舊部。

translations.literal: Turks and other Hu settled in the various prefectures were all ordered to cross north of the He and return to their old tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Turks and other nomads settled in the various prefectures were all ordered to cross north of the Yellow River and return to their old tribes.

sentences.zh: 又以左屯衛將軍阿史那忠為左賢王，左武衛將軍阿史那泥孰為右賢王。

translations.literal: Also appointed Left Tunwei General Ashina Zhong as Left Wise Prince, Left Wuwei General Ashina Nishu as Right Wise Prince.
translations.idiomatic: He also appointed Left Tunwei General Ashina Zhong as Left Wise Prince and Left Wuwei General Ashina Nishu as Right Wise Prince.

sentences.zh: 以貳之。

translations.literal: To serve as seconds in authority.
translations.idiomatic: They were appointed as deputies to divide authority between them.

sentences.zh: 薛延陀聞太宗遣思摩渡河北，慮其部落翻附磧北，預蓄輕騎，伺至而擊之。

translations.literal: Xueyantuo heard Taizong was sending Simo north of the He, feared their tribes would turn and attach to the northern desert; they gathered light cavalry beforehand to strike when they arrived.
translations.idiomatic: When Xueyantuo learned that Taizong was sending Simo north of the Yellow River, it feared the Turkish tribes would turn and attach themselves north of the desert. It gathered light cavalry in advance to strike them on arrival.

sentences.zh: 太宗遣敕之曰：「擅相侵者，國有常刑。」

translations.literal: Taizong sent an edict: "Whoever dares invade each other—the state has fixed punishments."
translations.idiomatic: Taizong sent an edict: "Whoever dares raid the other will face the fixed punishments of the state."

sentences.zh: 延陀曰：「至尊遣莫相侵掠，敢不奉詔。

translations.literal: Xueyantuo said: "The Sovereign orders that we not raid each other—how dare we disobey the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Xueyantuo replied: "The Sovereign has forbidden mutual raiding. How could we dare disobey?

sentences.zh: 然突厥翻覆難信，其未破前，連年殺中國人，動以千萬計。

translations.literal: Yet the Turks are fickle and hard to trust; before their defeat they killed Chinese year after year, often by the millions in count.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Turks are fickle and cannot be trusted. Before their defeat they killed Chinese year after year, often numbering in the millions.

sentences.zh: 至尊破突厥，須收為奴婢，將與百姓，而反養之如子，結社率竟反，此輩獸心，不可信也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty shattered the Turks—they ought to be taken as slaves and maids and given to the people—yet instead you nurture them like sons; Jieshelü ultimately rebelled—these people's beast-hearts cannot be trusted.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty shattered the Turks. They ought to have been taken as slaves and given to the people. Instead you have nurtured them like sons—and Jieshelü rebelled in the end. These people have the hearts of beasts and cannot be trusted.

sentences.zh: 臣荷恩甚深，請為至尊誅之。」

translations.literal: Your servant owes profound grace—I beg to execute them for Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: Your servant owes you deep grace. I beg leave to execute them on Your Majesty's behalf."

sentences.zh: 時思摩下部眾渡河者凡十萬，勝兵四萬人，思摩不能撫其眾，皆不愜服。

translations.literal: At that time among Simo's tribes those crossing the river totaled a hundred thousand; fit warriors forty thousand; Simo could not mollify his masses—all were discontent.
translations.idiomatic: At that time a hundred thousand of Simo's people crossed the river, including forty thousand fighting men. Simo could not win over his followers, and none were content.

sentences.zh: 至十七年，相率叛之，南渡河，請分處於勝、夏二州之間，詔許之。

translations.literal: Reached the seventeenth year, they successively rebelled, crossed south of the river, asked to be split and settled between Sheng and Xia prefectures; edict granted it.
translations.idiomatic: By the seventeenth year they rose in succession against him, crossed south of the river, and asked to be divided and settled between Sheng and Xia prefectures. The court granted the request.

sentences.zh: 思摩遂輕騎入朝，尋授右武衛將軍，從征遼東，為流矢所中；

translations.literal: Simo then rode light into court; soon appointed Right Wuwei General, followed the Liaodong campaign, struck by a stray arrow;
translations.idiomatic: Simo then rode lightly into court. He was soon made Right Wuwei General and accompanied the Liaodong campaign, where he was struck by a stray arrow.

sentences.zh: 太宗親為吮血，其見顧遇如此。

translations.literal: Taizong personally sucked the blood from his wound—such was the favor shown him.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong personally sucked the blood from his wound. Such was the favor shown him.

sentences.zh: 未幾，卒於京師。

translations.literal: Before long, died in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died in the capital.

sentences.zh: 贈兵部尚書、夏州都督，陪葬昭陵，立墳以象白道山，詔為立碑於化州。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Minister of War, Xia Zhou Dudu; buried with Zhaoling; mound made to resemble Mount Baidao; edict to erect a stele at Hua Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Minister of War and military governor of Xia Prefecture, buried with honor at Zhaoling. His mound was shaped to resemble Mount Baidao, and an edict ordered a stele erected at Hua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 先是，貞觀中，突厥別部有車鼻者，亦阿史那之族也。

translations.literal: Earlier, in Zhenguan, among Turk separate tribes there was one named Chebi, also of the Ashina clan.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, during the Zhenguan reign, among the separate Turkish tribes there was one named Chebi, also of the Ashina clan.

sentences.zh: 代為小可汗，牙於金山之北。

translations.literal: Generation after generation minor khan, headquarters north of Mount Jin.
translations.idiomatic: For generations he had been a minor khan, with his headquarters north of Mount Jin.

sentences.zh: 頡利可汗之敗，北荒諸部將推為大可汗，遇薛延陀為可汗，車鼻不敢當，遂率所部歸於延陀。

translations.literal: When Khan Jieli was defeated, northern wasteland tribes wished to install him as great khan; encountering Xueyantuo becoming khan, Chebi dared not contend, then led his tribe to submit to Xueyantuo.
translations.idiomatic: When Khan Jieli fell, the tribes of the northern wastes wished to install Chebi as great khan. But Xueyantuo had already taken the title, and Chebi dared not contend. He led his tribe to submit to Xueyantuo instead.

sentences.zh: 為人勇烈，有謀略，頗為眾附。

translations.literal: As a man he was brave and fierce, had stratagem—much esteemed by the masses.
translations.idiomatic: He was brave and fierce, skilled in strategy, and greatly admired by his followers.

sentences.zh: 延陀惡而將誅之，車鼻密知其謀，竄歸於舊所，其地去京師萬里，勝兵三萬人，自稱乙註車鼻可汗。

translations.literal: Xueyantuo hated him and was about to execute him; Chebi secretly learned the plot, fled back to his old seat—his land ten thousand li from the capital, fit warriors thirty thousand; styled himself Yizhu Chebi Khan.
translations.idiomatic: Xueyantuo hated him and planned to kill him. Chebi learned of the plot in secret, fled back to his old seat—a land ten thousand li from the capital, with thirty thousand fighting men—and styled himself Khan Yizhu Chebi.

sentences.zh: 西有歌羅祿，北有結骨，皆附隸之。

translations.literal: West was Geluolu, north was Jiegu—all attached to him.
translations.idiomatic: The Geluolu to the west and the Jiegu to the north all submitted to him.

sentences.zh: 自延陀破後，遣其子沙缽羅特勒來朝，貢方物，又請身入朝。

translations.literal: After Xueyantuo was broken, sent his son Shaballo Tele to court with tribute and also asked to enter court in person.
translations.idiomatic: After Xueyantuo was broken, he sent his son Shaballo Tele to court with tribute and also asked to come in person.

sentences.zh: 太宗遣將軍郭廣敬征之，竟不至。

translations.literal: Taizong sent General Guo Guangjing to summon him—he ultimately did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong sent General Guo Guangjing to summon him, but he never came.

sentences.zh: 太宗大怒。

translations.literal: Taizong was greatly enraged.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong was furious.

sentences.zh: 貞觀二十三年，遣右驍衛郎將高侃潛引回紇、仆骨等兵眾襲擊之，其酋長歌邏祿泥孰闕俟利發及拔塞匐處木昆莫賀咄俟斤等，率部落背車鼻，相繼來降。

translations.literal: Zhenguan twenty-third year, sent Right Xiao Wei Langjiang Gao Kan secretly to lead Huihe, Pugu and other troops in surprise attack; chieftains including Geluolu Nishu Que Silifa and Basai Fu Chumukun Mohuoduo Shijin and others led tribes to turn against Chebi and successively surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year of Zhenguan he sent Right Xiao Wei Langjiang Gao Kan secretly to lead Huihe, Pugu, and other forces in a surprise attack. Chieftains including Geluolu Nishu Que Silifa and Basai Fu Chumukun Mohuoduo Shijin led their tribes to turn against Chebi and surrender one after another.

sentences.zh: 永徽元年，侃軍次阿息山。

translations.literal: Yonghui first year, Kan's army halted at Mount Axi.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yonghui, Kan's army halted at Mount Axi.

sentences.zh: 車鼻聞王師至，召所部兵，皆不赴，遂攜其妻子從數百騎而遁，其眾盡降。

translations.literal: Chebi heard the royal army arrived, summoned his troops—none came; then took his wife and children and with several hundred horsemen fled; his masses all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: When Chebi heard the imperial army had arrived, he summoned his troops, but none came. He fled with his wife and children and a few hundred horsemen, and all his people surrendered.

sentences.zh: 侃率精騎追車鼻，獲之，送於京師。

translations.literal: Kan led elite cavalry in pursuit, captured Chebi, sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Kan led elite cavalry in pursuit, captured Chebi, and sent him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 仍獻於社廟，又獻於昭陵。

translations.literal: Still presented at the spirit tablets and also presented at Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: He was presented at the spirit tablets and then at Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 高宗數其罪而赦之，拜左武衛將軍，賜宅於長安，處其餘眾於郁督軍山，置狼山都督以統之。

translations.literal: Gaozong enumerated his crimes then pardoned him, appointed Left Wuwei General, bestowed a mansion in Chang'an; settled remaining masses at Yudujun Mountain, established Langshan Dudu to govern them.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong recited his crimes and then pardoned him, appointing him Left Wuwei General and granting him a mansion in Chang'an. The remaining tribes were settled at Yudujun Mountain, and a Langshan command was established to govern them.

sentences.zh: 車鼻長子羯漫陀，先統拔悉密部。

translations.literal: Chebi's eldest son Jiemantuo had earlier governed the Basmyl tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Chebi's eldest son Jiemantuo had earlier governed the Basmyl tribe.

sentences.zh: 車鼻未敗前，遣其子庵鑠入朝，太宗嘉之，拜左屯衛將軍，更置新黎州，以統其眾。

translations.literal: Before Chebi's defeat, sent his son Anshuo to court; Taizong praised it, appointed Left Tunwei General, newly established Xinli Zhou to govern his masses.
translations.idiomatic: Before Chebi's defeat he had sent his son Anshuo to court. Taizong praised this and made Anshuo Left Tunwei General, establishing Xinli Prefecture anew to govern his followers.

sentences.zh: 車鼻既破之後，突厥盡為封疆之臣，於是分置單于、瀚海二都護府。

translations.literal: After Chebi was broken, Turks all became frontier subjects; thereupon separately established Chanyu and Hanhai two Protectorates.
translations.idiomatic: After Chebi's defeat the Turks all became frontier subjects of the empire. The court then established two protectorates, Chanyu and Hanhai.

sentences.zh: 單于都護領狼山、雲中、桑乾三都督、蘇農等一十四州；

translations.literal: Chanyu Protector governed Langshan, Yunzhong, Sanggan three Dudu and Su'nong and fourteen other prefectures;
translations.idiomatic: The Chanyu Protector governed the three area commands of Langshan, Yunzhong, and Sanggan, together with Su'nong and fourteen other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 瀚海都護領瀚海、金微、新黎等七都督、仙萼、賀蘭等八州，各以其首領為都督、刺史。

translations.literal: Hanhai Protector governed Hanhai, Jinwei, Xinli and seven other Dudu, Xian'e, Helan and eight other prefectures—each with its chieftain as Dudu or Cishi.
translations.idiomatic: The Hanhai Protector governed Hanhai, Jinwei, Xinli, and seven other area commands, together with Xian'e, Helan, and eight other prefectures. In each case the tribal chieftain served as area commander or prefect.

sentences.zh: 高宗東封泰山，狼山都督葛邏祿社利等首領三十餘人，並扈從至嶽下，勒名於封禪之碑。

translations.literal: When Gaozong performed eastern feng at Mount Tai, Langshan Dudu Geluolu Sheli and thirty-odd other chieftains all escorted to the foot of the peak—their names carved on the fengchan stele.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong performed the eastern feng at Mount Tai, Langshan area commander Geluolu Sheli and more than thirty other chieftains all escorted him to the foot of the peak, and their names were carved on the fengchan stele.

sentences.zh: 自永徽已後，殆三十年，北鄙無事。

translations.literal: From Yonghui onward, nearly thirty years—the northern marches were without incident.
translations.idiomatic: From Yonghui onward, for nearly thirty years the northern frontier knew no trouble.

sentences.zh: 調露元年，單于管內突厥首領阿史德溫傅、奉職二部落，始相率反叛，立泥孰匐為可汗，二十四州並叛應之。

translations.literal: Tiaolu first year, within Chanyu jurisdiction Turk chieftains Ashide Wenfu and Fengzhi two tribes first successively rebelled, installed Nishu Fu as khan—twenty-four prefectures all rebelled in response.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tiaolu, within the Chanyu Protectorate the Turkish chieftains Ashide Wenfu and Fengzhi led their two tribes in rebellion, installing Nishu Fu as khan. Twenty-four prefectures rose in response.

sentences.zh: 高宗遣鴻臚卿蕭嗣業、右千牛將軍李景嘉率眾討之，反為溫傅所敗，兵士死者萬餘人。

translations.literal: Gaozong sent Honglu Qing Xiao Suye, Right Qianniu General Li Jingjia leading troops to suppress—instead defeated by Wenfu; soldiers dead over ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong sent Director of Guests Xiao Suye and Right Qianniu General Li Jingjia to suppress them, but Wenfu defeated them instead. More than ten thousand soldiers were killed.

sentences.zh: 又詔禮部尚書裴行儉為定襄道行軍大總管，率太僕少卿李思文、營州都督周道務等統眾三十餘萬，討擊溫傅，大破之。

translations.literal: Also ordered Minister of Rites Pei Xingjian as Dingxiang Circuit campaigning Grand Commander, leading Vice Minister of Imperial Studs Li Siwen, Ying Zhou Dudu Zhou Daowu and others commanding over three hundred thousand to strike Wenfu—greatly shattered them.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered Minister of Rites Pei Xingjian as grand commander of the Dingxiang campaign circuit, leading Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud Li Siwen, Ying Prefecture military governor Zhou Daowu, and others with more than three hundred thousand men against Wenfu. They broke his forces completely.

sentences.zh: 泥孰匐為其下所殺，並擒奉職而還。

translations.literal: Nishu Fu was killed by his subordinates; also captured Fengzhi and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Nishu Fu was killed by his own followers, and Fengzhi was captured and brought back.

sentences.zh: 永隆元年，突厥又迎頡利從兄之子阿史那伏念於夏州，將渡河立為可汗，諸部落復響應從之。

translations.literal: Yonglong first year, Turks again welcomed Jieli's paternal cousin's son Ashina Funian at Xia Zhou, intending to cross the river and install as khan—tribes again responded and followed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yonglong the Turks again welcomed Jieli's paternal cousin's son Ashina Funian at Xia Prefecture, intending to cross the river and install him as khan. The tribes once more answered and followed.

sentences.zh: 又詔裴行儉率將軍曹繼叔、程務挺、李崇直、李文暕等討之。

translations.literal: Again ordered Pei Xingjian leading Generals Cao Jishu, Cheng Wuting, Li Chongzhi, Li Wenliang and others to suppress.
translations.idiomatic: The court again ordered Pei Xingjian, with Generals Cao Jishu, Cheng Wuting, Li Chongzhi, and Li Wenliang, to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 伏念窘急，詣行儉降。

translations.literal: Funian in dire straits, came to Xingjian to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Funian, hard pressed, came to Xingjian and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 行儉遂虜伏念詣京師，斬於東市。

translations.literal: Xingjian thereupon took Fuzhen captive and brought him to the capital, executing him at the Eastern Market.
translations.idiomatic: Xingjian then marched Fuzhen as a prisoner to the capital and had him beheaded at the Eastern Market.

sentences.zh: 永淳二年，突厥阿史那骨咄祿復反叛。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongchun, Ashina Gutulu of the Turks rebelled again.
translations.idiomatic: In 683, Ashina Gutulu of the Türks rose in rebellion once more.

sentences.zh: 骨咄祿者，頡利之疏屬，亦姓阿史那氏。

translations.literal: Gutulu was a distant kinsman of Jieli, and likewise bore the surname Ashina.
translations.idiomatic: Gutulu was a collateral member of the Ashina clan, a distant relative of Jieli Khan.

sentences.zh: 其祖父本是單于右雲中都督舍利元英下首領也，世襲吐屯啜。

translations.literal: His grandfather had originally been a subordinate leader under Shel Yuan Ying, Chanyu Right Protector-General of Yunzhong; the family had hereditarily held the rank of tutunchuo.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather had served as a petty chief under Shel Yuan Ying, Right Protector-General of Yunzhong within the Chanyu Protectorate; the family had inherited the rank of tutunchuo for generations.

sentences.zh: 伏念既破，骨咄祿鳩集亡散，入總材山，聚為群盜，有眾五千餘人。

translations.literal: After Fuzhen was destroyed, Gutulu gathered scattered fugitives, entered Mount Zongcai, formed a band of brigands, and had a following of more than five thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: When Fuzhen fell, Gutulu rallied the scattered survivors, withdrew to Mount Zongcai, and mustered an outlaw band numbering over five thousand.

sentences.zh: 又抄掠九姓，得羊馬甚多，漸至強盛，乃自立為可汗。

translations.literal: He also raided the Nine Tribes, obtained many sheep and horses, gradually grew powerful, and thereupon declared himself khan.
translations.idiomatic: Raiding the Nine Tribes, he seized vast herds of sheep and horses; as his strength grew he proclaimed himself khan.

sentences.zh: 以其弟默啜為設，咄悉匐為葉護。

translations.literal: He appointed his younger brother Mochuo as she and Tuxibo as yehu.
translations.idiomatic: He made his younger brother Mochuo she and Tuxibo yehu.

sentences.zh: 時有阿史德元珍，在單于檢校降戶部落，嘗坐事為單于長史王本立所拘縶，會骨咄祿入寇，元珍請依舊檢校部落，本立許之，因而便投骨咄祿。

translations.literal: At that time there was Ashide Yuanzhen, who was inspecting surrendered-household tribes under the Chanyu Protectorate; he had once been imprisoned by the Chanyu chief secretary Wang Benli for an offense. When Gutulu invaded, Yuanzhen requested to resume inspection of the tribes; Benli consented, and Yuanzhen thereupon defected to Gutulu.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Ashide Yuanzhen was supervising surrendered-household tribes under the Chanyu Protectorate. He had once been detained by the Chanyu chief secretary Wang Benli on a charge of misconduct. When Gutulu raided the frontier, Yuanzhen asked to resume his tribal duties; Benli agreed, and Yuanzhen promptly went over to Gutulu.

sentences.zh: 骨咄祿得之，甚喜，立為阿波達干，令專統兵馬事。

translations.literal: Gutulu, greatly pleased to obtain him, made him apodagan and ordered him to command all military affairs exclusively.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted to have him, Gutulu appointed him apodagan and entrusted him with sole command of the troops.

sentences.zh: 永淳二年，進寇蔚州。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongchun, he advanced to raid You Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In 683 he launched a raid against You Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 豐州都督崔智辯擊之，反為賊所殺。

translations.literal: Feng Prefecture Protector-General Cui Zhibian attacked him but was in turn killed by the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Zhibian, Protector-General of Feng Prefecture, counterattacked but was killed by the enemy.

sentences.zh: 文明元年，又寇朔州，殺掠人吏，則天詔左武威衛大將軍程務挺為單于道安撫大使以備之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wenming, he again raided Shuo Prefecture, killing and plundering officials and people; Empress Wu appointed Left General of the Martial Might Guard Cheng Wuting Pacification Commissioner of the Chanyu Circuit to guard against him.
translations.idiomatic: In 684 he struck Shuo Prefecture again, slaughtering and looting officials and civilians. Empress Wu named Left General of the Martial Might Guard Cheng Wuting Pacification Commissioner of the Chanyu Circuit to meet the threat.

sentences.zh: 垂拱二年，骨咄祿又寇朔、代等州，左玉鈐衛中郎將淳於處平為陽曲道總管，與副將中郎將蒲英節率兵赴援，行至忻州，與賊戰，大敗，死者五千餘人。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chuigong, Gutulu again raided Shuo, Dai, and other prefectures; Left Central Guard Lieutenant Chunyu Chuping was made Commander of the Yangqu Circuit and, with his deputy Lieutenant Pu Yingjie, led troops to the relief; reaching Xin Prefecture they fought the rebels, suffered a great defeat, and more than five thousand men were killed.
translations.idiomatic: In 686 Gutulu raided Shuo, Dai, and neighboring prefectures. Left Central Guard Lieutenant Chunyu Chuping, appointed Commander of the Yangqu Circuit, marched to their aid with his deputy Pu Yingjie. At Xin Prefecture they joined battle and were routed; over five thousand soldiers died.

sentences.zh: 三年，骨咄祿及元珍又寇昌平，詔左鷹揚衛大將軍黑齒常之擊卻之。

translations.literal: In the third year, Gutulu and Yuanzhen again raided Changping; the court ordered Left General of the Soaring Hawk Guard Heichi Changzhi to drive them back.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Gutulu and Yuanzhen raided Changping; the court dispatched Left General of the Soaring Hawk Guard Heichi Changzhi and repulsed them.

sentences.zh: 其年八月，又寇朔州，復以常之為燕然道大總管，擊賊於黃花堆，大破之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of that year he again raided Shuo Prefecture; Changzhi was once more made Grand Commander of the Yanran Circuit and, attacking the rebels at Huanghuadui, inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: That August he raided Shuo Prefecture again. Changzhi was reappointed Grand Commander of the Yanran Circuit and crushed the enemy at Huanghuadui.

sentences.zh: 追奔四十餘里，賊眾遂散走磧北。

translations.literal: Pursuing the rout for more than forty li, the rebel host scattered and fled north of the desert.
translations.idiomatic: The pursuit ran more than forty li; the rebel force broke apart and fled into the northern wastes.

sentences.zh: 右監門衛中郎將爨寶璧又率精兵一萬三千人出塞窮追，反為骨咄祿所敗，全軍盡沒，寶璧輕騎遁歸。

translations.literal: Right Gate Guard Lieutenant Cuan Baobi also led an elite force of thirteen thousand men beyond the frontier in relentless pursuit but was in turn defeated by Gutulu; the entire army was destroyed, and Baobi escaped on a light horse.
translations.idiomatic: Right Gate Guard Lieutenant Cuan Baobi then led thirteen thousand picked troops in pursuit beyond the border, only to be beaten by Gutulu. His whole force was wiped out; Baobi fled back alone on a swift mount.

sentences.zh: 初，寶璧見常之破賊，遽表請窮其餘黨，則天詔常之與寶璧計議，遙為聲援。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Baobi saw that Changzhi had broken the rebels, he hastily memorialized requesting to exterminate the remaining band; Empress Wu ordered Changzhi and Baobi to consult and provide distant support.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, seeing Changzhi's victory, Baobi had urgently petitioned to hunt down the remnants. Empress Wu instructed Changzhi and Baobi to coordinate plans and lend distant support.

sentences.zh: 寶璧以為破賊在朝夕，貪功先行。

translations.literal: Baobi thought the rebels would be destroyed within days and, greedy for merit, marched ahead.
translations.idiomatic: Baobi believed victory was a matter of days and, eager for glory, pushed ahead on his own.

sentences.zh: 又令人出塞二千餘里覘候，見元珍等部落皆不設備，遂率眾掩襲之。

translations.literal: He also sent men more than two thousand li beyond the frontier to reconnoiter; seeing that Yuanzhen's tribes were entirely unprepared, he led his force in a surprise attack.
translations.idiomatic: He sent scouts more than two thousand li beyond the border and, finding Yuanzhen's camps unguarded, launched a surprise assault.

sentences.zh: 既至，又遣人報賊，令得設備出戰，遂為賊所覆，寶璧坐此伏誅。

translations.literal: After arriving he again sent men to inform the enemy, allowing them to prepare and come out to fight; he was therefore overrun by the rebels, and Baobi was executed for this offense.
translations.idiomatic: Once there, he inexplicably warned the enemy, giving them time to arm and meet him in battle. They annihilated his force, and Baobi was put to death for it.

sentences.zh: 則天大怒，因改骨咄祿為不卒祿。

translations.literal: Empress Wu was greatly enraged and therefore changed Gutulu's name to Buzulu.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu, furious, rechristened Gutulu Buzulu—"the Unfinished One."

sentences.zh: 元珍後率兵討突騎施，臨陣戰死。

translations.literal: Yuanzhen later led troops against the Turgesh and was killed in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhen later marched against the Turgesh and fell on the field.

sentences.zh: 骨咄祿，天授中病卒。

translations.literal: Gutulu died of illness during the Tianshou era.
translations.idiomatic: Gutulu died of illness during the Tianshou period.

sentences.zh: 默啜者，骨咄祿之弟也。

translations.literal: Mochuo was Gutulu's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Mochuo was Gutulu's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 骨咄祿死時，其子尚幼，默啜遂篡其位，自立為可汗。

translations.literal: When Gutulu died his son was still young; Mochuo thereupon usurped the position and declared himself khan.
translations.idiomatic: Gutulu's son was still a child when he died; Mochuo seized the throne and proclaimed himself khan.

sentences.zh: 長壽二年，率眾寇靈州，殺掠人吏。

translations.literal: In the second year of Changshou he led a host to raid Ling Prefecture, killing and plundering officials and people.
translations.idiomatic: In 693 he led his tribes against Ling Prefecture, slaughtering and looting officials and civilians.

sentences.zh: 則天遣白馬寺僧薛懷義為代北道行軍大總管，領十大將軍以討之，既不遇賊，尋班師焉。

translations.literal: Empress Wu dispatched the White Horse Temple monk Xue Huaiyi as Grand Commander of the Daibei Circuit with ten great generals to punish him; they never encountered the enemy and soon withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu sent Xue Huaiyi, a monk of White Horse Temple, as Grand Commander of the Daibei Circuit at the head of ten great generals to chastise him. They never found the enemy and soon marched home.

sentences.zh: 默啜俄遣使來朝，則天大悅，冊授左衛大將軍，封歸國公，賜物五千段。

translations.literal: Before long Mochuo sent envoys to court; Empress Wu was greatly pleased, enfeoffed him as Left Guard General and Duke of Returning to the Realm, and bestowed five thousand bolts of goods.
translations.idiomatic: Mochuo soon sent envoys to court. Empress Wu was delighted, appointed him Left Guard General, created him Duke of Returning to the Realm, and granted five thousand bolts of goods.

sentences.zh: 明年，復遣使請和，又加授遷善可汗。

translations.literal: The next year he again sent envoys requesting peace and was further invested as Qianshan Khan.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he sent envoys seeking peace and was further invested as Qianshan Khan.

sentences.zh: 萬歲通天元年，契丹首領李盡忠、孫萬榮反叛，攻陷營府。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wansui Tongtian, the Khitan leaders Li Jinzhong and Sun Wanrong rebelled and captured Ying Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In 696 the Khitan chiefs Li Jinzhong and Sun Wanrong rebelled and overran Ying Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 默啜遣使上言：「請還河西降戶，即率部落兵馬為國家討擊契丹。」

translations.literal: Mochuo sent envoys to report: "If the surrendered households of Hexi are returned, I will lead my tribal cavalry to strike the Khitan for the state.
translations.idiomatic: Mochuo sent envoys with a message: "Return the surrendered households of Hexi, and I will lead my tribal horsemen to crush the Khitan on the empire's behalf.

sentences.zh: 制許之。

translations.literal: The edict granted this.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved.

sentences.zh: 默啜遂攻討契丹，部眾大潰，盡獲其家口，默啜自此兵眾漸盛。

translations.literal: Mochuo thereupon attacked the Khitan; their forces collapsed in rout, and he captured all their families; from this his army gradually grew stronger.
translations.idiomatic: Mochuo then fell upon the Khitan. Their army broke and fled; he seized their entire population. From that day his forces swelled.

sentences.zh: 則天尋遣使冊立默啜為特進、頡跌利施大單于、立功報國可汗。

translations.literal: Empress Wu soon sent envoys to invest Mochuo as Special Advancement, Grand Chanyu of the Yiedielishi line, and Khan Who Serves the State with Meritorious Achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu soon dispatched envoys to invest Mochuo as Special Advancement, Grand Chanyu of the Yiedielishi line, and Khan Who Serves the State with Meritorious Achievement.

sentences.zh: 聖歷元年，默啜表請與則天為子，並言有女，請和親。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shenglí, Mochuo memorialized requesting to become Empress Wu's adopted son, and stating that he had a daughter, requested a marriage alliance.
translations.idiomatic: In 698 Mochuo petitioned to become Empress Wu's adopted son and, noting that he had a daughter, asked for a marriage alliance.

sentences.zh: 初，咸亨中，突厥諸部落來降附者，多處之豐、勝、靈、夏、朔、代等六州，謂之降戶。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the Xianheng era, many Turkic tribes that had surrendered were settled in the six prefectures of Feng, Sheng, Ling, Xia, Shuo, and Dai—these were called the surrendered households.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Xianheng era many Türk tribes that submitted had been settled in Feng, Sheng, Ling, Xia, Shuo, and Dai—the so-called surrendered households.

sentences.zh: 默啜至是，又索此降戶及單于都護府之地，兼請農器、種子。

translations.literal: Mochuo now again demanded these surrendered households and the territory of the Chanyu Protectorate, and also requested farm tools and seed.
translations.idiomatic: Mochuo now demanded those surrendered households back, along with the lands of the Chanyu Protectorate, plus farm tools and seed grain.

sentences.zh: 則天初不許，默啜大怨怒，言辭甚慢，拘我使人司賓卿田歸道，將害之。

translations.literal: Empress Wu at first refused; Mochuo was greatly resentful and spoke with extreme insolence, detaining our envoy Director of Reception Tian Guidao and intending to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu refused at first. Mochuo flew into a rage, spoke with open contempt, seized our envoy Director of Reception Tian Guidao, and prepared to execute him.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷懼其兵勢，納言姚璹、鸞臺侍郎楊再思建議請許其和親，遂盡驅六州降戶數千帳，並種子四萬餘碩、農器三千事以與之，默啜浸強由此也。

translations.literal: The court then feared his military strength; Censor-in-Chief Yao Shu and Vice Minister of the Phoenix Terrace Yang Zaisi advised permitting the marriage alliance; the thousands of households of surrendered people in the six prefectures were therefore all driven out, together with more than forty thousand shi of seed and three thousand sets of farm tools, and given to him—Mochuo grew ever stronger from this.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing his armies, the court yielded. Censor-in-Chief Yao Shu and Vice Minister of the Phoenix Terrace Yang Zaisi urged acceptance of the alliance. Thousands of surrendered households from the six prefectures were uprooted, together with over forty thousand shi of seed and three thousand sets of farm tools, and handed over to him. Mochuo's power rose from that bargain.

sentences.zh: 其年，則天令魏王武承嗣、男淮陽王延秀就納其女為妃，遣右豹韜衛大將軍閻知微攝春官尚書，右武威衛郎將楊鸞莊攝司賓卿，大賫金帛，送赴虜庭。

translations.literal: That year Empress Wu ordered Prince of Wei Wu Chengsi and the prince's son, Huaiyang Prince Wu Yanxiu, to go and take his daughter as consort; she dispatched Right General of the Leopard Bow Guard Yan Zhiwei acting as Minister of Spring Affairs and Right Captain of the Martial Might Guard Yang Luanzhuang acting as Director of Reception, bearing great stores of gold and silk, to escort them to the barbarian court.
translations.idiomatic: That year Empress Wu sent Prince of Wei Wu Chengsi and his son Huaiyang Prince Wu Yanxiu to receive Mochuo's daughter in marriage. Right General of the Leopard Bow Guard Yan Zhiwei, acting Minister of Spring Affairs, and Right Captain of the Martial Might Guard Yang Luanzhuang, acting Director of Reception, were sent with lavish gifts to the steppe court.

sentences.zh: 行至黑沙南庭，默啜謂知微等曰：「我女擬嫁與李家天子兒，你今將武家兒來，此是天子兒否？

translations.literal: Reaching the southern court at Heisha, Mochuo said to Zhiwei and the others: "I intended to marry my daughter to a son of the Li Son of Heaven. You now bring a son of the Wu family—is this a son of Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: At the southern court of Heisha, Mochuo confronted Zhiwei and his party: "I meant to marry my daughter to a son of the Li Son of Heaven. You bring me a son of the Wu clan—is this a Son of Heaven?

sentences.zh: 我突厥積代已來，降附李家，今聞李家天子種末總盡，唯有兩兒在，我今將兵助立。」

translations.literal: We Turks for many generations have submitted to the Li house; now I hear the line of Li Sons of Heaven is nearly extinct, with only two sons remaining—I shall now lead troops to help establish one.
translations.idiomatic: For generations my people have bowed to the House of Li. Now I hear the Li line is all but spent, with only two sons left. I will march and help set one of them on the throne.

sentences.zh: 遂收延秀等，拘之別所。

translations.literal: He thereupon seized Yanxiu and the others and detained them separately.
translations.idiomatic: He then seized Yanxiu and his companions and held them apart.

sentences.zh: 偽號知微為可汗，與之率眾十餘萬，襲我靜難及平狄、清夷等軍。

translations.literal: He falsely proclaimed Zhiwei khan and, together with him, led a host of more than one hundred thousand to strike our Jingnan, Pingdi, and Qingyi garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed Zhiwei khan in mockery and, with him at his side, led more than a hundred thousand men against our Jingnan, Pingdi, and Qingyi garrisons.

sentences.zh: 靜難軍使左正鋒衛將軍慕容玄皦以兵五千人降之。

translations.literal: Jingnan Garrison Commander Left Forward Guard General Murong Xuanjiao surrendered with five thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Xuanjiao, commander of Jingnan Garrison, surrendered with five thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 俄進寇媯、檀等州，則天令司屬卿武重規為天兵中道大總管，右武威衛將軍沙咤忠義為天兵西道前軍總管，幽州都督張仁亶為天兵東道總管，率兵三十萬擊之。

translations.literal: Soon he advanced to raid Gui and Tan prefectures; Empress Wu appointed Director of Imperial Clansmen Wu Chonggui Grand Commander of the Central Heaven Army, Right Martial Might Guard General Shacha Zhongyi Vanguard Commander of the Western Heaven Army, and Youzhou Protector-General Zhang Renbian Commander of the Eastern Heaven Army, leading three hundred thousand troops to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: He soon raided Gui and Tan prefectures. Empress Wu named Director of Imperial Clansmen Wu Chonggui Grand Commander of the Central Heaven Army, Right Martial Might Guard General Shacha Zhongyi Vanguard of the Western Heaven Army, and Youzhou Protector-General Zhang Renbian Commander of the Eastern Heaven Army, with three hundred thousand men to meet him.

sentences.zh: 右羽林衛大將軍閻敬容為天兵西道後軍總管，統兵十五萬以為後援。

translations.literal: Right Feathered Forest Guard General Yan Rongrong was made Rear Commander of the Western Heaven Army, commanding one hundred fifty thousand men as reserve.
translations.idiomatic: Right Feathered Forest Guard General Yan Rongrong was appointed Rear Commander of the Western Heaven Army with one hundred fifty thousand men in reserve.

sentences.zh: 默啜又出自恆嶽道，寇蔚州，陷飛狐縣。

translations.literal: Mochuo also came out by the Hengyue route, raided You Prefecture, and captured Feihu County.
translations.idiomatic: Mochuo also descended by the Hengyue route, struck You Prefecture, and took Feihu County.

sentences.zh: 俄進攻定州，殺刺史孫彥高，焚燒百姓廬舍，虜掠男女，無少長皆殺之。

translations.literal: Soon he advanced to attack Ding Prefecture, killed Prefect Sun Yangao, burned the people's dwellings, and carried off men and women; none, young or old, was spared.
translations.idiomatic: He then pressed Ding Prefecture, killed Prefect Sun Yangao, burned the people's homes, and dragged off captives—old and young alike were slaughtered.

sentences.zh: 則天大怒，購斬默啜者，封王，改默啜號為斬啜。

translations.literal: Empress Wu was greatly enraged; she offered enfeoffment as king to whoever could slay Mochuo and changed Mochuo's title to Zhanchuo.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu, enraged, promised kingship to whoever killed Mochuo and rechristened him Zhanchuo—"the Slain One."

sentences.zh: 尋又圍逼趙州，長史唐波若翻城應之，刺史高睿抗節不從，遂遇害。

translations.literal: Soon he again besieged Zhao Prefecture; Chief Administrator Tang Boruo opened the city in collusion, but Prefect Gao Rui held firm and refused; he was therefore killed.
translations.idiomatic: He soon encircled Zhao Prefecture. Chief Administrator Tang Boruo turned traitor and opened the gates, but Prefect Gao Rui stood fast and was murdered for it.

sentences.zh: 則天乃立廬陵王為皇太子，令充河北道行軍大元帥。

translations.literal: Empress Wu thereupon installed Prince of Luling as crown prince and ordered him to serve as Grand Marshal of the Hebei Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu then named Prince of Luling crown prince and appointed him Grand Marshal of the Hebei Circuit.

sentences.zh: 軍未發而默啜盡抄掠趙、定等州男女八九萬人，從五回道而去，所過殘殺，不可勝紀。

translations.literal: Before the army marched, Mochuo had already carried off eighty or ninety thousand men and women of Zhao, Ding, and other prefectures and departed by the Wuhui route; the slaughter along his path was beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Before the army could move, Mochuo had already swept away eighty or ninety thousand people from Zhao, Ding, and neighboring prefectures along the Wuhui route, leaving a trail of devastation beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 沙咤忠義及後軍總管李多祚等皆持重兵，與賊相望，不敢戰。

translations.literal: Shacha Zhongyi and Rear Commander Li Duozuo and others all held heavy forces and faced the enemy without daring to fight.
translations.idiomatic: Shacha Zhongyi, Rear Commander Li Duozuo, and the rest held vast armies yet stood idle, afraid to engage.

sentences.zh: 河北道元帥、納言狄仁傑總兵十萬追之，無所及。

translations.literal: Hebei Circuit Grand Marshal and Censor-in-Chief Di Renjie mustered one hundred thousand troops in pursuit but could not overtake them.
translations.idiomatic: Hebei Grand Marshal and Censor-in-Chief Di Renjie led a hundred thousand men in pursuit but never caught them.

sentences.zh: 二年，默啜立其弟咄悉匐為左廂察，骨咄祿子默矩為右廂察，各主兵馬二萬餘人。

translations.literal: In the second year, Mochuo installed his younger brother Tuxibo as Left Wing Inspector and Gutulu's son Moju as Right Wing Inspector, each commanding more than twenty thousand cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Mochuo appointed his brother Tuxibo Left Wing Inspector and Gutulu's son Moju Right Wing Inspector, each with more than twenty thousand horsemen.

sentences.zh: 又立其子匐俱為小可汗，位在兩察之上，仍主處木昆等十姓兵馬四萬餘人。

translations.literal: He also installed his son Fuju as Lesser Khan, ranking above the two inspectors, and still commanding more than forty thousand troops of the Chumukun and other ten surnames.
translations.idiomatic: He made his son Fuju Lesser Khan, senior to both wing inspectors, with command over more than forty thousand warriors of the Chumukun and the other ten tribes.

sentences.zh: 又號為拓西可汗，自是連歲寇邊。

translations.literal: He also styled himself Tuoxi Khan; from this he raided the frontier year after year.
translations.idiomatic: He took the title Tuoxi Khan as well and from then on raided the borders every year.

sentences.zh: 久視元年，掠隴右諸監馬萬餘匹而去。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiushi he plundered more than ten thousand horses from the horse pastures of Longyou and departed.
translations.idiomatic: In 700 he drove off more than ten thousand horses from the Longyou stud farms and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 制右肅政御史大夫魏元忠為靈武道行軍大總管，以備之，又命安北大都督相王旦為天兵道元帥，統諸軍討擊，竟未行而賊退。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Right Censor-in-Chief Wei Yuanzhong Grand Commander of the Lingwu Circuit to guard against him, and also ordered Northern Pacification Grand Protector Prince of Xiang Dan Grand Marshal of the Heaven Army Circuit to command the armies in punitive attack; before they marched the enemy had already withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yuanzhong, Right Censor-in-Chief, was named Grand Commander of the Lingwu Circuit to block him; Prince of Xiang Dan, Northern Pacification Grand Protector, was ordered to lead the Heaven Army Circuit in a punitive campaign. The armies never marched—the enemy had already retreated.

sentences.zh: 長安三年，默啜遣使莫賀達干，請以女妻皇太子之子。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chang'an, Mochuo sent his envoy Mohedagan requesting that his daughter marry a son of the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: In 703 Mochuo sent his envoy Mohedagan to ask that his daughter marry a son of the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 則天令太子男平恩王重俊、義興王重明廷立見之。

translations.literal: Empress Wu ordered the crown prince's sons, Prince of Ping'en Wu Chongjun and Prince of Yixing Wu Chongming, to receive him at court in formal audience.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu had the crown prince's sons, Prince of Ping'en Wu Chongjun and Prince of Yixing Wu Chongming, receive him in formal audience at court.

sentences.zh: 默啜遣大酋移力貪汗入朝，獻馬千匹，及方物以謝許親之意。

translations.literal: Mochuo sent the great chieftain Yilibaohan to court, presenting one thousand horses and regional goods to thank them for agreeing to the marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Mochuo sent the great chieftain Yilibaohan to court with a thousand horses and native gifts in thanks for the promised marriage.

sentences.zh: 則天宴之於宿羽亭，太子、相王及朝集使三品以上並預會，重賜以遣之。

translations.literal: Empress Wu feasted them at Suyu Pavilion; the crown prince, the Prince of Xiang, and all tribute envoys of third rank and above attended, and they were richly rewarded before dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu held a feast for them at Suyu Pavilion. The crown prince, the Prince of Xiang, and tribute envoys of third rank and above all attended; lavish gifts sent them on their way.

sentences.zh: 中宗即位，默啜又寇靈州鳴沙縣。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhongzong took the throne, Mochuo again raided Mingsha County in Ling Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Zhongzong ascended the throne, Mochuo raided Mingsha County in Ling Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 靈武軍大總管沙咤忠義拒戰久之，官軍敗績，死者六千餘人。

translations.literal: Grand Commander of the Lingwu Army Shacha Zhongyi resisted for a long time; the government army was defeated and more than six thousand men were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commander of the Lingwu Army Shacha Zhongyi fought a long defense, but the imperial force was beaten and more than six thousand soldiers died.

sentences.zh: 賊遂進寇原、會等州，掠隴右群牧馬萬餘匹而去，忠義坐免。

translations.literal: The rebels then advanced to raid Yuan and Hui prefectures, plundered more than ten thousand horses from the Longyou stud farms, and departed; Zhongyi was removed from office for this.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy then struck Yuan and Hui prefectures, drove off more than ten thousand horses from the Longyou pastures, and withdrew. Zhongyi was dismissed for the defeat.

sentences.zh: 中宗下制絕其請婚，仍購募能斬獲默啜者封國王，授諸衛大將軍，賞物二千段。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhongzong issued an edict rejecting the marriage request and again offered enfeoffment as king of the realm and appointment as Grand General of the Guards, with a reward of two thousand bolts of goods, to whoever could capture or kill Mochuo.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhongzong issued an edict refusing the marriage and again promised kingship, a Guard Grand Generalship, and two thousand bolts of goods to whoever captured or killed Mochuo.

sentences.zh: 又命內外官各進破突厥諸策。

translations.literal: He also ordered civil and military officials each to submit strategies for defeating the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: He also commanded every civil and military official to submit plans for breaking the Türks.

sentences.zh: 右補闕盧俌上疏曰：

translations.literal: Right Reminder Lu Fu submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Right Reminder Lu Fu submitted a memorial, saying:

sentences.zh: 臣聞有虞咸熙，苗人逆命，殷宗大化，鬼方不賓，則戎狄交侵，其來遠矣。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that when Yu of the Shun age achieved universal harmony, the Miao rebelled; when the Yin founder accomplished great transformation, the Gui Fang did not submit—thus raids by the Rong and Di are an affliction of ancient standing.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that when Yu of the Shun age brought all under harmony, the Miao defied him; when the Yin founder wrought great transformation, the Gui Fang refused allegiance. Border raids by the northern peoples are an ancient affliction.

sentences.zh: 漢高帝納婁敬之議，與匈奴和親，妻以宗女，賂以鉅萬，冒頓益驕，邊寇不止。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaodi of Han accepted Lou Jing's counsel, concluded a marriage alliance with the Xiongnu, bestowed an imperial daughter in marriage, and lavished gifts worth tens of thousands—yet Modun grew only haughtier, and frontier incursions never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaodi of Han took Lou Jing's advice, married a princess to the Xiongnu, and showered them with treasure worth myriads—yet Modun grew only prouder, and the frontier knew no peace.

sentences.zh: 則遠荒之地，凶悍之俗，難以德綏，可以威制，而降自三代，無聞上策。

translations.literal: Thus in distant wastelands where custom runs fierce and brutal, rule by virtue cannot suffice—only force can restrain them—and since the Three Dynasties no superior policy has ever been heard of.
translations.idiomatic: In distant wastes where men are fierce and custom brutal, virtue alone cannot pacify them—only force can. Since the Three Dynasties, no better policy has been found.

sentences.zh: 今匈奴不臣，擾我亭障，皇赫斯怒，將整元戎。

translations.literal: Now the Xiongnu refuse allegiance and harass our frontier posts; the Son of Heaven's wrath has kindled, and the main army is to be mustered.
translations.idiomatic: Today the northern enemy withholds submission and harries our frontier posts. Imperial wrath has flared, and the great army is to be assembled.

sentences.zh: 臣聞方叔帥師，功歌周《雅》；

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that Fang Shu led the army and his merit was sung in the Zhou "Minor Odes";
translations.idiomatic: I have heard how Fang Shu took command and had his triumph sung in the Zhou "Minor Odes";

sentences.zh: 去病耀武，勛勒燕山，則萬里折沖，在於擇將。

translations.literal: Huo Qubing displayed martial glory and carved his feats on Mount Yan—thus to repel the foe a thousand li away depends upon choosing the right general.
translations.idiomatic: how Huo Qubing flashed his martial glory and carved his deeds on Mount Yan. To break the enemy a thousand li away depends on choosing the right commander.

sentences.zh: 《春秋》謀元帥，取其說《禮樂》、敦《詩書》。

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn Annals say that in selecting a commander-in-chief, one should choose one versed in the Rites and Music and steeped in the Odes and Documents.
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn Annals teach that in choosing a commander one should seek a man learned in the Rites and Music and steeped in the Odes and Documents.

sentences.zh: 晉臣杜預，射不穿劄，而建平吳之勛，是知中權制謀，不在一夫之勇。

translations.literal: The Jin minister Du Yu could not pierce a leaf with his arrow, yet he achieved the conquest of Wu—thus central command and strategy do not rest on the bravery of a single man.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin minister Du Yu could not pierce a leaf with his bow, yet he conquered Wu. Supreme command rests on strategy, not on one man's courage.

sentences.zh: 其蕃將沙咤忠義等身雖驍悍，誌無遠圖，此乃騎將之材，本不可當大任。

translations.literal: Though frontier generals such as Shacha Zhongyi are personally fierce and bold, they lack far-reaching vision; they are cavalry commanders by nature and cannot properly bear heavy responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier generals like Shacha Zhongyi may be personally fierce, but they lack far-sighted design. They are horsemen by trade and should not be entrusted with supreme command.

sentences.zh: 且師出以律，將軍死綏。

translations.literal: Moreover, when the army marches, it must obey discipline; the general dies holding the line.
translations.idiomatic: When armies march, discipline is law; a general dies holding his ground.

sentences.zh: 秦克長平，趙括受戮；

translations.literal: When Qin took Changping, Zhao Kuo was put to death;
translations.idiomatic: When Qin took Changping, Zhao Kuo was executed;

sentences.zh: 胡去馬邑，王恢坐誅，則棄軍有刑，古之常典。

translations.literal: when the Xiongnu withdrew from Mayi, Wang Hui was executed upon conviction—abandoning the army carries punishment; such is the ancient constant rule.
translations.idiomatic: when the Xiongnu slipped away from Mayi, Wang Hui paid with his life. Desertion of the army is a capital crime—such has always been the law.

sentences.zh: 近者鳴沙之役，主將先逃，輕挫國威，須正邦憲。

translations.literal: Recently at the Battle of Mingsha the commanding general fled first, lightly damaging national prestige— the laws of the realm must be upheld.
translations.idiomatic: At Mingsha the commander fled first and lightly shamed the realm. The law must be enforced.

sentences.zh: 又其中軍既敗，陳亂矢窮，義勇之士，猶能死戰，功合紀錄，以勸戎行，賞罰既明，將士盡節，此擒敵之術也。

translations.literal: When the central army was defeated, ranks in disarray and arrows spent, brave men still fought to the death—such deeds merit record and reward to encourage the troops; when rewards and punishments are clear, officers and soldiers will give their utmost—this is the art of capturing the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: When the center broke, ranks tangled and quivers empty, brave men still fought to the death. Such deeds deserve record and reward to steel the ranks. Where reward and punishment are clear, officers and soldiers will stand firm—this is how enemies are taken.

sentences.zh: 臣聞以蠻夷攻蠻夷，中國之長算。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that using barbarians to attack barbarians is a time-honored stratagem of China.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that setting barbarian against barbarian is China's oldest stratagem.

sentences.zh: 故陳湯統西域而郅支滅，常惠用烏孫而匈奴敗。

translations.literal: Thus Chen Tang commanded the Western Regions and Zhizhi perished; Chang Hui employed the Wusun and the Xiongnu were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Tang led the Western Regions and Zhizhi fell; Chang Hui wielded the Wusun and the Xiongnu were broken.

sentences.zh: 請購辯勇之士，班、傅之儔，旁結諸蕃，與圖攻取，此又掎角之勢也。

translations.literal: I beg that eloquent and brave men, peers of Ban and Fu, be recruited to ally with neighboring tribes in a joint campaign—this would create a pincer force.
translations.idiomatic: Recruit eloquent and daring men—peers of Ban Chao and Fu Jiezi—to bind neighboring tribes in joint attack. That would give us a pincer.

sentences.zh: 臣聞昔置新秦以實塞下，宜因古法，募人徙邊，選其勝兵，免其行役，次廬伍，明教令，則狃習戎事，究識夷情，其所虜獲，因而賞之。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that in antiquity Xinqin was established to populate the frontier; we should follow the ancient method, recruit settlers for the border, select their best fighters, exempt them from corvée, organize them in military units, set clear regulations—thus they grow habituated to warfare and thoroughly know barbarian ways, and whatever they capture in raids shall be their reward.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity Xinqin was founded to fill the frontier. Follow that ancient way: recruit settlers for the border, choose their strongest men, free them from corvée, array them in units under clear command. Let them grow used to war and learn the ways of the steppe; whatever they capture in raid shall be theirs.

sentences.zh: 近戰則守家，遠戰則利貨，趨赴鋒鏑，不勞訓誓，朝賦「楊柳」，夕歌《杕杜》，十年之後，可以久安。

translations.literal: Fighting close to home they guard their households; fighting far they profit from loot—rushing to the clash of blades without needing repeated drill; morning levies of "Yangliu," evening songs of "Didu"—after ten years, long peace may be secured.
translations.idiomatic: Near home they defend their own hearths; far afield they profit from plunder. They will race to the clash of arms without endless drill—levied at dawn with "Yangliu," singing "Didu" by dusk. In ten years the frontier may know lasting peace.

sentences.zh: 臣聞漢拜郅都，匈奴避境；

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that when Han appointed Zhe Du, the Xiongnu avoided his territory;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that when Han made Zhe Du prefect, the Xiongnu shunned his border;

sentences.zh: 趙命李牧，林胡遠竄。

translations.literal: when Zhao commissioned Li Mu, the Linhu fled far away.
translations.idiomatic: when Zhao gave Li Mu command, the Linhu fled to the ends of the earth.

sentences.zh: 則朔方之安危，邊城之勝負，地方千里，制在一賢。

translations.literal: Thus the security of Shuofang, victory or defeat at the frontier fortresses—a thousand li of territory—rests upon one worthy man.
translations.idiomatic: The safety of Shuofang, victory or defeat along a thousand li of wall—all hangs on one worthy man.

sentences.zh: 其邊州刺史不可不慎擇，得其人而任之。

translations.literal: Frontier prefects must be chosen with the utmost care, and the right men entrusted with office.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier prefects must be chosen with the greatest care and the right men given authority.

sentences.zh: 蒐乘訓兵，屯田積粟，謹設烽燧，精飾戈矛，來則懲而禦之，去則備而守之，此又古之善經也。

translations.literal: Gather chariots, drill troops, establish garrison farms and store grain, carefully set beacon towers, finely maintain weapons—when they come, punish and repel them; when they go, prepare and defend—this too is an excellent ancient policy.
translations.idiomatic: Muster chariots, drill soldiers, farm the garrisons and fill the granaries, man the beacon towers, sharpen the spears. When the enemy comes, strike and drive him off; when he goes, stand ready. This too is the ancient way.

sentences.zh: 去歲亢陽，天下不稔，利在保境，不可窮兵。

translations.literal: Last year drought afflicted the land and the harvest failed throughout the realm; the advantage lies in securing the borders, not in exhausting the army with campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: Last year's drought ruined the harvest across the realm. The gain lies in holding the border, not in wearing out the army with distant campaigns.

sentences.zh: 使內郡黔黎，各安其業，擇共宰牧，輕其賦徭，事無過舉，爵不以私。

translations.literal: Let the common people of the interior districts each rest secure in their livelihoods; choose upright governors, lighten taxes and corvée, let affairs proceed without excess, and let honors not be granted privately.
translations.idiomatic: Let the people of the interior keep their trades in peace. Choose upright magistrates, lighten taxes and corvée, let government err on the side of restraint, and grant no honors from private favor.

sentences.zh: 愛人之財，節其徭役；

translations.literal: Cherish the people's wealth and limit their corvée;
translations.idiomatic: Treasure the people's goods and limit their labor;

sentences.zh: 惜人之力，不廣臺榭。

translations.literal: spare the people's strength and do not lavishly build terraces and pavilions.
translations.idiomatic: spare their strength and do not raise vast terraces and towers.

sentences.zh: 察地利天時以趨耕獲，命秋狝冬狩以教戰陣。

translations.literal: Observe terrain and seasons to hasten planting and harvest; order autumn hunts and winter drives to teach battle formations.
translations.idiomatic: Read the land and the seasons to speed sowing and reaping; command autumn hunts and winter maneuvers to teach the arts of war.

sentences.zh: 則數年之後，有勇知方，帑藏山積，金革犀利。

translations.literal: Then after several years, there will be courage and knowledge of the proper way, treasury stores piled like mountains, weapons and armor sharp and keen.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years the realm would have warriors brave and disciplined, treasuries heaped high as hills, blades and mail honed to a killing edge.

sentences.zh: 然後整六軍，絕大漠，雷擊萬里，風掃二庭，斬蹛林之酋，懸槁街之邸，使百蠻震怖，五兵載戢，則上合天時，下順人事。

translations.literal: Then one would marshal the six armies, cross the great desert, strike like thunder for ten thousand li, sweep like wind through the two courts, behead the chieftain of Dielin, hang bodies at Gaojie's lodge, make the hundred barbarians tremble in terror, the five weapons all sheathed—then above matching heaven's season, below conforming to human affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Then you would array the six armies, cross the great desert, roll like thunder across ten thousand li and sweep like wind through the twin frontier courts—behead chieftains as Zhou Yafu did at Dielin, display captives at Gaojie as in Han times—until every barbarian people quakes and every blade is stowed again. Heaven's timing above and human will below would at last align.

sentences.zh: 理內以及外，綏近以來遠，以惠中國，以靜四方。

translations.literal: Govern within and extend to the outer, pacify the near to win the far, with bounty for China, with peace for the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Put the inner house in order and reach outward; soothe those near at hand to draw the distant in—nourishing the heartland, stilling the four corners of the earth.

sentences.zh: 臣少慕文儒，不習軍旅，奇正之術，多愧前良，獻替是司，輕陳瞽議。

translations.literal: Your subject from youth admired literary scholars, did not study military affairs; in the arts of regular and irregular deployment, much shamed before past worthies; holding office of advice and censure, lightly offering blind man's counsel.
translations.idiomatic: I have admired the way of letters since youth and never trained in arms. In the arts of orthodox and unorthodox warfare I fall far short of the masters of old. Yet as one charged with remonstrance and replacement, I venture this blind man's counsel.

sentences.zh: 上覽而善之。

translations.literal: The emperor read it and approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read the memorial and was pleased with it.

sentences.zh: 默啜於是殺我行人假鴻臚卿臧思言。

translations.literal: Mochuo thereupon killed our envoy Acting Master of Ceremonies Zang Siyan.
translations.idiomatic: Mochuo then killed our envoy, Acting Master of Ceremonies Zang Siyan.

sentences.zh: 思言對賊不屈節，特贈鴻臚卿，仍命左屯衛大將軍張仁亶攝右御史臺大夫，充朔方道大總管以禦之。

translations.literal: Siyan faced the enemy without yielding his integrity; posthumously granted Master of Ceremonies. Also ordered Left Garrison Guard General Zhang Renbian to act as Vice Censor-in-Chief and serve as Grand Commander of the Shuofang Circuit to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: Siyan had faced the enemy without breaking faith; he was posthumously honored as Master of Ceremonies. The throne also ordered Left Garrison Guard General Zhang Renbian to serve as acting Vice Censor-in-Chief and Grand Commander of the Shuofang Circuit to meet the threat.

sentences.zh: 仁亶始於河外築三受降城，絕其南寇之路。

translations.literal: Renbian first built the three Surrender-Accepting Cities beyond the Yellow River, cutting off their southern raiding route.
translations.idiomatic: Renbian first raised the three Surrender-Accepting Cities south of the river, severing the Turks' path of southern raids.

sentences.zh: 睿宗踐祚，默啜又遣使請和親。

translations.literal: When Ruizong ascended the throne, Mochuo again sent envoys requesting marriage alliance.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruizong took the throne, Mochuo once more sent envoys to ask for a marriage alliance.

sentences.zh: 制以宋王成器女為金山公主許嫁之。

translations.literal: An edict betrothed to him the daughter of Prince of Song Chengqi as Princess Jinshan.
translations.idiomatic: An edict promised him the daughter of Prince of Song Chengqi as Princess Jinshan.

sentences.zh: 默啜乃遣其男楊我支特勒來朝，授右驍衛員外大將軍。

translations.literal: Mochuo then sent his son Yang Wozhi tele to court; appointed External Grand General of the Right Martial Cavaliers.
translations.idiomatic: Mochuo sent his son Yang Wozhi tele to court and had him appointed External Grand General of the Right Martial Cavaliers.

sentences.zh: 俄而睿宗傳位，親竟不成。

translations.literal: Soon Ruizong passed the throne; the marriage alliance was never completed.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Ruizong abdicated, and the marriage was never concluded.

sentences.zh: 初，默啜景雲中率兵西擊娑葛，破滅之。

translations.literal: Initially, in the Jingyun era Mochuo led troops west to attack Suoge and destroyed him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, during the Jingyun reign, Mochuo had marched west against Suoge and wiped him out.

sentences.zh: 契丹及奚，自神功之後，常受其征役，其地東西萬餘里，控弦四十萬，自頡利之後最為強盛。

translations.literal: Khitan and Xi since after the Shendgong era constantly suffered his conscription; his territory extended over ten thousand li east to west, with four hundred thousand bowmen—strongest since Elig.
translations.idiomatic: From the Shendgong era onward the Khitan and Xi had borne his levies and corvée. His domain stretched more than ten thousand li from east to west; he could put four hundred thousand archers in the field—the mightiest Turkic power since Elig Khan.

sentences.zh: 自恃兵威，虐用其眾。

translations.literal: Trusting in military might, he cruelly exploited his people.
translations.idiomatic: Confident in his armies, he drove his people with brutal severity.

sentences.zh: 默啜既老，部落漸多逃散。

translations.literal: When Mochuo grew old, tribes gradually deserted in large numbers.
translations.idiomatic: As Mochuo aged, clans and tribes began to slip away in ever greater numbers.

sentences.zh: 開元二年，遣其子移涅可汗及同俄特勒、妹婿火拔頡利發石阿失畢率精騎圍逼北庭。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaiyuan, sent his son Yinike Khan with Tong'e tele, brother-in-law Hubo-elite-fa Shi Ashibi leading crack cavalry to surround and press Beiting.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 2 he dispatched his son Yinike Khan, together with Tong'e tele and his brother-in-law Hubo-elite-fa Shi Ashibi, at the head of elite horsemen to besiege Beiting.

sentences.zh: 右驍衛將軍郭虔瓘嬰城固守，俄而出兵擒同俄特勒於城下，斬之。

translations.literal: Right Martial Cavalier General Guo Qian'guan held the city in siege defense; soon sallied forth and captured Tong'e tele below the walls, beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Right Martial Cavalier General Guo Qian'guan shut the gates and held the city; then he sallied out, seized Tong'e tele beneath the walls, and executed him.

sentences.zh: 虜因退縮，火拔懼不敢歸，攜其妻來奔，制授左衛大將軍，封燕北郡王，封其妻為金山公主，賜宅一區，奴婢十人，馬十匹，物千段。

translations.literal: The invaders thus retreated; Hubo feared to return, brought his wife and defected; edict appointed Left Guard Grand General, enfeoffed as Prince of Yanbei Commandery, enfeoffed his wife as Princess Jinshan, granted one residence, ten slaves, ten horses, a thousand bolts of goods.
translations.idiomatic: The raiders withdrew. Hubo, afraid to go home, fled to the Tang with his wife. By edict he was made Left Guard Grand General and Prince of Yanbei Commandery; his wife was created Princess Jinshan and given a mansion, ten servants, ten horses, and a thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 明年，十姓部落左廂五咄六啜、右廂五弩失畢五俟斤及子婿高麗莫離支高文簡、睟跌都督崿跌思泰等各率其眾，相繼來降，前後總萬餘帳。

translations.literal: Next year, the ten-surname tribes—left wing Five Tulu Chiefs, right wing Five Nushibi Chiefs, and son-in-law Goguryeo Molizhi Gao Wenjian, Uyghur commander Otu Sitai, etc.—each led their people and submitted in succession, more than ten thousand tents in total.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the chiefs of the Ten Surnames—the five Tulu chiefs of the left wing and the five Nushibi chiefs of the right, along with Mochuo's Goguryeo son-in-law Molizhi Gao Wenjian, the Uyghur commander Otu Sitai, and others—led their followers to surrender one after another, more than ten thousand tents in all.

sentences.zh: 制令居河南之舊地。

translations.literal: Edict ordered them to dwell in their former lands south of the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: An edict settled them on their old grazing grounds south of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 授高文簡左衛員外大將軍，封遼西郡王；

translations.literal: Appointed Gao Wenjian External Grand General of the Left Guard, enfeoffed as Prince of Liaoxi Commandery;
translations.idiomatic: Gao Wenjian was made External Grand General of the Left Guard and Prince of Liaoxi Commandery;

sentences.zh: 睟跌思泰為特進、右衛員外大將軍兼睟跌都督，封樓煩郡公。

translations.literal: Otu Sitai as Special Advancement, External Grand General of the Right Guard and concurrent Uyghur commander, enfeoffed as Duke of Loufan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Otu Sitai was granted Special Advancement, made External Grand General of the Right Guard and concurrent Uyghur commander, and enfeoffed as Duke of Loufan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 自余首領，封拜賜物各有差。

translations.literal: Remaining chieftains received enfeoffments, appointments, and gifts according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: The other leaders received titles, offices, and gifts in due measure.

sentences.zh: 默啜女婿阿史德胡祿，俄又歸朝，授以特進。

translations.literal: Mochuo's son-in-law Ashide Hulu soon also submitted to court, granted Special Advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Mochuo's son-in-law Ashide Hulu soon defected as well and was given the rank of Special Advancement.

sentences.zh: 其秋，默啜與九姓首領阿布思等戰於磧北。

translations.literal: That autumn, Mochuo battled the nine-surname chieftain Abu Si and others north of the desert.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Mochuo fought the Nine Surnames chieftain Abu Si and his allies north of the desert.

sentences.zh: 九姓大潰，人畜多死，阿布思率眾來降。

translations.literal: The nine surnames suffered great rout, many people and livestock died; Abu Si led his people to submit.
translations.idiomatic: The Nine Surnames were shattered; men and herds perished in great numbers, and Abu Si came over with what remained of his people.

sentences.zh: 四年，默啜又北討九姓拔曳固，戰於獨樂河，拔曳固大敗。

translations.literal: Fourth year, Mochuo again marched north against the nine surnames Bayegu, battled at the Dule River; Bayegu suffered great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Mochuo marched north again against the Bayegu of the Nine Surnames and met them on the Dule River; the Bayegu were routed.

sentences.zh: 默啜負勝輕歸，而不設備。

translations.literal: Mochuo, buoyed by victory, returned lightly without making precautions.
translations.idiomatic: Drunk on victory, Mochuo withdrew carelessly and took no precautions.

sentences.zh: 遇拔曳固迸卒頡質略於柳林中，突出擊默啜，斬之。

translations.literal: Encountered Bayegu fugitive soldier Ketuilie in the willow grove; he burst forth and attacked Mochuo, beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: In a grove of willows he ran into Ketuilie, a Bayegu straggler, who sprang out, struck him down, and took his head.

sentences.zh: 便與入蕃使郝靈荃傳默啜首至京師。

translations.literal: Then together with the envoy entering the barbarian lands Hao Lingquan, conveyed Mochuo's head to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He and the envoy to the Turks, Hao Lingquan, then brought Mochuo's head to the capital.

sentences.zh: 骨咄祿之子闕特勒鳩合舊部，殺默啜子小可汗及諸弟並親信略盡，立其兄左賢王默棘連，是為毗伽可汗。

translations.literal: Kutlug's son Köl Tigin gathered the old tribes, killed Mochuo's son the lesser khan and all his brothers and close associates nearly to the last man, installed his elder brother the Left Wise Prince Mojilian—this was Bilge Khan.
translations.idiomatic: Kutlug's son Köl Tigin rallied the old clans, slaughtered Mochuo's son the lesser khan along with his brothers and trusted men almost to the last, and set up his elder brother, the Left Wise Prince Mojilian, as Bilge Khan.

sentences.zh: 毗伽可汗以開元四年即位，本蕃號為小殺。

translations.literal: Bilge Khan ascended in Kaiyuan fourth year; in his own realm he was called Xiaosha.
translations.idiomatic: Bilge Khan took power in Kaiyuan 4; among his own people he was known as Xiaosha.

sentences.zh: 性仁友，自以得國是闕特勒之功，固讓之。

translations.literal: By nature benevolent and friendly; believing he owed the realm to Köl Tigin's merit, he firmly offered to yield.
translations.idiomatic: Mild and loyal by temperament, he held that the throne was Köl Tigin's due and pressed him to accept it.

sentences.zh: 闕特勒不受，遂以為左賢王，專掌兵馬。

translations.literal: Köl Tigin did not accept; he was made Left Wise Prince, exclusively in charge of troops and horses.
translations.idiomatic: Köl Tigin refused. He was made Left Wise Prince instead and given sole command of the armies.

sentences.zh: 是時奚、契丹相率款塞，突騎施蘇祿自立為可汗，突厥部落頗多攜貳，乃召默啜時衙官暾欲谷為謀主。

translations.literal: At this time Xi and Khitan in succession came to the border to submit; Turgesh Suluk proclaimed himself khan; many Turkic tribes wavered; he summoned Mochuo's former court official Tonyukuk as chief strategist.
translations.idiomatic: About then the Xi and Khitan were submitting at the frontier in numbers, Suluk of the Turgesh had declared himself khan, and many Turkic tribes were wavering. Xiaosha recalled Tonyukuk, a court officer from Mochuo's day, to serve as his chief adviser.

sentences.zh: 初，默啜下衙官盡為闕特勒所殺，暾欲谷以女為小殺可敦，遂免死。

translations.literal: Initially all Mochuo's lower court officials were killed by Köl Tigin; Tonyukuk by giving his daughter as Xiaosha's khatun escaped death.
translations.idiomatic: When Köl Tigin had first seized power he had put Mochuo's lesser court officers to the sword; Tonyukuk alone survived because his daughter became Xiaosha's khatun.

sentences.zh: 廢歸部落，乃復用，年已七十餘，蕃人甚敬伏之。

translations.literal: Sent back to his tribe in disgrace, then reemployed; already over seventy years old; barbarians greatly respected and submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Dismissed and sent back to his clan, he was later brought into service again. He was already past seventy, and the steppe peoples revered him deeply.

sentences.zh: 俄而降戶阿悉爛、睟跌思泰等復自河曲叛歸。

translations.literal: Soon surrendered households Ashilan, Otu Sitai and others again rebelled from the river bend and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the surrendered tribesmen Ashilan, Otu Sitai, and others broke away from the river bend and went back to the Turks.

sentences.zh: 初，降戶南至單于，左衛大將軍單于副都護張知運，盡收其器仗，令渡河而南，蕃人怨怒。

translations.literal: Initially when surrendered households went south to Chanyu, Left Guard Grand General Chanyu Vice Protector Zhang Zhiyun confiscated all their weapons, ordered them to cross the river south; barbarians resented this in anger.
translations.idiomatic: When the surrendered households had first moved south to Chanyu, Left Guard Grand General and Chanyu Vice Protector Zhang Zhiyun had stripped them of every weapon and driven them across the river. The tribesmen seethed with resentment.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞姜晦為巡邊使，蕃人訴無弓矢。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Jiang Hui as border inspection envoy; barbarians complained they had no bows and arrows.
translations.idiomatic: The censor-in-chief Jiang Hui, touring the frontier as imperial envoy, heard them protest that they had been left without bows or arrows.

sentences.zh: 不得射獵，晦悉給還之。

translations.literal: Unable to hunt; Hui returned them all.
translations.idiomatic: They could not even hunt. Jiang Hui ordered every weapon returned.

sentences.zh: 故有抗敵之具。

translations.literal: Thus they had means to resist the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: And so they once again had the means to fight.

sentences.zh: 張知運既不設備，與降戶戰於青剛嶺，為降戶所敗。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhiyun made no preparations; battled surrendered households at Qinggang Ridge, was defeated by them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhiyun, having made no ready defense, met the defectors at Qinggang Ridge and was beaten.

sentences.zh: 臨陣生擒知運，擬送與突厥。
