translations.literal: In battle captured Zhiyun alive; intended to deliver him to the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: They took him alive on the field and meant to hand him over to the Turks.

sentences.zh: 朔方總管薛納率兵追討之。

translations.literal: Shuofang Commander Xue Na led troops to pursue and punish them.
translations.idiomatic: Shuofang commander Xue Na marched out in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 賊至大斌縣，又為將軍郭知運所擊。

translations.literal: Rebels reached Dabin County, again struck by General Guo Zhiyun.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels reached Dabin County, where General Guo Zhiyun fell upon them.

sentences.zh: 賊眾大潰散，投黑山呼延谷，釋張知運而去。

translations.literal: Rebel masses greatly scattered and fled, threw themselves into Heishan Huyan Valley, released Zhang Zhiyun and departed.
translations.idiomatic: The host broke and scattered into Black Mountain's Huyan Valley, freeing Zhang Zhiyun before they fled.

sentences.zh: 上以張知運喪師，斬之以徇。

translations.literal: Emperor because Zhang Zhiyun lost his army, beheaded him as public example.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Zhang Zhiyun beheaded for losing his command, as a warning to others.

sentences.zh: 小殺既得降戶，謀欲南入為寇。

translations.literal: Xiaosha having gained the surrendered households, planned to invade south as raider.
translations.idiomatic: With the defectors back under his banner, Xiaosha plotted a southern raid.

sentences.zh: 暾欲谷曰：「唐主英武，人和年豐，未有間隙，不可動也。

translations.literal: Tonyukuk said: "The Tang ruler is heroic and martial; the people are at peace and the harvests full; there is no opening—one must not move.
translations.idiomatic: Tonyukuk said, "The Tang emperor is fierce in war; his people are united and the granaries full. There is no seam to exploit—we must not stir.

sentences.zh: 我眾新集，猶尚疲羸，須且息養三數年，始可觀變而舉。」

translations.literal: Our masses are newly gathered and still weak and exhausted; we must rest and nurture them for several years before we can watch for changes and act."
translations.idiomatic: Our clans are only just gathered and still spent. Let us breathe and recover for a few years, then watch how the wind shifts before we strike."

sentences.zh: 小殺又欲修築城壁，造立寺觀。

translations.literal: Xiaosha again wished to build city walls and erect temples and monasteries.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaosha then proposed building walled towns and founding temples.

sentences.zh: 暾欲谷曰：「不可。

translations.literal: Tonyukuk said: "This cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: Tonyukuk said, "That must not be done.

sentences.zh: 突厥人戶寡少，不敵唐家百分之一，所以常能抗拒者，正以隨逐水草，居處無常，射獵為業，又皆習武。

translations.literal: Turkic households are few and scant, not a hundredth part of Tang's numbers; the reason they have always been able to resist is precisely that they follow grass and water, dwell without fixed place, take hunting as their livelihood, and all are practiced in arms.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks are few—hardly one in a hundred compared with Tang. We have held our own only because we roam with the grass and water, keep no fixed abode, live by the bow and the hunt, and every man knows war.

sentences.zh: 強則進兵抄掠，弱則竄伏山林，唐兵雖多，無所施用。

translations.literal: When strong they advance to raid and plunder; when weak they hide in mountain forests; though Tang troops are many, there is nowhere to apply them.
translations.idiomatic: When we are strong we ride out to loot; when we are weak we vanish into the hills. Tang armies may be countless, yet they have nothing to strike.

sentences.zh: 若築城而居，改變舊俗，一朝失利，必將為唐所並。

translations.literal: If we build cities and dwell in them, changing our old customs, once we suffer a setback we will surely be swallowed by Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Build walls and settle down, change the old ways, and the first hard loss will see us devoured by Tang.

sentences.zh: 且寺觀之法，教人仁弱，本非用武爭強之道，不可置也。」

translations.literal: Moreover the law of temples and monasteries teaches men to be gentle and soft; it is fundamentally not the way of using arms to contend for strength—one must not establish them."
translations.idiomatic: And temples teach men to grow soft and mild—that is no path for a people that lives by the sword. Do not raise them."

sentences.zh: 小殺等深然其策。

translations.literal: Xiaosha and the others deeply approved his plan.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaosha and his chiefs were fully persuaded.

sentences.zh: 八年冬，御史大夫王晙俊為朔方大總管，奏請西征拔悉密，東發奚、契丹兩蕃，期以明年秋初，引朔方兵數道俱入，掩突厥衙帳於稽落河上。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, winter, Censor-in-Chief Wang Jun was made Grand Commander of Shuofang; memorialized requesting a western campaign against the Baximi and an eastern mobilization of Xi and Khitan, planning for early autumn of the next year to lead Shuofang forces by several routes together to strike the Turkic court encampment on the Jiluo River.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the eighth year Censor-in-Chief Wang Jun became Grand Commander of Shuofang and proposed a western strike against the Baximi while the Xi and Khitan marched from the east, intending that early the next autumn Shuofang troops would converge by several routes and fall on the Turkic royal camp at the Jiluo River.

sentences.zh: 小殺聞之，大恐。

translations.literal: Xiaosha heard this and was greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaosha heard of the plan he was deeply alarmed.

sentences.zh: 暾欲谷曰：「拔悉密今在北庭，與兩蕃東、西相去極遠，勢必不合。

translations.literal: Tonyukuk said: "The Baximi are now at Beiting, extremely far from the two tribes east and west—they surely cannot coordinate.
translations.idiomatic: Tonyukuk said, "The Baximi hold Beiting now, far from both eastern and western allies—they cannot possibly join forces.

sentences.zh: 王晙兵馬，計亦無能至此。

translations.literal: Wang Jun's troops, calculated, also cannot reach here.
translations.idiomatic: And Wang Jun's army, by any reckoning, cannot come this far.

sentences.zh: 必若能來，候其臨到，即移衙帳向北三日，唐兵糧盡，自然去矣。

translations.literal: If they truly can come, when they are about to arrive, simply move the court encampment north for three days; Tang troops' provisions exhausted, they will naturally leave.
translations.idiomatic: Even if they do come, wait until they are near, then shift the royal camp three days' ride to the north. When Tang grain runs out they will withdraw of themselves.

sentences.zh: 且拔悉密輕而好利，聞命必是先來，王晙與張嘉貞不協，奏請有所不愜，必不敢動。

translations.literal: Moreover the Baximi are light and greedy for profit; hearing the order they will surely come first. Wang Jun and Zhang Jiazhen are not in harmony; if the memorial request is not to his liking, he will surely not move.
translations.idiomatic: The Baximi are rash and greedy—they will hurry ahead at the first word. Wang Jun and Zhang Jiazhen are at odds; if the court does not grant Wang Jun what he wants, he will not march.

sentences.zh: 若王晙兵馬不來，拔悉密獨至，即須擊取之，勢易為也！」

translations.literal: If Wang Jun's troops do not come and the Baximi come alone, then we must strike and take them—the situation will be easy!"
translations.idiomatic: If Wang Jun stays home and only the Baximi appear, we need only crush them—that will be easy work!"

sentences.zh: 九年秋，拔悉密果臨突厥衙帳，而王晙兵及兩蕃不至。

translations.literal: Ninth year autumn, the Baximi indeed approached the Turkic court encampment, but Wang Jun's troops and the two tribes did not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the ninth year the Baximi did reach the Turkic camp, but Wang Jun's army and the two allied peoples never came.

sentences.zh: 拔悉密懼而引退。

translations.literal: The Baximi feared and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The Baximi, afraid, pulled back.

sentences.zh: 突厥欲擊之，暾欲谷曰：「此眾去家千里，必將死戰，未可擊也，不如以兵躡之。」

translations.literal: The Turks wished to strike them; Tonyukuk said: "These masses are a thousand li from home—they will surely fight to the death; one must not attack them; better to follow with troops."
translations.idiomatic: The Turks wanted to give chase. Tonyukuk said, "Those men are a thousand li from home and will sell their lives dearly—do not meet them head-on. Trail them instead."

sentences.zh: 去北庭二百里，暾欲谷分兵間道先掩北庭，因縱卒擊拔悉密之還眾。

translations.literal: Two hundred li from Beiting, Tonyukuk divided troops by hidden routes to strike Beiting first, then released soldiers to attack the Baximi returning masses.
translations.idiomatic: Two hundred li from Beiting he split his force, sent detachments by hidden paths to seize Beiting first, then loosed his riders on the retreating Baximi.

sentences.zh: 遂散走投北庭，而城陷不得入，盡為突厥所擒，並虜其男女而還。

translations.literal: They scattered and fled toward Beiting, but the city fell and they could not enter; all were captured by the Turks, who also carried off their men and women on the return.
translations.idiomatic: The Baximi broke and ran for Beiting, but the city had already fallen and the gates were shut; the Turks took them all, men and women together, and drove them home.

sentences.zh: 暾欲谷回兵，因而出赤亭以掠涼州羊馬。

translations.literal: Tonyukuk turned his army and then issued from Chiting to plunder Liangzhou's sheep and horses.
translations.idiomatic: Tonyukuk wheeled about and came out through Chiting to loot sheep and horses in Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 時楊敬述為涼州都督，遣副將盧公利、判官元澄，出兵邀擊之。

translations.literal: At that time Yang Jingshu was Liangzhou Protector-General; sent Vice General Lu Gongli and aide Yuan Cheng to lead troops and intercept them.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jingshu was then Protector-General of Liangzhou; he sent Vice General Lu Gongli and staff officer Yuan Cheng to intercept the raiders.

sentences.zh: 暾欲谷曰：「敬述若守城自固，即與連和；

translations.literal: Tonyukuk said: "If Jingshu holds the city and stays firm, then make alliance with him;
translations.idiomatic: Tonyukuk said, "If Jingshu shuts the walls and holds fast, treat with him;

sentences.zh: 若出兵相當，即須決戰。

translations.literal: if he sends troops to meet us, then we must fight a decisive battle.
translations.idiomatic: if he comes out to fight, we must break him in open battle.

sentences.zh: 我今乘勝，必有功矣！」

translations.literal: I now ride on victory—there will surely be achievement!"
translations.idiomatic: We ride on victory now—how can we fail?"

sentences.zh: 公利等兵至刪丹，遇賊，元澄令兵士揎臂持滿，仍急結其袖，會風雪凍烈，盡墜弓矢。

translations.literal: Gongli and the others' troops reached Shandan; encountered the enemy; Yuan Cheng ordered soldiers to bare arms and draw bows full, then quickly tied their sleeves; meeting wind and snow bitterly cold, all dropped bows and arrows.
translations.idiomatic: When Gongli's men reached Shandan they met the enemy. Yuan Cheng had the soldiers roll up their sleeves, draw their bows to the full, and then bind their sleeves tight—but a biting wind and snow froze them stiff, and bowstrings and arrows fell useless to the ground.

sentences.zh: 由是官軍大敗，元澄脫身而走。

translations.literal: Because of this the government army suffered great defeat; Yuan Cheng escaped by himself.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang force was routed; Yuan Cheng alone got away.

sentences.zh: 敬述坐削除官爵，白衣檢校涼州事。

translations.literal: Jingshu was punished by removal of office and rank, serving Liangzhou affairs in plain clothes under probation.
translations.idiomatic: Jingshu was stripped of rank and title and left to manage Liangzhou in plain clothes under probation.

sentences.zh: 小殺由是大振，盡有默啜之眾。

translations.literal: Xiaosha thereby greatly flourished, fully possessing Mochuo's masses.
translations.idiomatic: From that day Xiaosha's power surged until he held all the strength Mochuo had once commanded.

sentences.zh: 俄又遣使請和，乞與玄宗為子，上許之。

translations.literal: Soon again sent envoys requesting peace, begging to become son to Emperor Xuanzong; the emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: He soon sent envoys again to sue for peace, asking to be received as the emperor's adopted son, and Xuanzong agreed.

sentences.zh: 仍請尚公主，上但厚賜而遣之。

translations.literal: Also requested marriage with a princess; the emperor only gave rich gifts and sent them away.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked for an imperial princess in marriage; the court granted lavish gifts but sent him away without a bride.

sentences.zh: 十三年，玄宗將東巡，中書令張說謀欲加兵以備突厥。

translations.literal: Thirteenth year, Emperor Xuanzong was about to tour the east; Chief Minister Zhang Yue planned to increase troops to guard against the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, as Xuanzong prepared to tour the east, Chief Minister Zhang Yue wanted to reinforce the borders against the Turks.

sentences.zh: 兵部郎中裴光庭曰：「封禪者，告成之事，忽此征發，豈非名實相乖？」

translations.literal: Bureau of Military Affairs Director Pei Guangting said: "The feng and shan rites are ceremonies of completed achievement—suddenly launching this mobilization, is it not a mismatch of name and reality?"
translations.idiomatic: Pei Guangting, director in the Bureau of Military Affairs, said, "The feng and shan are rites of perfected peace—why summon armies now and make the deed contradict the word?"

sentences.zh: 說曰：「突厥比雖請和，獸心難測。

translations.literal: Yue said: "The Turks though recently requesting peace—the heart of a beast is hard to measure.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yue replied, "The Turks may talk peace, but a wolf's heart is never sure.

sentences.zh: 且小殺者仁而愛人，眾為之用；

translations.literal: Moreover Xiaosha is benevolent and cherishes men; the masses act for him;
translations.idiomatic: Xiaosha is humane and wins men's loyalty;

sentences.zh: 闕特勒驍武善戰，所向無前；

translations.literal: Köl Tigin is fierce and martial, good at battle, wherever he goes none precedes him;
translations.idiomatic: Köl Tigin is a peerless fighter, unstoppable wherever he rides;

sentences.zh: 暾欲谷深沈有謀，老而益智，李靖、徐勣之流也。

translations.literal: Tonyukuk is deep and reserved with stratagems; old yet growing in wisdom—men of the Li Jing and Xu Ji type.
translations.idiomatic: Tonyukuk is deep, patient, and cunning—still sharpening with age, a match for Li Jing or Xu Ji.

sentences.zh: 三虜協心，動無遺策，知我舉國東巡，萬一窺邊，何以禦之？」

translations.literal: These three barbarians united in heart, moving without leftover stratagem—knowing our whole realm tours east, if by chance they spy the border, how shall we resist them?"
translations.idiomatic: Three such leaders, of one mind and leaving no plan unused—if they see the whole empire marching east, what will stop them from testing the frontier?"

sentences.zh: 光庭請遣使征其大臣扈從，則突厥不敢不從，又亦難為舉動。

translations.literal: Guangting requested sending envoys to summon their great ministers to attend in retinue—then the Turks would not dare refuse, and it would also be hard for them to make any move.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Guangting proposed summoning their senior ministers to attend the emperor in person—the Turks would hardly refuse, and they would find it hard to stir abroad.

sentences.zh: 說然其言，乃遣中書直省袁振攝鴻臚卿，往突厥以告其意。

translations.literal: Yue approved his words; then sent Secretariat Direct Office Yuan Zhen acting Master of Ceremonies to the Turks to announce the intention.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yue accepted the idea and dispatched Yuan Zhen of the Secretariat Direct Office, acting as Master of Ceremonies, to lay the matter before the khan.

sentences.zh: 小殺與其妻及闕特勒、暾欲谷等環坐帳中設宴，謂振曰：「吐蕃狗種，唐國與之為婚；

translations.literal: Xiaosha with his wife and Köl Tigin, Tonyukuk and others sat in a ring in the tent feasting; said to Zhen: "Tibetan dog-breed—Tang marries daughters to them;
translations.idiomatic: Xiaosha, his wife, Köl Tigin, Tonyukuk, and the rest feasted in a circle within the tent and said to Yuan Zhen, "The Tibetans are a dog pack, yet Tang gives them brides;

sentences.zh: 奚及契丹，舊是突厥之奴，亦尚唐家公主；

translations.literal: Xi and Khitan, formerly slaves of the Turks, also marry Tang princesses;
translations.idiomatic: the Xi and Khitan were once Turkic slaves, yet they too receive Tang princesses;

sentences.zh: 突厥前後請結和親，獨不蒙許，何也？」

translations.literal: the Turks repeatedly request marriage alliance, alone not granted permission—why?"
translations.idiomatic: we Turks have asked again and again for a marriage alliance, and alone among them we are refused—why?"

sentences.zh: 袁振曰：「可汗既與皇帝為子，父子豈合為婚姻？」

translations.literal: Yuan Zhen said: "The khan is already son to the emperor—how can father and son also become marriage kin?"
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zhen said, "You are already the emperor's adopted son—can father and son also marry?"

sentences.zh: 小殺等曰：「兩蕃亦蒙賜姓，猶得尚主，但依此例，有何不可？

translations.literal: Xiaosha and the others said: "The two tribes also received bestowed surnames, yet could marry princesses—following that precedent, what cannot be done?
translations.idiomatic: They answered, "Those two peoples were granted imperial surnames and still received princesses—by that precedent, what is impossible?

sentences.zh: 且聞入蕃公主，皆非天子之女，今之所求，豈問真假，頻請不得，實亦羞見諸蕃。」

translations.literal: Moreover I hear princesses sent to the barbarians are none the emperor's own daughters—what we seek now, why ask true or false? Repeated requests denied—we are truly shamed before the other tribes."
translations.idiomatic: Besides, the princesses sent beyond the frontier are seldom the emperor's own daughters. What we ask for now—does it matter whether the bride is royal blood? To be refused again and again is shame we cannot show the other peoples."

sentences.zh: 振許為奏請。

translations.literal: Zhen promised to memorialize the request.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zhen promised to submit the request to the throne.

sentences.zh: 小殺乃遣其大臣阿史德頡利發入朝貢獻，因扈從東巡。

translations.literal: Xiaosha then sent his great minister Ashide-elite-fa to enter court with tribute, and thereby attend the eastern tour in retinue.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaosha then dispatched his senior minister Ashide-elite-fa to the capital with tribute, and so to accompany the emperor on the eastern progress.

sentences.zh: 玄宗發都，至嘉會頓，引頡利發及諸蕃酋長入仗，仍與之弓箭。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong set out from the capital; reaching Jiahui Station, he brought Ashina Defa and the chieftains of the various frontier peoples into the imperial guard formation and also gave them bows and arrows.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong left the capital and reached Jiahui Station on his eastern tour, he had Ashina Defa and the chieftains of the various subject peoples enter the imperial escort and handed them bows and arrows.

sentences.zh: 時有兔起於御馬之前，上引弓傍射，一發獲之。

translations.literal: At that time a hare sprang up before the emperor's horse; the emperor drew his bow and shot sideways, bringing it down with one arrow.
translations.idiomatic: A hare suddenly bolted from in front of the imperial horse. The emperor strung his bow, fired a shot on the move, and dropped it with a single arrow.

sentences.zh: 頡利發便下嘛捧兔蹈舞曰：「聖人神武超絕，若天上則不知，人間無也。」

translations.literal: Ashina Defa immediately dismounted, held up the rabbit, and danced, saying: "The sage's divine martial prowess is beyond all measure—if he is in heaven I cannot say, but among men there is none."
translations.idiomatic: Ashina Defa at once dismounted, held up the rabbit in both hands, and danced as he cried: "Your sacred might surpasses all bounds. Whether you belong to heaven I cannot know—but among men there is none like you."

sentences.zh: 上因令問饑否。

translations.literal: The emperor therefore had someone ask whether they were hungry.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then asked whether they were hungry.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「仰觀聖武如此．十日不食，猶為飽也！」

translations.literal: He replied: "Looking up at such sacred martial prowess, even ten days without eating would still count as having eaten one's fill!"
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "Having seen such sacred prowess, even if I went ten days without food I would still feel sated!"

sentences.zh: 自是常令突厥入仗馳射。

translations.literal: From then on the Turks were regularly permitted to enter the guard formation for mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: From that time the Turks were regularly allowed into the imperial escort to ride and shoot.

sentences.zh: 起居舍人呂向上疏曰：

translations.literal: Court diarist Lü Xiang submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: The court diarist Lü Xiang submitted a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 臣聞鴟梟不鳴，未為瑞鳥，猛虎雖伏，豈齊仁獸，是由醜性毒行，久務常積故也。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that when the owl-falcon does not cry, it is not yet an auspicious bird; though the fierce tiger lies hidden, how can it be ranked with benevolent beasts—this is because vicious nature and poisonous conduct are things long pursued and constantly accumulated.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard it said that an owl is no bird of good omen simply because it keeps silent, and a crouching tiger is no gentle beast. Fierce nature and savage habits are not acquired in a day—they are the harvest of long cultivation.

sentences.zh: 今夫突厥者，正與此類，安忍殘賊，莫顧君親！

translations.literal: Now the Turks are exactly of this sort—how they endure cruelty and slaughter, caring nothing for ruler or kin!
translations.idiomatic: The Turks are precisely of this kind: cruel, ruthless, and heedless of sovereign or family.

sentences.zh: 陛下持武義臨之，修文德來之，既懾威靈，又沐聲教；

translations.literal: Your Majesty with martial righteousness has confronted them and cultivated civil virtue to draw them in; they have both been awed by your majesty and bathed in your transforming influence;
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has met them with armed righteousness and drawn them in with civil virtue. They tremble before your majesty and rejoice in your civilizing influence.

sentences.zh: 以力以勢，不得不庭。

translations.literal: by force and by circumstance they cannot but come to court.
translations.idiomatic: By force and circumstance they have no choice but to attend court.

sentences.zh: 故稽顙稱臣，奔命遣使。

translations.literal: Therefore they bow their foreheads and call themselves subjects, rushing to dispatch envoys.
translations.idiomatic: That is why they kowtow as vassals and hurry to send envoys.

sentences.zh: 陛下乃能收其傾效，雜以從官，赴封禪之禮，參玉帛之會，此德業自盛，固不可名焉。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has yet been able to accept their utmost loyalty, mix them among attendant officials, send them to the feng and shan rites, and have them join the convocation of jade and silk—such virtue and achievement are of themselves full and cannot be named.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has been gracious enough to accept their sworn fealty, mingle them among your attendants, bring them to the feng and shan ceremonies, and seat them at the convocation of jade and silk emissaries. Your virtue and achievement are already beyond words.

sentences.zh: 因復詔許侍遊，召入禁仗。

translations.literal: Yet again an edict permitted them to accompany the tour, summoning them into the inner guard.
translations.idiomatic: You have further granted them leave to join your progresses and summoned them into the inner imperial escort.

sentences.zh: 仰英姿之四照，送神藝之百發，恩意俱極，誠無得逾焉。

translations.literal: They look up to your heroic radiance shining on all sides, witness your divine marksmanship of a hundred hits—the favor and affection have both reached their utmost; truly there is nothing that could surpass this.
translations.idiomatic: They may gaze upon your heroic radiance and watch your uncanny skill of a hundred shots on the mark. Your grace and favor could hardly go further.

sentences.zh: 乃更賜以馳逐，使操弓矢，競飛鏃於前，同獲獸之樂，是屑略太過，未敢取也。

translations.literal: Yet you further bestow on them the chase, letting them wield bow and arrow, competing to fly shafts before the emperor, sharing in the joy of the hunt—this is exceeding courtesy too far; your servant dares not approve it.
translations.idiomatic: To grant them the hunt as well, put bows and arrows in their hands, let them race their shafts before you, and share the joy of the kill—that is indulgence carried too far, and I cannot bring myself to approve it.

sentences.zh: 雖聖胸豁達，與物無猜，而愚心徘徊，與時加栗。

translations.literal: Though the sage's breast is open and without suspicion toward things, your servant's foolish heart hesitates and grows more fearful with the times.
translations.idiomatic: Though Your Majesty's mind is broad and trusts without reserve, my own dull heart wavers and grows more fearful by the day.

sentences.zh: 儻此等各懷犬吠，交肆盜憎，荊卿詭動，何羅竊至，暫逼嚴蹕，稍冒清塵，縱即殪玄方，墟幽土，單于為醢，穹廬為汙，何塞過責？

translations.literal: If these men each harbor dog-like hostility, unleash mutual theft and hatred, plot like Jing Ke with deceptive movement, or steal upon you like He Luo, momentarily pressing upon the imperial procession and slightly befouling the clear dust—even if they were immediately slain in the northern wilds, their lands made desolate, the chanyu turned to mincemeat, and the yurts made filth, how could that atone for the fault?
translations.idiomatic: If among them lurks the spirit of a barking dog, of thieves who turn on one another, of a Jing Ke plotting treacherous violence, or a He Luo stealing up unawares—if they should for a moment press upon the imperial train and stain the royal path—even were they slaughtered to the last man, their lands laid waste, their khans minced to pulp and their yurts trampled into filth, who could answer for the blame?

sentences.zh: 特願陛下勿復親近，使知分限。

translations.literal: Your servant specially wishes Your Majesty not to draw near them again, and to let them know their proper limits.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to keep them at a distance hereafter and make them understand the bounds of their place.

sentences.zh: 待不失常，歸於得所，以謂回兩曜之鑒，祛九宇之憂，孰不幸甚！

translations.literal: To keep them from losing their proper station and see them returned to their proper place—this, it may be said, would turn back the mirror of the two luminaries and dispel the worries of the nine realms—what good fortune could be greater!
translations.idiomatic: To keep all in proper order and each man in his station would restore the clarity of sun and moon and lift the anxieties of the realm under heaven. What blessing could be greater?

sentences.zh: 上納其言，遂令諸蕃先發。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted his words and thereupon ordered the various frontier peoples to depart first.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted the memorial and ordered the foreign chieftains to depart ahead of him.

sentences.zh: 東封回，上為頡利發設宴，厚賜而遣之，竟不許其和親。

translations.literal: Returning from the eastern feng, the emperor held a banquet for Ashina Defa, richly rewarded him, and sent him away; ultimately he did not grant the marriage alliance.
translations.idiomatic: On his return from the eastern feng, the emperor held a banquet for Ashina Defa, lavished gifts upon him, and sent him home—but never granted the marriage alliance he sought.

sentences.zh: 十五年，小殺使其大臣梅錄啜來朝，獻名馬三十匹。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year Xiaosha sent his great minister Meiluo chuo to court, presenting thirty famous horses.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Kaiyuan, Xiaosha sent his chief minister Meiluo chuo to court with a tribute of thirty fine horses.

sentences.zh: 時吐蕃與小殺書，將計議同時入寇，小殺並獻其書。

translations.literal: At that time Tibet wrote to Xiaosha planning a simultaneous invasion; Xiaosha also presented the letter.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet had written to Xiaosha proposing a joint invasion, and Xiaosha turned the letter over to the court as well.

sentences.zh: 上嘉其誠，引梅錄啜宴於紫宸殿，厚加賞賚，仍許於朔方軍西受降城為互市之所，每年賫縑帛數十萬匹就邊以遺之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his sincerity, entertained Meiluo chuo at the Zichen Hall with a banquet, richly rewarded him, and furthermore permitted Shouxiang City west of the Shuofang Army as a place for border markets; every year several hundred thousand bolts of silk were sent to the frontier as gifts to them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his loyalty, feasted Meiluo chuo in the Hall of Purple Dawn, and showered him with gifts. He also designated Shouxiang City, west of the Shuofang Army, as a border market and each year sent several hundred thousand bolts of silk to the frontier as presents for them.

sentences.zh: 二十年，闕特勒死，詔金吾將軍張去逸、都官郎中呂向，賫璽書入蕃吊祭，並為立碑。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year Kül Tigin died; an edict ordered Jinwu General Zhang Quyi and Director of the Office for Review of Punishments Lü Xiang to carry the imperial letter into the foreign land to condole and sacrifice, and also to erect a stele.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year Kül Tigin died. The court dispatched Jinwu General Zhang Quyi and Director of the Office for Review of Punishments Lü Xiang to the steppe with an imperial letter of condolence and orders to set up a memorial stele.

sentences.zh: 上自為碑文，仍立祠廟，刻石為像，四壁畫其戰陣之狀。

translations.literal: The emperor personally composed the stele text, also established a temple shrine, carved stone into his image, and painted the walls on all four sides with scenes of his battle formations.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wrote the inscription himself, established a temple in Kül Tigin's honor, set up a stone image of him, and had the four walls painted with scenes of his battles.

sentences.zh: 二十年，小殺為其大臣梅錄啜所毒，藥發，未死，先討斬梅錄啜，盡滅其黨。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year Xiaosha was poisoned by his minister Meiluo chuo; when the drug took effect, before dying he first moved to behead Meiluo chuo and utterly destroy his faction.
translations.idiomatic: That same year Xiaosha was poisoned by his minister Meiluo chuo. When the poison began to take hold, before he died he struck down Meiluo chuo and exterminated his faction.

sentences.zh: 既卒，國人立其子為伊然可汗。

translations.literal: After he died, the people of the state installed his son as Khan Yiran.
translations.idiomatic: After his death the Turks enthroned his son as Khan Yiran.

sentences.zh: 詔宗正卿李佺往申吊祭，並冊立伊然，為立碑廟。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Director of the Imperial Clan Li Quan to go convey condolences and sacrifices, and also to invest Yiran, establishing stele and temple for him.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent Director of the Imperial Clan Li Quan to offer condolences, invest Yiran as khan, and erect stele and temple in his name.

sentences.zh: 仍令史官起居舍人李融為其碑文。

translations.literal: Li Rong, court diarist among the historiographers, was further ordered to compose his stele text.
translations.idiomatic: The court diarist and historiographer Li Rong was commissioned to write the inscription.

sentences.zh: 無幾，伊然病卒，又立其弟為登利可汗。

translations.literal: Before long Yiran died of illness; his younger brother was again installed as Khan Dengli.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Khan Yiran sickened and died. His younger brother was enthroned as Khan Dengli.

sentences.zh: 登利者，猶華言果報也。

translations.literal: Dengli means, in Chinese parlance, "karmic retribution."
translations.idiomatic: Dengli means, in Chinese, "the fruit of one's deeds."

sentences.zh: 登利年幼，其母即暾欲谷之女，與其小臣飲斯達干奸通，干預國政，不為蕃人所伏。

translations.literal: Dengli was young; his mother was a daughter of Ton Yabghu, and she had an illicit affair with his minor official Yinsi taghan, interfering in state affairs—he was not accepted by the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: Dengli was still a boy. His mother, a daughter of Ton Yabghu, carried on an affair with a petty official named Yinsi taghan and meddled in affairs of state. Neither was respected by the Turks.

sentences.zh: 登利從叔父二人分掌兵馬，在東者號為左殺，在西者號為右殺，其精銳皆分在兩殺之下。

translations.literal: Dengli's two paternal uncles by collateral line divided command of the troops—he in the east was called Left-Sha, he in the west was called Right-Sha; the elite forces were all distributed under the two Sha.
translations.idiomatic: Two of Dengli's uncles divided the armies between them. The one in the east was called Left Sha, the one in the west Right Sha, and the best warriors of the realm were split between them.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，上遣右金吾將軍李質賫璽書，又冊立登利為可汗。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year the emperor sent Right Jinwu General Li Zhi carrying the imperial letter, again investing Dengli as khan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year the emperor sent Right Jinwu General Li Zhi with an imperial letter to invest Dengli once again as khan.

sentences.zh: 俄而登利與其母誘斬西殺，盡並其眾。

translations.literal: Before long Dengli and his mother lured and beheaded West-Sha, wholly absorbing his following.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Dengli and his mother tricked West Sha into an audience and beheaded him, absorbing all his followers.

sentences.zh: 而左殺懼禍及己，勒兵攻登利，殺之。

translations.literal: East-Sha fearing disaster would reach him, mobilized troops to attack Dengli and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: East Sha, fearing he would be next, raised troops against Dengli and killed him.

sentences.zh: 自立，號烏蘇米施可汗。

translations.literal: He installed himself, taking the title Khan Uchumiš.
translations.idiomatic: He then proclaimed himself Khan Uchumiš.

sentences.zh: 左殺又不為國人所附，拔悉密部落起兵擊之。

translations.literal: East-Sha again was not followed by the people of the state; the Basmyl tribe raised troops to strike him.
translations.idiomatic: East Sha won no support from the people. The Basmyl tribe rose against him.

sentences.zh: 左殺大敗，脫身遁走，國中大亂。

translations.literal: East-Sha was greatly defeated, slipped away and fled; the state fell into great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: East Sha suffered a crushing defeat and fled for his life. The realm descended into chaos.

sentences.zh: 西殺妻子及默啜之孫勃德支特勒、毗伽可汗女大洛公主、伊然可汗小妻余塞匐、登利可汗女余燭公主及阿布思頡利發等，並率其部眾相次來降。

translations.literal: West-Sha's wife and children, Mo-ch'o's grandson Tegin Boduzhi, Bilge Kagan's daughter Princess Daluo, Yiran Khan's junior wife Yusafu, Dengli Khan's daughter Princess Yuzhu, Ashina Abusi irkin, and others—all led their tribes in succession to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: West Sha's wife and children; Mo-ch'o's grandson Tegin Boduzhi; Bilge Kagan's daughter, Princess Daluo; Khan Yiran's junior wife Yusafu; Khan Dengli's daughter, Princess Yuzhu; Ashina Abusi irkin; and others led their followers to surrender one after another.

sentences.zh: 天寶元年八月，降虜至京師，上令先謁太廟，仍於殿庭引見，禦華萼樓以宴之，上賦詩以紀其事。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Tianbao, the surrendered captives reached the capital; the emperor ordered them first to visit the imperial ancestral temple, then received them in audience in the palace hall, mounted to the Hua'e Tower to feast them, and composed a poem to record the affair.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the first Tianbao year, the surrendered Turks reached Chang'an. The emperor had them pay homage at the imperial ancestral temple first, then received them in audience, and entertained them from the Hua'e Tower, composing a poem to commemorate the occasion.

sentences.zh: 西突厥本與北突厥同祖。

translations.literal: The Western Turks originally shared the same ancestry as the Northern Turks.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Turks and the Northern Turks sprang from the same line.

sentences.zh: 初，木桿與沙缽略可汗有隙，因分為二。

translations.literal: At first Mughan and Shabo'e Khan had a rift, and therefore they split into two.
translations.idiomatic: Originally Mughan and Khan Shabo'e had quarreled, and the people split into two wings.

sentences.zh: 其國即烏孫之故地，東至突厥國，西至雷翥海，南至疏勒，北至瀚海，在長安北七千里。

translations.literal: Their state was the old land of the Wusun; east to the Turk state, west to Thunder Bird Sea, south to Shule, north to the Vast Sea—seven thousand li north of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Their realm occupied the old Wusun lands, reaching east to the Eastern Turk domains, west to Lake Balkhash, south to Shule, and north to the steppe sea—seven thousand li north of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 自焉耆國西北七日行，至其南庭；

translations.literal: From Yanqi northwest seven days' travel reaches its Southern Court;
translations.idiomatic: From Yanqi, seven days' travel to the northwest brought one to their Southern Court.

sentences.zh: 又正北八日行，至其北庭。

translations.literal: again eight days due north reaches its Northern Court.
translations.idiomatic: Eight more days due north brought one to their Northern Court.

sentences.zh: 鐵勒、龜茲及西域諸胡國，皆歸附之。

translations.literal: Tiele, Kucha, and the various Hu states of the Western Regions all submitted to them.
translations.idiomatic: The Tiele, Kucha, and the other Hu states of the Western Regions all submitted to them.

sentences.zh: 其人雜有都陸及弩失畢、歌邏祿、處月、處密，伊吾等諸種。

translations.literal: Their people mixed included the Dulu, Nushibi, Qarluq, Chumukun, Chumi, Yiwu, and other sorts.
translations.idiomatic: Their population was a mix of Dulu, Nushibi, Qarluq, Chumukun, Chumi, Yiwu, and other tribes.

sentences.zh: 風俗大抵與突厥同，唯言語微差。

translations.literal: Customs were largely the same as the Turks, only the language slightly differed.
translations.idiomatic: Their customs were largely those of the Turks, with only slight differences in speech.

sentences.zh: 其官有葉護，有特勒，常以可汗子弟及宗族為之；

translations.literal: Their offices included yabghu and tegin, usually filled by the khan's sons, brothers, and clan members;
translations.idiomatic: High office included the ranks of yabghu and tegin, usually held by the khan's sons, brothers, and kinsmen.

sentences.zh: 又有乙斤、屈利啜、閻洪達、頡利發、吐屯、俟斤等官，皆代襲其位。

translations.literal: there were also irkin, quriltu, yan hongda, irkinfa, tutun, and irkin offices, all inherited in succession.
translations.idiomatic: There were also the offices of irkin, quriltu, yan hongda, irkinfa, tutun, and irkin, all passing from generation to generation.

sentences.zh: 處羅可汗，隋煬帝大業中與其弟闕達設及特勒大奈入朝。

translations.literal: Niri Khan, in the Daye era of Sui Emperor Yang, entered court with his younger brother Que dazhi and Tegin Dani.
translations.idiomatic: Khan Niri, during Emperor Yang's Daye reign, came to court with his younger brother Que dazhi and Tegin Dani.

sentences.zh: 仍從煬帝征高麗，賜號為曷薩那可汗。

translations.literal: He still followed Emperor Yang's campaign against Goguryeo and was granted the title Yeshana Khan.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied Emperor Yang on the campaign against Goguryeo and was given the title Yeshana Khan.

sentences.zh: 遇江都之亂，從宇文化及至河北。

translations.literal: Encountering the Jiangdu turmoil, he followed Yuwen Huaji to Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jiangdu catastrophe struck, he followed Yuwen Huaji into Hebei.

sentences.zh: 化及敗，歸長安，高祖為之降榻，引與同坐，封歸義郡王。

translations.literal: When Huaji was defeated, he returned to Chang'an; Gaozu lowered his couch for him, drew him to sit together, and enfeoffed him as Prince of Guiyi Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After Huaji's defeat he made his way to Chang'an. Gaozu had a seat lowered in his honor, received him to sit at his side, and enfeoffed him as Prince of Guiyi.

sentences.zh: 獻大珠於高祖。

translations.literal: He presented large pearls to Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: He presented large pearls to Gaozu as tribute.

sentences.zh: 高祖勞之曰：「珠信為寶，朕所重者赤心，珠無所用。」

translations.literal: Gaozu comforted him, saying: "Pearls are indeed treasures, but what I value is a loyal heart—pearls are of no use to me."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu thanked him, saying: "Pearls are indeed precious, but what I value is a loyal heart. Pearls are of no use to me."

sentences.zh: 竟不受之。

translations.literal: In the end he did not accept them.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he declined them.

sentences.zh: 先與始畢有隙，及在京師，始畢遣使請殺之，高祖不許。

translations.literal: He had earlier had a rift with Shibi; when he was in the capital, Shibi sent envoys asking that he be killed, and Gaozu did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: He had long been at odds with Shibi. When he was living in the capital, Shibi sent envoys demanding his death, but Gaozu refused.

sentences.zh: 群臣諫曰：「今若不與，則是存一人而失一國也，後必為患。」

translations.literal: The ministers remonstrated, saying: "If Your Majesty does not grant this now, it means preserving one man and losing one state—later this will surely become a calamity."
translations.idiomatic: His ministers urged: "If you refuse, you will be saving one man at the cost of a whole kingdom. This will surely bring trouble later."

sentences.zh: 太宗曰：「人窮來歸我，殺之不義。」

translations.literal: Taizong said: "A man in desperation came to us; to kill him would be unrighteous."
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said: "This man came to us in his hour of need. To kill him would be unjust."

sentences.zh: 驟諫於高祖，由是遲回者久之。

translations.literal: He repeatedly remonstrated with Gaozu, and thereby Gaozu hesitated for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed the argument again and again, and Gaozu wavered for a long while.

sentences.zh: 不得已，乃引曷薩那於內殿，與之縱酒，既而送至中書省，縱北突厥使殺之。

translations.literal: With no alternative, he then led Yeshana into the inner hall, drank freely with him, afterward sent him to the Secretariat, and let the Northern Turk envoys kill him.
translations.idiomatic: At last, having no alternative, he summoned Yeshana to the inner hall, caroused with him one last time, then had him escorted to the Secretariat and allowed the Northern Turk envoys to kill him.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，令以禮改葬。

translations.literal: When Taizong ascended the throne, he ordered him reburied according to proper rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong came to the throne, he ordered Yeshana reburied with full honors.

sentences.zh: 闕達設初居於會寧，有部落三千余騎。

translations.literal: Que dazhi at first dwelt at Huining, with a tribe of more than three thousand horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: Que dazhi had originally settled at Huining with a following of more than three thousand mounted warriors.

sentences.zh: 至隋末，自稱闕達可汗。

translations.literal: By the end of Sui he styled himself Khan Que da.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of the Sui he proclaimed himself Khan Que da.

sentences.zh: 武德初，遣使內屬，拜吐烏過拔闕可汗，厚加撫慰。

translations.literal: Early in Wude he sent envoys to submit internally; he was appointed Khan Tuwoguo ba Que, and richly comforted and reassured.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Wude reign he sent envoys declaring submission to Tang. He was invested as Khan Tuwoguo ba Que and treated with generous favor.

sentences.zh: 尋為李軌所滅。

translations.literal: Before long he was destroyed by Li Gui.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was destroyed by Li Gui.

sentences.zh: 特勒大奈，隋大業中與曷薩那可汗同歸中國。

translations.literal: Tegin Dani, in the Daye era of Sui returned to China together with Yeshana Khan.
translations.idiomatic: Tegin Dani came to China together with Yeshana Khan during the Sui emperor Yang's Daye reign.

sentences.zh: 及從煬帝討遼東，以功授金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When he followed Emperor Yang's campaign against Liaodong, by merit he was appointed Jinzi Guanglu Dafu.
translations.idiomatic: When he followed Emperor Yang's Liaodong campaign, he was rewarded with the title of Jinzi Glory-Palace Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 後分其部落於樓煩。

translations.literal: Later his tribe was divided and settled at Loufan.
translations.idiomatic: Later his tribe was settled at Loufan.

sentences.zh: 會高祖舉兵，大奈率其眾以從。

translations.literal: When Gaozu raised arms, Dani led his masses to follow.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu rose in arms, Dani led his followers to join him.

sentences.zh: 隋將桑顯和襲義軍於飲馬泉，諸軍多已奔退，大奈將數百騎出顯和後，掩其不備，擊，大破之，諸軍復振。

translations.literal: Sui general Sang Xianhe attacked the Righteous Army at Yinma Spring; many armies had already fled in retreat; Dani led several hundred horsemen out behind Xianhe, took him unawares, struck, and greatly defeated him; the armies recovered their morale.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui general Sang Xianhe struck the Righteous Army at Yinma Spring. Most of the Tang forces had already broken and fled. Dani led several hundred horsemen around behind Xianhe, took him by surprise, and routed him. The army's spirit revived.

sentences.zh: 拜光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He was appointed Guanglu Dafu.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Glory-Palace Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 及平京城，以力戰功，賞物五千段，賜姓史氏。

translations.literal: When the capital was pacified, for fierce combat merit he was rewarded with five thousand bolts of goods and granted the surname Shi.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital was taken, he was rewarded with five thousand bolts of goods for his valor in battle and granted the surname Shi.

sentences.zh: 武德初，從太宗破薛舉。

translations.literal: Early in Wude he followed Taizong in defeating Xue Ju.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Wude reign he followed Taizong in the defeat of Xue Ju.

sentences.zh: 又從平王世充，破竇建德、劉黑闥，並有殊功。

translations.literal: He again followed in pacifying Wang Shichong, defeating Dou Jiande and Liu Heita—all with outstanding merit.
translations.idiomatic: He also helped pacify Wang Shichong and scored notable victories against Dou Jiande and Liu Heita.

sentences.zh: 賜宮女三人，雜彩萬余段。

translations.literal: He was granted three palace women and more than ten thousand bolts of assorted silks.
translations.idiomatic: He was given three palace women and more than ten thousand bolts of colored silk.

sentences.zh: 貞觀三年，累遷右武衛大將軍、檢校豐州都督，封竇國公，實封三百戶。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenguan he was successively promoted to Right Wuwei Grand General, acting military governor of Feng Prefecture, enfeoffed as Duke of Dou State with a fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhenguan he rose to Right Wuwei Grand General and acting military governor of Feng Prefecture, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Dou with a fief of three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 十二年卒，贈輔國大將軍。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he died; posthumously granted Auxiliary State Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twelfth year and was posthumously made Auxiliary State Grand General.

sentences.zh: 初，曷薩那之朝隋也，為煬帝所拘，其國人遂立薩那之叔父，曰射匱可汗。

translations.literal: At first, when Yeshana went to court at Sui, he was detained by Emperor Yang; the people of his state thereupon installed Yeshana's paternal uncle, called Khan Shekui.
translations.idiomatic: When Yeshana had gone to the Sui court, Emperor Yang held him captive. His people thereupon enthroned Yeshana's uncle as Khan Shekui.

sentences.zh: 射匱可汗者，達頭可汗之孫也。

translations.literal: Khan Shekui was a grandson of Khan Datou.
translations.idiomatic: Khan Shekui was a grandson of Khan Datou.

sentences.zh: 既立後，始開土宇，東至金山，西至海，自玉門已西諸國皆役屬之。

translations.literal: After he was installed he first expanded territory; east to Mount Jin, west to the sea—from Yumen westward all states were compelled to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Once enthroned he began to expand his domain east to Mount Jin and west to the sea. From Yumen Gate westward every state bowed to his authority.

sentences.zh: 遂與北突厥為敵，乃建庭於龜茲北三彌山，尋卒。

translations.literal: He then became enemy to the Northern Turks; he established his court at Mount Sanmi north of Kucha, and soon died.
translations.idiomatic: He made an enemy of the Northern Turks, established his court at Mount Sanmi north of Kucha, and soon died.

sentences.zh: 弟統葉護可汗代立。

translations.literal: His younger brother Khan Tong Yehu succeeded in his place.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Tong Yehu succeeded him as khan.

sentences.zh: 統葉護可汗，勇而有謀，善攻戰。

translations.literal: Khan Tong Yehu was brave and possessed stratagem, skilled in attack and battle.
translations.idiomatic: Khan Tong Yehu was brave, shrewd, and masterful in war.

sentences.zh: 遂北並鐵勒，西拒波斯，南接罽賓，悉歸之。

translations.literal: He then north annexed Tiele, west resisted Persia, south connected to Kabul—all submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: He conquered the Tiele to the north, held Persia at bay in the west, and reached south to Kabul. All submitted to him.

sentences.zh: 控弦數十萬，霸有西域，據舊烏孫之地。

translations.literal: He could field several hundred thousand archers, hegemonized the Western Regions, and occupied the old Wusun lands.
translations.idiomatic: He could field several hundred thousand archers, dominated the Western Regions, and held the old Wusun lands.

sentences.zh: 又移庭於石國北之千泉。

translations.literal: He again moved his court to the Thousand Springs north of the Stone Kingdom.
translations.idiomatic: He moved his court to the Thousand Springs north of Sogdiana.

sentences.zh: 其西域諸國王悉授頡利發，並遣吐屯一人監統之，督其征賦。

translations.literal: The kings of the various Western Region states were all appointed irkinfa, and one tutun was dispatched to each to oversee and supervise collection of taxes and levies.
translations.idiomatic: He invested the kings of the Western Regions as irkinfa and sent a tutun to each to supervise taxation and levies.

sentences.zh: 西戎之盛，未之有也。

translations.literal: Such greatness among the Western Rong had never existed before.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Regions had never known such power.

sentences.zh: 武德三年，遣使貢條支巨卵。

translations.literal: In Wude 3 envoys were sent presenting Tiaozhi giant eggs.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Wude he sent envoys presenting giant eggs from Tiaozhi.

sentences.zh: 時北突厥作患，高祖厚加撫結，與之並力以圖北蕃，統葉護許以五年冬。

translations.literal: At that time the Northern Turks were causing trouble; Gaozu richly wooed and allied with him, joining forces to plan against the northern barbarians; Tong Yehu promised the winter of the fifth year.
translations.idiomatic: While the Northern Turks were raiding the frontier, Gaozu courted Tong Yehu warmly and proposed a joint campaign against the northern peoples. Tong Yehu promised to join forces in the winter of the fifth year.

sentences.zh: 大軍將發，頡利可汗聞之，大懼，復與統葉護通和，無相征伐。

translations.literal: When the great army was about to set out, Illig Khan heard of it and was greatly afraid; he again made peace with Tong Yehu, with no mutual campaigning.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tang army was preparing to march, Illig Khan learned of the plan and was terrified. He renewed peace with Tong Yehu, and the two sides ceased hostilities.

sentences.zh: 統葉護尋遣使來請婚。

translations.literal: Tong Yehu soon sent envoys to request a marriage alliance.
translations.idiomatic: Tong Yehu soon sent envoys to ask for a marriage alliance.

sentences.zh: 高祖謂侍臣曰：「西突厥去我懸遠，急疾不相得力，今請婚，其計安在？」

translations.literal: Gaozu said to attendant ministers: "The Western Turks are far from us at opposite ends; in urgent straits they cannot aid each other effectively—now they request marriage; what plan lies behind this?"
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu asked his ministers: "The Western Turks are impossibly far from us. In a crisis they could not help us quickly. Why do they now seek a marriage alliance? What is their aim?"

sentences.zh: 封德彜對曰：「當今之務，莫若遠交而近攻，正可權許其婚，以威北狄。

translations.literal: Feng Deyi replied: "The urgent task of the day is none other than befriending the distant and attacking the near—we may provisionally grant the marriage to overawe the northern Di.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Deyi answered: "Our pressing need is to befriend the distant and strike the near. We should grant the marriage for now, as a threat to the northern barbarians.

sentences.zh: 待之數年後，中國盛全，徐思其宜。」

translations.literal: Wait several years; when China is fully flourishing, then slowly consider what is suitable.
translations.idiomatic: Wait a few years. When the empire is secure and prosperous, we can decide what is truly fitting.

sentences.zh: 高祖遂許之婚，令高平王道立至其國，統葉護大悅。

translations.literal: 」Gaozu thereupon agreed to the marriage, ordered Prince Daoli of Gaoping to go to their realm, and Ishbara was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu then agreed to the marriage and sent Prince Daoli of Gaoping to the Western Turk realm. Ishbara was overjoyed.

sentences.zh: 遇頡利可汗頻歲入寇，西蕃路梗，由是未果為婚。

translations.literal: But Jieli Khan raided in successive years, the routes to the western regions were blocked, and for this reason the marriage was never accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: Jieli Khan raided year after year, cutting the roads to the western regions, and the marriage was never carried through.

sentences.zh: 貞觀元年，遣真珠統俟斤與高平王道立來獻萬釘寶鈿金帶，馬五千匹。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenguan, he sent Zhenzhu Tong Irkin and Prince Daoli of Gaoping to present a gold belt studded with ten thousand gems and five thousand horses.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhenguan, Ishbara sent Zhenzhu Tong Irkin and Prince Daoli of Gaoping with tribute: a gold belt studded with ten thousand gems and five thousand horses.

sentences.zh: 時統葉護自負強盛，無恩於國，部眾鹹怨，歌邏祿種多叛之。

translations.literal: At that time Ishbara relied on his own strength, showed no kindness toward the state, all his tribes resented him, and many of the Qarluk clans rebelled against him.
translations.idiomatic: Ishbara had grown arrogant in his power and showed the court no gratitude. His tribes seethed with resentment, and many Qarluk clans broke away.

sentences.zh: 頡利可汗不悅中國與之和親，數遣兵入寇，又遣人謂統葉護曰：「汝若迎唐家公主，要須經我國中而過。」

translations.literal: Jieli Khan was displeased that China had made peace through marriage, repeatedly sent troops to raid, and also sent someone to tell Ishbara, saying, "If you welcome a Tang princess, she must pass through our territory.
translations.idiomatic: Jieli Khan resented China's marriage alliance and sent raiders year after year. He also sent word to Ishbara: "If you mean to receive a Tang princess, she will have to pass through our lands.

sentences.zh: 統葉護患之，未克婚。

translations.literal: 」Ishbara was troubled by this and could not complete the marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Ishbara was alarmed, and the marriage could not be concluded.

sentences.zh: 為其伯父所殺而自立，是為莫賀咄侯屈利俟毗可汗。

translations.literal: He was killed by his uncle, who seized power for himself; this was Moheduo Hou Quli Sibi Khan.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle killed him and seized the throne for himself, taking the title Moheduo Hou Quli Sibi Khan.

sentences.zh: 太宗聞統葉護之死，甚悼之，遣賫玉帛至其死所祭而焚之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong heard of Ishbara's death, he deeply mourned him and sent jade and silks to the place of his death to offer sacrifice and burn them.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong learned of Ishbara's death, he mourned deeply and sent jade and silk to the place where he had fallen for rites of mourning, which were burned in offering.

sentences.zh: 會其國亂，不果至而止。

translations.literal: But civil strife broke out in the realm, and the envoys never reached their destination and turned back.
translations.idiomatic: Civil strife broke out in the realm, however, and the envoys never completed the journey.

sentences.zh: 莫賀咄侯屈利俟毗可汗，先分統突厥種類為小可汗，及此自稱大可汗，國人不附。

translations.literal: Moheduo Hou Quli Sibi Khan had previously governed Turkic tribes as lesser khans; when he now declared himself great khan, the people of the realm did not submit to him.
translations.idiomatic: Moheduo Hou Quli Sibi Khan had once ruled a Turkic division as a lesser khan. When he now proclaimed himself great khan, the tribes refused to follow him.

sentences.zh: 弩失畢部共推泥孰莫賀設為可汗，泥孰不從。

translations.literal: The Nishibi tribes jointly proposed Nishou Moheshe as khan; Nishou did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The Nishibi tribes together proposed Nishou Moheshe as khan, but Nishou declined.

sentences.zh: 時統葉護之子咥力特勒避莫賀咄之難，亡在康居，泥孰遂迎而立之，是為乙毗缽羅肆葉護可汗。

translations.literal: At that time Ishbara's son Heli Teler, fleeing Moheduo's persecution, had taken refuge in Kangju; Nishou thereupon went to welcome him and enthroned him as Yibi Boluo Siyehu Khan.
translations.idiomatic: Ishbara's son Heli Teler, fleeing Moheduo's persecution, had taken refuge in Kangju. Nishou went to meet him and raised him as Yibi Boluo Siyehu Khan.

sentences.zh: 連兵不息，俱遣使來朝，各請婚於我。

translations.literal: Fighting continued without cease; both sent envoys to court, each requesting marriage with us.
translations.idiomatic: War between them never ceased. Both sides sent envoys to court, each asking for a marriage alliance.

sentences.zh: 太宗答之曰：「汝國擾亂，君臣未定，戰爭不息，何得言婚！」

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong replied, saying, "Your realm is in turmoil, ruler and subject are unsettled, war does not cease—how can you speak of marriage!
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong answered: "Your realm is in chaos. Ruler and subjects are unsettled and war never stops. How can you speak of marriage?

sentences.zh: 竟不許。

translations.literal: 」In the end he did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he refused.

sentences.zh: 仍諷令各保所部，無相征伐。

translations.literal: He also urged them each to hold to their own tribes and refrain from attacking one another.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged both sides to keep to their own tribes and cease fighting one another.

sentences.zh: 其西域諸國及鐵勒先役屬於西突厥者，悉叛之，國內虛耗。

translations.literal: The states of the Western Regions and the Tiele peoples that had formerly been subject to the Western Turks all rebelled against them, and the realm was drained hollow.
translations.idiomatic: The states of the Western Regions and the Tiele peoples who had long served the Western Turks all broke away, leaving the realm hollowed out.

sentences.zh: 肆葉護既是舊主之子，為眾心所歸，其西面都陸可汗及莫賀咄可汗部豪帥，多來附之。

translations.literal: As the son of the former ruler and the focus of popular loyalty, Siyehu drew many tribal chiefs from the western Duluo Khan and from Moheduo Khan's followers to come and attach themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: Siyehu was the son of the former ruler and the man to whom hearts turned. Many chiefs from the western Duluo Khan's following and from Moheduo Khan's tribes came over to him.

sentences.zh: 又興兵以擊莫賀咄，大敗之。

translations.literal: He again raised troops to attack Moheduo and routed him utterly.
translations.idiomatic: He raised troops again to strike Moheduo and routed him completely.

sentences.zh: 莫賀咄遁於金山，尋為咄陸可汗所害，國人乃奉肆葉護為大可汗。

translations.literal: Moheduo fled to Mount Jin; before long he was killed by Dulo Khan, and the people of the realm thereupon upheld Siyehu as great khan.
translations.idiomatic: Moheduo fled to Mount Jin, was soon killed by Dulo Khan, and the tribes then upheld Siyehu as great khan.

sentences.zh: 肆葉護可汗立，大發兵北征鐵勒，薛延陀逆擊之，反為所敗。

translations.literal: When Siyehu Khan took the throne, he mustered a great force to campaign north against the Tiele; the Xueyantuo met him in battle and in turn defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Once Siyehu Khan was enthroned, he mustered a great army to campaign north against the Tiele. The Xueyantuo met him in battle and turned the defeat back on him.

sentences.zh: 肆葉護性猜狠信讒，無統馭之略。

translations.literal: Siyehu was by nature suspicious, fierce, and credulous of slander, with no talent for governing.
translations.idiomatic: Siyehu was suspicious and cruel by nature, quick to believe slander, and lacked any gift for rule.

sentences.zh: 有乙利可汗者，於肆葉護功最多，由是授小可汗，以非罪族滅之。

translations.literal: There was one Yili Khan who had served Siyehu with the greatest merit; for this he was appointed lesser khan, and then, on a charge without merit, his entire clan was executed.
translations.idiomatic: One Yili Khan had done more for Siyehu than any other man and was made lesser khan for it—then, on a groundless charge, Siyehu exterminated his whole clan.

sentences.zh: 群下震駭，莫能自固。

translations.literal: His subordinates were shaken with terror and none could hold his position secure.
translations.idiomatic: His followers were terrified, and no one could feel secure in his place.

sentences.zh: 肆葉護素憚泥孰，而陰欲圖之，泥孰遂適焉耆。

translations.literal: Siyehu had long feared Nishou and secretly plotted against him; Nishou thereupon went to live in Yanqi.
translations.idiomatic: Siyehu had long feared Nishou and secretly plotted against him. Nishou withdrew to Yanqi.

sentences.zh: 其後沒卑達幹與突厥弩失畢二部豪帥潛謀擊之，肆葉護以輕騎遁於康居，尋卒。

translations.literal: Thereafter Meibei Dagan and the chieftains of the two Nishibi tribes secretly plotted to attack him; Siyehu fled to Kangju with a light cavalry escort and soon died.
translations.idiomatic: Later Meibei Dagan and the chiefs of two Nishibi divisions secretly plotted against him. Siyehu fled to Kangju with a small cavalry escort and soon died.

sentences.zh: 國人迎泥孰於焉耆而立之，是為咄陸可汗。

translations.literal: The people of the realm welcomed Nishou from Yanqi and enthroned him; this was Dulo Khan.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes brought Nishou back from Yanqi and enthroned him as Dulo Khan.

sentences.zh: 咄陸可汗泥孰者，亦稱大渡可汗。

translations.literal: Dulo Khan Nishou was also called Great Crossing Khan.
translations.idiomatic: Dulo Khan Nishou was also known as Great Crossing Khan.

sentences.zh: 父莫賀設，本隸統葉護。

translations.literal: His father Moheshe had originally been under Ishbara's command.
translations.idiomatic: His father Moheshe had originally served under Ishbara.

sentences.zh: 武德中，嘗至京師。

translations.literal: During the Wude era he once came to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wude reign he once visited the capital.

sentences.zh: 時太宗居籓，務加懷輯，與之結盟為兄弟。

translations.literal: At that time the future Emperor Taizong held a princely fief; he went out of his way to win Nishou over and swore brotherhood with him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the future Emperor Taizong was still a prince. He went out of his way to win Nishou over and swore brotherhood with him.

sentences.zh: 既被推為可汗，遣使詣闕請降。

translations.literal: Once he had been raised as khan, he sent envoys to court to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Once the tribes had raised him as khan, he sent envoys to court to submit.

sentences.zh: 太宗遣使賜以名號及鼓纛。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong sent envoys granting him a title, drums, and banners.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong sent envoys to invest him with a title and grant him drums and banners.

sentences.zh: 貞觀七年，遣鴻臚少卿劉善因至其國，冊授為吞阿婁拔奚利邲咄陸可汗。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Zhenguan, he dispatched Honglu Vice Minister Liu Shanyin to his realm to invest him as Tenalouba Xili Bing Dulo Khan.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Zhenguan, the court sent Honglu Vice Minister Liu Shanyin to invest him formally as Tenalouba Xili Bing Dulo Khan.

sentences.zh: 明年，泥孰卒，其弟同娥設立，是為沙缽羅咥利失可汗。

translations.literal: The following year Nishou died; his younger brother Tong'e She succeeded him; this was Shaboluo Helilishi Khan.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Nishou died. His younger brother Tong'e She succeeded him as Shaboluo Helilishi Khan.

sentences.zh: 沙缽羅咥利失可汗，以貞觀九年上表請婚，獻馬五百疋。

translations.literal: Shaboluo Helilishi Khan, in the ninth year of Zhenguan, submitted a memorial requesting marriage and presented five hundred horses.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Zhenguan, Shaboluo Helilishi Khan submitted a memorial asking for a marriage alliance and presented five hundred horses.

sentences.zh: 朝廷唯厚加撫慰，未許其婚。

translations.literal: The court only treated him with generous reassurance and did not grant the marriage.
translations.idiomatic: The court treated him generously but did not grant the marriage.

sentences.zh: 俄而其國分為十部，每部令一人統之，號為十設。

translations.literal: Before long his realm was divided into ten divisions, each placed under one man to govern; these were called the ten she.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the realm was divided into ten divisions, each governed by one man and called a she.

sentences.zh: 每設賜以一箭，故稱十箭焉。

translations.literal: Each she was granted one arrow; hence they were called the Ten Arrows.
translations.idiomatic: Each she was given one arrow, and from this they came to be called the Ten Arrows.

sentences.zh: 又分十箭為左右廂，一廂各置五箭。

translations.literal: The Ten Arrows were further split into left and right wings, five arrows to each wing.
translations.idiomatic: The Ten Arrows were then divided into left and right wings, with five arrows in each.

sentences.zh: 其左廂號五咄六部落，置五大啜，一啜管一箭；

translations.literal: The left wing was called the Five Dulu tribes; five great chuo were appointed, each chuo governing one arrow;
translations.idiomatic: The left wing was called the Five Dulu tribes. Five great chuo were appointed, each governing one arrow;

sentences.zh: 其右廂號為五弩失畢，置五大俟斤，一俟斤管一箭，都號為十箭。

translations.literal: the right wing was called the Five Nishibi; five great irkin were appointed, each irkin governing one arrow—all together called the Ten Arrows.
translations.idiomatic: the right wing was called the Five Nishibi. Five great irkin were appointed, each governing one arrow. Together they were known as the Ten Arrows.

sentences.zh: 其後或稱一箭為一部落，大箭頭為大首領。

translations.literal: Later one arrow might be called one tribe, and the head of a major arrow the great chieftain.
translations.idiomatic: Later a single arrow came to mean a tribe, and the holder of a major arrow its great chieftain.

sentences.zh: 五咄六部落居於碎葉已東，五弩失畢部落居於碎葉已西，自是都號為十姓部落。

translations.literal: The Five Dulu tribes lived east of Suyab; the Five Nishibi tribes lived west of Suyab—from this time they were altogether called the Ten Surname Tribes.
translations.idiomatic: The Five Dulu tribes lived east of Suyab and the Five Nishibi west of it. From then on the whole confederation was called the Ten Surname Tribes.

sentences.zh: 咥利失既不為眾所歸，部眾攜貳，為其統吐屯所襲，麾下亡散。

translations.literal: Helilishi won no general allegiance; his tribes grew divided, and he was attacked by his tudun commander Tongtu; his followers scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Helilishi commanded no loyalty. His tribes wavered, his tudun commander Tongtu attacked him, and his followers scattered.

sentences.zh: 咥利失以左右百余騎拒之，戰數合，統吐屯不利而去。

translations.literal: Helilishi met them with a little more than a hundred cavalry on either flank; after several clashes Tongtu gained no advantage and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Helilishi met the attack with barely a hundred horsemen on each flank. After several clashes Tongtu gained nothing and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 咥利失奔其弟步利設，與保焉耆。

translations.literal: Helilishi fled to his younger brother Buli She, and together they held Yanqi.
translations.idiomatic: Helilishi fled to his younger brother Buli She, and together they held Yanqi.

sentences.zh: 其阿悉吉闕俟斤與統吐屯等召國人，將立欲谷設為大可汗。

translations.literal: The Ashijie Que Irkin and Tongtu summoned the people of the realm, intending to install Yugu She as great khan.
translations.idiomatic: The Ashijie Que Irkin and Tongtu summoned the tribes, intending to raise Yugu She as great khan.

sentences.zh: 以咥利失為小可汗。

translations.literal: Helilishi was to be lesser khan.
translations.idiomatic: Helilishi was to serve as lesser khan.

sentences.zh: 統吐屯為人所殺，欲谷設兵又為其俟斤所破，咥利失復得舊地，弩失畢、處密等並歸咥利失。

translations.literal: Tongtu was killed by someone; Yugu She's forces were in turn broken by an irkin; Helilishi recovered his old territory, and the Nishibi, Chumi, and others all returned to him.
translations.idiomatic: Tongtu was killed. Yugu She's army was in turn broken by an irkin. Helilishi recovered his old lands, and the Nishibi, Chumi, and others all returned to him.

sentences.zh: 十二年，西部竟立欲谷設為乙毗咄陸可汗。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year the western tribes at last enthroned Yugu She as Yibi Dulo Khan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year the western tribes at last enthroned Yugu She as Yibi Dulo Khan.

sentences.zh: 乙毗咄陸可汗既立，與咥利失大戰，兩軍多死，各引去。

translations.literal: Once Yibi Dulo Khan was established, he fought a great battle with Helilishi; both armies suffered heavy losses and each side withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yibi Dulo Khan was established, he fought a great battle with Helilishi. Both armies bled heavily and each side pulled back.

sentences.zh: 因與咥利失中分，自伊列河已西屬咄陸，已東屬咥利失。

translations.literal: They then divided the realm between them: from the Ili River west belonged to Dulo; from the river east belonged to Helilishi.
translations.idiomatic: They then split the realm between them: everything west of the Ili River went to Dulo, everything east to Helilishi.

sentences.zh: 咄陸可汗又建庭於鏃曷山西，謂為北庭。

translations.literal: Dulo Khan also established his court west of Mount Zhu'e; this was called the Northern Court.
translations.idiomatic: Dulo Khan also set up his court west of Mount Zhu'e, calling it the Northern Court.

sentences.zh: 自厥越失、拔悉彌、駁馬、結骨、火燅、觸水昆諸國皆臣之。

translations.literal: From Jueyueshi, Boshimi, Boma, Jiegu, Huoxun, and Chushuikun, all the states submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Jueyueshi, Boshimi, Boma, Jiegu, Huoxun, Chushuikun, and the other states all submitted to him.

sentences.zh: 十三年，咥利失為其吐屯俟利發與欲谷設通謀作難，咥利失窮蹙，奔拔汗那而死。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Helilishi's tudun Irli Fa conspired with Yugu She to raise trouble; Helilishi was driven to extremity, fled to Ferghana, and died there.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year Helilishi's tudun Irli Fa conspired with Yugu She against him. Helilishi was cornered, fled to Ferghana, and died there.

sentences.zh: 弩失畢部落酋帥迎咥利失弟伽那之子薄布特勒而立之，是為乙毗沙缽羅葉護可汗。

translations.literal: Nishibi tribal chiefs welcomed Helilishi's brother Gana's son Kebutele and enthroned him; this was Yibi Shaboluo Yabghu Khan.
translations.idiomatic: Nishibi chiefs welcomed Helilishi's brother Gana's son Kebutele and enthroned him as Yibi Shaboluo Yabghu Khan.

sentences.zh: 乙毗沙缽羅葉護可汗既立，建庭於睢合水北，謂之南庭。

translations.literal: Once Yibi Shaboluo Yabghu Khan was established, he set up his court north of the Suihe River; this was called the Southern Court.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yibi Shaboluo Yabghu Khan was established, he set up his court north of the Suihe River and called it the Southern Court.

sentences.zh: 東以伊列河為界，自龜茲、鄯善，且末、吐火羅、焉耆、石國、史國、何國、穆國、康國，皆受其節度。

translations.literal: Eastward the Ili River formed the boundary; from Kucha, Shanshan, Qiemo, Tuhuolo, Yanqi, Chach, Samarkand, Bukhara, Maymurgh, and Kangjiu, all came under his command.
translations.idiomatic: The Ili River marked the eastern boundary. From Kucha and Shanshan to Qiemo, Tuhuolo, Yanqi, Chach, Samarkand, Bukhara, Maymurgh, and Kangjiu—all came under his command.

sentences.zh: 累遣使朝貢，太宗降璽書慰勉。

translations.literal: He repeatedly sent envoys with tribute; Emperor Taizong issued imperial letters of encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys with tribute again and again, and Emperor Taizong answered with imperial letters of encouragement.

sentences.zh: 貞觀十五年，令左領軍將軍張大師往授焉，賜以鼓纛。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Zhenguan he ordered Left Palace Guard General Zhang Dashi to go invest him and granted drums and banners.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Zhenguan the court sent Left Palace Guard General Zhang Dashi to invest him and granted him drums and banners.

sentences.zh: 於時咄陸可汗與葉護頗相攻擊。

translations.literal: At that time Dulo Khan and the Yabghu were frequently striking at one another.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Dulo Khan and the Yabghu were locked in frequent combat.

sentences.zh: 會咄陸遣使詣闕，太宗諭以敦睦之道。

translations.literal: When Dulo sent envoys to court, Emperor Taizong instructed them in the principles of amity.
translations.idiomatic: When Dulo sent envoys to court, Emperor Taizong urged them toward peace.

sentences.zh: 咄陸於時兵眾漸強，西域諸國復來歸附。

translations.literal: Dulo's forces gradually grew stronger, and the states of the Western Regions again submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Dulo's armies grew steadily stronger, and the states of the Western Regions began submitting to him again.

sentences.zh: 未幾，咄陸遣石國吐屯攻葉護，擒之，送於咄陸，尋為所殺。

translations.literal: Before long Dulo sent a Chach tudun to attack the Yabghu, captured him, sent him to Dulo, and soon had him killed.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Dulo sent a Chach tudun to attack the Yabghu, capture him, and deliver him to Dulo, who soon had him killed.

sentences.zh: 咄陸可汗既並其國，弩失畢諸姓心不服咄陸，皆叛之。

translations.literal: Once Dulo Khan had absorbed his realm, the Nishibi clans refused in their hearts to accept Dulo and all rebelled against him.
translations.idiomatic: After Dulo Khan swallowed the Yabghu's realm, the Nishibi clans refused to accept him and rose in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 咄陸復率兵擊吐火羅，破之。

translations.literal: Dulo again led troops against Tuhuolo and defeated it.
translations.idiomatic: Dulo led troops against Tuhuolo again and broke it.

sentences.zh: 自恃其強，專擅西域。

translations.literal: Confident in his strength, he monopolized the Western Regions.
translations.idiomatic: Confident in his power, he claimed the Western Regions for himself alone.

sentences.zh: 遣兵寇伊州，安西都護郭恪率輕騎二千自烏骨邀擊，敗之。

translations.literal: He sent troops to raid Yizhou; Protector-General of Anxi Guo Ke led two thousand light cavalry from Wugu to intercept and defeat them.
translations.idiomatic: He sent troops to raid Yizhou. Protector-General of Anxi Guo Ke led two thousand light cavalry from Wugu to intercept them and won.

sentences.zh: 咄陸又遣處月、處密等圍天山縣，郭恪又擊走之。

translations.literal: Dulo again sent the Chuyue and Chumi to besiege Tianshan County; Guo Ke again drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: Dulo again sent the Chuyue and Chumi to besiege Tianshan County, and Guo Ke drove them off once more.

sentences.zh: 恪乘勝進拔處月俟斤所居之城，追奔及於遏索山，斬首千余級，降其處密之眾而歸。

translations.literal: Guo Ke pressed the victory, stormed the city where the Chuyue irkin lived, pursued the fugitives to Mount Esuo, took more than a thousand heads, and accepted the surrender of the Chumi before returning.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ke pressed the victory, stormed the Chuyue irkin's stronghold, pursued the fugitives to Mount Esuo, took more than a thousand heads, accepted the surrender of the Chumi, and returned.

sentences.zh: 咄陸初以泥孰啜自擅取所部物，斬之以徇；

translations.literal: Dulo had earlier executed the Dulu chuo Nishou for arrogantly taking goods from his tribe as his own and displayed the severed head as a warning;
translations.idiomatic: Dulo had earlier executed a Dulu chuo named Nishou for seizing his tribe's goods on his own authority and displayed the severed head as a warning;

sentences.zh: 尋為泥孰啜部將胡祿居所襲，眾多亡逸，其國大亂。

translations.literal: soon afterward he was struck by Helu Ju, a commander under the Dulu chuo Nishou; many fled, and the realm fell into great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: soon afterward he was attacked by Helu Ju, a commander under that Dulu chuo. Many fled, and the realm fell into chaos.

sentences.zh: 貞觀十五年，部下屋利啜等謀欲廢咄陸，各遣使詣闕，請立可汗。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Zhenguan subordinates including Wuli Chuo plotted to depose Dulo; each sent envoys to court requesting that a khan be installed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Zhenguan, subordinates including Wuli Chuo plotted to depose Dulo. Each faction sent envoys to court asking that a khan be installed.

sentences.zh: 太宗遣使賫璽書立莫賀咄乙毗可汗之子，是為乙毗射匱可汗。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong sent envoys bearing an imperial letter to install the son of Moheduo Yibi Khan; this was Yibi Shekui Khan.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong sent envoys with an imperial letter to install the son of Moheduo Yibi Khan as Yibi Shekui Khan.

sentences.zh: 乙毗射匱可汗立，乃發弩失畢兵就白水擊咄陸。

translations.literal: Once Yibi Shekui Khan was enthroned, he mobilized Nishibi forces at Baishui to strike Dulo.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yibi Shekui Khan was enthroned, he mobilized Nishibi forces at Baishui to attack Dulo.

sentences.zh: 自知不為眾所附，乃西走吐火羅國。

translations.literal: Knowing he commanded no loyalty, Dulo fled west to Tuhuolo.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing he had lost the tribes' support, Dulo fled west to Tuhuolo.

sentences.zh: 中國使人先為咄陸所拘者，射匱悉以禮資送歸長安，復遣使貢方物，請賜婚。

translations.literal: Tang envoys whom Dulo had earlier detained, Shekui courteously escorted back to Chang'an; he again sent envoys bearing tribute and requesting a marriage grant.
translations.idiomatic: Shekui courteously escorted back to Chang'an the Tang envoys Dulo had earlier detained, then sent fresh envoys with tribute and a request for a marriage alliance.

sentences.zh: 太宗許之，詔令割龜茲、於闐、疏勒、硃俱波、蔥嶺等五國為聘禮。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong agreed and decreed that Kucha, Khotan, Kashgar, Shugnan, and the Pamirs—five states—be ceded as betrothal gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong agreed and decreed that Kucha, Khotan, Kashgar, Shugnan, and the Pamirs—five states—be granted as betrothal gifts.

sentences.zh: 及太宗崩，賀魯反叛，射匱部落為其所並。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong died, Helu rebelled and absorbed Shekui's tribes.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Taizong's death, Helu rebelled and swallowed Shekui's tribes.

sentences.zh: 阿史那賀魯者，曳步利設射匱特勒之子也。

translations.literal: Ashina Helu was the son of Yebuli She Shekui Teler.
translations.idiomatic: Ashina Helu was the son of Yebuli She Shekui Teler.

sentences.zh: 初，阿史那步真既來歸國，咄陸可汗乃立賀魯為葉護，以繼步真。

translations.literal: At first, after Ashina Buzhen came to submit to the Tang, Dulo Khan installed Helu as yabghu to succeed Buzhen.
translations.idiomatic: After Ashina Buzhen came over to the Tang, Dulo Khan installed Helu as yabghu to succeed him.

sentences.zh: 居於多邏斯川，在西州直北一千五百里，統處密、處月、姑蘇、歌羅祿、弩失畢五姓之眾。

translations.literal: He dwelt on the Talas River, fifteen hundred li due north of Xizhou, commanding the five surname peoples of Chumi, Chuyue, Gusu, Qarluq, and Nishibi.
translations.idiomatic: He made his seat on the Talas River, fifteen hundred li due north of Xizhou, and ruled the five surname peoples of Chumi, Chuyue, Gusu, Qarluq, and Nishibi.

sentences.zh: 其後，咄陸西走吐火羅國，射匱可汗遣兵迫逐，賀魯不常厥居。

translations.literal: Later, when Dulo fled west to Tuhuolo, Shekui Khan sent troops in pursuit; Helu had no fixed residence.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Dulo fled west to Tuhuolo, Shekui Khan sent troops after him, and Helu had no fixed home.

sentences.zh: 貞觀二十二年，乃率其部落內屬，詔居廷州。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year of Zhenguan he led his tribes to submit; an edict settled them in Tingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year of Zhenguan he led his tribes to submit. An edict settled them in Tingzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋授左驍衛將軍、瑤池都督。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed General of the Left Brave Guards and Military Governor of Yaochi.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed General of the Left Brave Guards and Military Governor of Yaochi.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，進拜左驍衛大將軍，瑤池都督如故。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong took the throne, Helu was promoted to Grand General of the Left Brave Guards, retaining the Yaochi governorship.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong took the throne, Helu was promoted to Grand General of the Left Brave Guards while keeping his post as Military Governor of Yaochi.

sentences.zh: 永徽二年，與其子咥運率眾西遁，據咄陸可汗之地，總有西域諸郡，建牙於雙河及千泉，自號沙缽羅可汗，統攝咄陸、弩失畢十姓。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yonghui he fled west with his son Yiyun, seized Dulo Khan's old lands, controlled the commanderies of the Western Regions, set up his court at Shuanghe and the Thousand Springs, styled himself Shaboluo Khan, and ruled the ten surnames of Dulo and Nishibi.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yonghui he fled west with his son Yiyun, seized Dulo Khan's old lands, took control of the Western Regions, set up his court at Shuanghe and the Thousand Springs, styled himself Shaboluo Khan, and ruled the ten surnames of Dulo and Nishibi.

sentences.zh: 其咄陸有五啜：一曰處木昆律啜；

translations.literal: Among the Dulu there were five chuo: the first was Chumukunlu Chuo;
translations.idiomatic: The Dulu had five chuo. The first was Chumukunlu Chuo;

sentences.zh: 二曰胡祿居闕啜，賀魯以女妻之；

translations.literal: the second was Helu Juque Chuo, whom Helu gave his daughter in marriage;
translations.idiomatic: the second was Helu Juque Chuo, to whom Helu gave his daughter in marriage;

sentences.zh: 三曰攝舍提暾啜；

translations.literal: the third was Shesheti Tun Chuo;
translations.idiomatic: the third was Shesheti Tun Chuo;

sentences.zh: 四曰突騎施賀邏施啜；

translations.literal: the fourth was Tuqishi Heluoshi Chuo;
translations.idiomatic: the fourth was Tuqishi Heluoshi Chuo;

sentences.zh: 五曰鼠尼施處半啜。

translations.literal: the fifth was Shunishi Chuban Chuo.
translations.idiomatic: the fifth was Shunishi Chuban Chuo.

sentences.zh: 弩失畢有五俟斤：一曰阿悉結闕俟斤，最為強盛；

translations.literal: Among the Nishibi there were five irkin: the first was Ashijie Que Irkin, the most powerful of all;
