translations.idiomatic: The Nishibi had five irkin. The first was Ashijie Que Irkin, the strongest of them;

sentences.zh: 二曰哥舒闕俟斤；

translations.literal: the second was Geshu Que Irkin;
translations.idiomatic: the second was Geshu Que Irkin;

sentences.zh: 三曰拔塞幹暾沙缽俟斤，四曰阿悉結泥孰俟斤；

translations.literal: the third was Basagan Tun Shabo Irkin; the fourth was Ashijie Nishou Irkin;
translations.idiomatic: the third was Basagan Tun Shabo Irkin; the fourth was Ashijie Nishou Irkin;

sentences.zh: 五曰哥舒處半俟斤。

translations.literal: the fifth was Geshu Chuban Irkin.
translations.idiomatic: the fifth was Geshu Chuban Irkin.

sentences.zh: 各有所部，勝兵數十萬，並羈屬賀魯。

translations.literal: Each had his own following; their battle-ready forces numbered in the hundreds of thousands, all bound to Helu.
translations.idiomatic: Each commanded his own followers. Their battle-ready forces numbered in the hundreds of thousands, all bound to Helu.

sentences.zh: 西域諸國，亦多附隸焉。

translations.literal: Many states of the Western Regions also attached themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: Many states of the Western Regions attached themselves to him as well.

sentences.zh: 賀魯尋立咥運為莫賀咄葉護，數侵擾西蕃諸部，又進寇廷州。

translations.literal: Helu soon installed Yiyun as Moheduo Yabghu; they repeatedly harassed the western tribes and again advanced to raid Tingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Helu soon installed Yiyun as Moheduo Yabghu. Together they repeatedly harassed the western tribes and again raided Tingzhou.

sentences.zh: 三年，詔遣左武候大將軍梁建方、右驍衛大將軍契苾何力率燕然都護所部回紇兵五萬騎討之，前後斬首五千級，虜渠帥六十余人。

translations.literal: In the third year, an edict ordered Left Martial Guard Grand General Liang Jianfang and Right Xiaowei Grand General Qibi Heli to lead fifty thousand mounted Uyghur troops from the Yanran Protector's command to suppress them. In all they beheaded five thousand and captured more than sixty chieftains.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year an edict dispatched Left Martial Guard Grand General Liang Jianfang and Right Xiaowei Grand General Qibi Heli at the head of fifty thousand Uyghur horsemen from the Yanran Protector's command to suppress Helu. They beheaded five thousand in all and took more than sixty chieftains captive.

sentences.zh: 四年，咄陸可汗死，其子真珠護與五弩失畢請擊賀魯，破其牙帳，斬首千余級。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Dulo Khan died. His son Zhenzhu Yabghu, together with the five Nishibi tribes, asked permission to attack Helu, broke his main camp, and beheaded more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Dulo Khan died. His son Zhenzhu Yabghu and the five Nishibi tribes asked leave to strike Helu, broke his main camp, and took more than a thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 顯慶二年，遣右屯衛將軍蘇定方，燕然都護任雅相，副都護蕭嗣業，左驍衛大將軍、瀚海都督回紇婆閏等率師討擊，仍使右武衛大將軍阿史那彌射、左屯衛大將軍阿史那步真為安撫大使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianqing, Su Dingfang, General of the Right Tunwei Guards; Ren Yaoxiang, Protector of Yanran; Xiao Siye, Deputy Protector; Po'er of the Huihe, Grand General of the Left Xiaowei Guards and Governor of Hanhai, and others were sent with an army to pursue and attack. Ashina Mishshe, Grand General of the Right Wuwei Guards, and Ashina Bozhen, Grand General of the Left Tunwei Guards, were appointed pacification commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xianqing the court sent Su Dingfang, General of the Right Tunwei Guards; Ren Yaoxiang, Protector of Yanran; Xiao Siye, Deputy Protector; Po'er of the Huihe, Grand General of the Left Xiaowei Guards and Governor of Hanhai; and others to pursue and attack Helu. Ashina Mishshe, Grand General of the Right Wuwei Guards, and Ashina Bozhen, Grand General of the Left Tunwei Guards, were appointed pacification commissioners.

sentences.zh: 定方行至曳咥河西，賀魯率胡祿居闕啜等二萬余騎列陣而待。

translations.literal: Su Dingfang reached the west bank of the Yedu River. Helu gathered more than twenty thousand horsemen, including Hu Lu Ju Que Chuo, and formed battle lines to await them.
translations.idiomatic: Su Dingfang reached the west bank of the Yedu River. Helu drew up more than twenty thousand horsemen, including Hu Lu Ju Que Chuo, in battle array to meet him.

sentences.zh: 定方率副總管任雅相等與之交戰，賊眾大敗，斬大首領都搭達幹等二百余人。

translations.literal: Su Dingfang led Deputy Commander Ren Yaoxiang and others into battle. The rebel forces were utterly defeated; more than two hundred major chieftains including Bodhdaghan were beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Su Dingfang led Deputy Commander Ren Yaoxiang and others into battle. The rebels were routed, and more than two hundred major chieftains, including Bodhdaghan, were beheaded.

sentences.zh: 賀魯及闕啜輕騎奔竄，渡伊麗河，兵馬溺死者甚眾。

translations.literal: Helu and Que Chuo fled with light cavalry, crossed the Yili River, and a great many men and horses drowned.
translations.idiomatic: Helu and Que Chuo fled with light cavalry across the Yili River. A great many men and horses drowned in the crossing.

sentences.zh: 嗣業至千泉賀魯下牙之處，彌射進軍至伊麗水，處月、處密等部各率眾來降。

translations.literal: Xiao Siye reached the place where Helu had established his southern camp at the Thousand Springs. Mishshe advanced to the Yili River. The Chuyue, Chumid, and other tribes each led their followers to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Siye reached the Thousand Springs, where Helu had kept his southern camp. Mishshe advanced to the Yili River. The Chuyue, Chumid, and other tribes came over one after another.

sentences.zh: 彌射又進次雙河，賀魯先使步失達幹鳩集散卒，據柵拒戰。

translations.literal: Mishshe advanced again and encamped at Shuanghe. Helu had already sent Bushidaghan to gather scattered troops and hold a stockade against attack.
translations.idiomatic: Mishshe pressed on to Shuanghe. Helu had already sent Bushidaghan to rally scattered troops and hold a fortified stockade.

sentences.zh: 彌射、步真攻之，大潰；

translations.literal: Mishshe and Bozhen attacked and utterly routed them;
translations.idiomatic: Mishshe and Bozhen attacked and broke them completely;

sentences.zh: 又與蘇定方攻賀魯於碎葉水，大破之。

translations.literal: they then joined Su Dingfang in an attack on Helu at the Suyab River and thoroughly defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: then joined Su Dingfang in an attack on Helu at the Suyab River and defeated him utterly.

sentences.zh: 賀魯與咥運欲投鼠耨設，至石國之蘇咄城傍，人馬饑乏，城主伊涅達幹詐將酒食出迎，賀魯信其言入城，遂被拘執。

translations.literal: Helu and Yiyun intended to seek refuge with Shunishi She. When they reached the vicinity of Sudu City in the State of Shi, men and horses were starving and exhausted. The city lord Yinedaghan falsely offered food and wine in welcome outside the gates. Helu believed him and entered the city, whereupon he was seized and held.
translations.idiomatic: Helu and Yiyun meant to take refuge with Shunishi She. Near Sudu City in the State of Shi, their men and horses were starving. The city lord Yinedaghan feigned welcome with food and wine. Helu trusted him, entered the city, and was seized.

sentences.zh: 蕭嗣業既至石國，鼠耨設乃以賀魯屬之。

translations.literal: When Xiao Siye reached the State of Shi, Shunishi She turned Helu over to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Siye arrived in the State of Shi, Shunishi She handed Helu over to him.

sentences.zh: 賀魯謂嗣業曰：「我破亡虜耳！

translations.literal: Helu said to Xiao Siye: "I am a defeated and ruined captive!
translations.idiomatic: Helu said to Xiao Siye, "I am a broken captive, nothing more!

sentences.zh: 先帝厚我，而我背之，今日之敗，天怒我也。

translations.literal: The former emperor treated me generously, and I betrayed him. Today's defeat is Heaven's anger at me.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor treated me with great kindness, and I turned against him. This defeat is Heaven's wrath upon me.

sentences.zh: 舊聞漢法，殺人皆於都市，至京殺我，請向昭陵，使得謝罪於先帝，是本願也。」

translations.literal: I have long heard that under Han law, executions are carried out in the capital market. When you reach the capital and execute me, I beg you to do so facing Zhaoling, so that I may ask forgiveness of the former emperor. That is my true wish.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that under Han law executions are carried out in the capital market. When you reach the capital and put me to death, I beg that it be done facing Zhaoling, so I may ask forgiveness of the late emperor. That is my true wish.

sentences.zh: 高宗聞而湣之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong heard this, he was moved to pity.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong heard this, he was moved to pity.

sentences.zh: 及俘賀魯至京師，令獻於昭陵及太廟，詔特免死。

translations.literal: When the captive Helu reached the capital, he was made to present himself at Zhaoling and the Imperial Ancestral Temple. An edict especially spared his life.
translations.idiomatic: When Helu was brought to the capital as a captive, he was presented at Zhaoling and the Imperial Ancestral Temple. An edict specially spared his life.

sentences.zh: 分其種落置昆陵、濛池二都護府，其所役屬諸國，皆分置州府，西盡於波斯，並隸安西都護府。

translations.literal: His tribes were divided and placed under the two protectorates of Kunling and Mengchi. All the states that had been subject to him were apportioned into prefectures and districts, reaching west to Persia, all under the Protectorate General of Anxi.
translations.idiomatic: His tribes were divided between the Kunling and Mengchi protectorates. The states that had served under him were parcelled out into prefectures and districts as far west as Persia, all under the Protectorate General of Anxi.

sentences.zh: 四年，賀魯卒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Helu died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Helu died.

sentences.zh: 詔葬於頡利墓側，刻石以紀其事。

translations.literal: An edict ordered burial beside Jieli's tomb, with a stele carved to record the matter.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered him buried beside Jieli's tomb, with a stele carved to record the affair.

sentences.zh: 阿史那彌射者，室點密可汗五代孫也。

translations.literal: Ashina Mishshe was the fifth-generation descendant of Ishbara Yabghu.
translations.idiomatic: Ashina Mishshe was a fifth-generation descendant of Ishbara Yabghu.

sentences.zh: 初，室點密從單於統領十大首領，有兵十萬眾，往平西域諸胡國，自為可汗，號十姓部落，世統其眾。

translations.literal: Originally Ishbara, following the Shanyu, had commanded ten great chieftains with a hundred thousand troops. He went to pacify the various foreign states of the Western Regions, declared himself khan, and was called the Ten Surname Tribes, ruling their followers through successive generations.
translations.idiomatic: In the beginning Ishbara, serving under the Shanyu, had commanded ten great chieftains and a hundred thousand troops. He went west to pacify the foreign states of the Western Regions, declared himself khan, and took the name Ten Surname Tribes, passing rule of the people down through the generations.

sentences.zh: 彌射在本蕃為莫賀咄葉護。

translations.literal: In his own realm Mishshe had been Moheduo Yabghu.
translations.idiomatic: In his own realm Mishshe had held the title Moheduo Yabghu.

sentences.zh: 貞觀六年，詔遣鴻臚少卿劉善因就蕃立為奚利邲咄陸可汗，賜以鼓纛、彩帛萬段。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhenguan, an edict ordered Vice Director of the Court for Diplomatic Reception Liu Shanyin to go to their realm and install him as Xili Kui Dulo Khan, bestowing upon him drums, banners, and ten thousand bolts of colored silk.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Zhenguan an edict sent Vice Director of the Court for Diplomatic Reception Liu Shanyin to their realm to install him as Xili Kui Dulo Khan, with drums, banners, and ten thousand bolts of colored silk.

sentences.zh: 其族兄步真欲自立為可汗，遂謀殺彌射弟侄二十余人。

translations.literal: His clansman elder cousin Bozhen wished to install himself as khan and thereupon plotted to kill more than twenty of Mishshe's brothers and nephews.
translations.idiomatic: His elder clansman Bozhen wished to make himself khan and plotted to kill more than twenty of Mishshe's brothers and nephews.

sentences.zh: 彌射既與步真有隙，以貞觀十三年率所部處月、處密部落入朝，授右監門大將軍。

translations.literal: Mishshe, now estranged from Bozhen, in the thirteenth year of Zhenguan led his Chuyue and Chumid tribes to court and was appointed Grand General of the Right Palace Gate Guards.
translations.idiomatic: Estranged from Bozhen, Mishshe in the thirteenth year of Zhenguan led his Chuyue and Chumid tribes to court and was made Grand General of the Right Palace Gate Guards.

sentences.zh: 其後步真遂自立為咄陸葉護，其部落多不服，委之遁去。

translations.literal: Afterward Bozhen declared himself Dulo Yabghu. Many of his tribes would not submit and drifted away from him.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Bozhen declared himself Dulo Yabghu. Many of his tribes refused to follow him and drifted away.

sentences.zh: 步真復攜家屬入朝，授左屯衛大將軍。

translations.literal: Bozhen again came to court with his family and was appointed Grand General of the Left Tunwei Guards.
translations.idiomatic: Bozhen came to court again with his family and was appointed Grand General of the Left Tunwei Guards.

sentences.zh: 彌射後從太宗征高麗有功，封平襄縣伯。

translations.literal: Later Mishshe followed Emperor Taizong on the campaign against Goguryeo with merit and was enfeoffed as Baron of Pingxiang County.
translations.idiomatic: Later Mishshe followed Emperor Taizong against Goguryeo with distinction and was enfeoffed Baron of Pingxiang County.

sentences.zh: 顯慶二年，轉右武衛大將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianqing he was transferred to the post of Grand General of the Right Wuwei Guards.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xianqing he was transferred to Grand General of the Right Wuwei Guards.

sentences.zh: 及討平賀魯，乃冊立彌射為興昔亡可汗兼右衛大將軍、昆陵都護，分押賀魯下五咄六部落。

translations.literal: When Helu had been subdued, Mishshe was formally installed as Khan Irbis She, concurrently Grand General of the Right Guards, Protector of Kunling, and given charge of the five Dulu tribes formerly under Helu.
translations.idiomatic: After Helu was subdued, Mishshe was invested as Khan Irbis She, concurrently Grand General of the Right Guards and Protector of Kunling, and given charge of the five Dulu tribes that had served under Helu.

sentences.zh: 步真授繼往絕可汗，兼右衛大將軍、濛池都護，仍分押五弩失畢部落。

translations.literal: Bozhen was appointed Khan Jiwangjue, concurrently Grand General of the Right Guards and Protector of Mengchi, and was likewise given charge of the five Nishibi tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Bozhen was appointed Khan Jiwangjue, concurrently Grand General of the Right Guards and Protector of Mengchi, and likewise given charge of the five Nishibi tribes.

sentences.zh: 因下詔曰：

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict was issued, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon an edict was issued, saying:

sentences.zh: 自西蕃罹亂，三十余年。

translations.literal: Since the western regions fell into disorder, more than thirty years have passed.
translations.idiomatic: The western regions have been in turmoil for more than thirty years.

sentences.zh: 比者賀魯猖狂，百姓重被劫掠。

translations.literal: Recently Helu ran wild, and the common people suffered repeated plunder.
translations.idiomatic: Of late Helu has run wild, and the people have suffered repeated raids.

sentences.zh: 朕君臨四海，情均養育。

translations.literal: I rule the four seas, my solicitude equal in nurture for all.
translations.idiomatic: I rule the four seas and hold all alike in my care.

sentences.zh: 不可使兇狡之虜，恣行侵漁，無辜之氓，久遭塗炭。

translations.literal: I cannot permit cruel and cunning barbarians to roam at will preying upon others, nor innocent people to long suffer devastation.
translations.idiomatic: I cannot allow cruel and cunning barbarians to prey at will, nor innocent people to endure ruin year after year.

sentences.zh: 故遣右屯衛將軍蘇定方等統率騎勇，北路討逐。

translations.literal: Therefore I sent Su Dingfang, General of the Right Tunwei Guards, and others to command mounted warriors and pursue them by the northern route.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I sent Su Dingfang, General of the Right Tunwei Guards, and others to lead mounted warriors in pursuit along the northern route.

sentences.zh: 卿等宣暢朝風，南道撫育。

translations.literal: You are to spread the court's influence abroad and pacify and nurture them along the southern route.
translations.idiomatic: You are to carry the court's influence abroad and pacify and nurture the tribes along the southern route.

sentences.zh: 遂使兇渠畏威，夷人慕德，伐叛柔服，西域總平。

translations.literal: Thus the rebel chieftains came to fear our might, the foreign tribes admired our virtue, rebels were suppressed and the submissive were treated with kindness, and the Western Regions were wholly pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Thus rebel chieftains came to fear our might, foreign tribes admired our virtue, rebels were struck down and the submissive were treated with kindness, and the Western Regions were wholly pacified.

sentences.zh: 賀魯父子既已擒獲，諸頭部落須有統領。

translations.literal: Helu and his son have now been captured; the various tribal divisions require leaders.
translations.idiomatic: Helu and his son are now captives. The tribal divisions need leaders.

sentences.zh: 卿早歸闕庭，久參宿衛，深感恩義，甚知法式，所以冊立卿等各為一部可汗。

translations.literal: You returned early to the imperial court, have long served as palace guards, deeply feel gratitude and loyalty, and understand law and ritual well — therefore I install each of you as khan of a separate division.
translations.idiomatic: You came early to the imperial court, have long served in the palace guard, feel deep gratitude and loyalty, and understand law and ritual well. Therefore I install each of you as khan over a separate division.

sentences.zh: 但諸姓從賀魯，非其本情，卿等才至即降，亦是赤心向國。

translations.literal: Yet the various tribes followed Helu, not from their hearts' inclination. That you surrendered as soon as you arrived also shows your true loyalty to the state.
translations.idiomatic: The various tribes followed Helu against their hearts' inclination. That you surrendered the moment you arrived shows your true loyalty to the state.

sentences.zh: 卿宜與盧承慶等準其部落大小，位望高下，節級授刺史以下官。

translations.literal: You should work with Lu Chengqing and others, according to each tribe's size and its chieftains' standing, to appoint them to offices of prefect and below by appropriate ranks.
translations.idiomatic: You should work with Lu Chengqing and others to appoint chieftains, according to each tribe's size and each man's standing, to offices of prefect and below by appropriate ranks.

sentences.zh: 龍朔中，又令彌射、步真率所部從釭海道大總管蘇海政討龜茲。

translations.literal: In the Longshuo reign, Mishshe and Bozhen were again ordered to lead their followers under Circuit Grand Commander Su Haizheng of the Ganghaidao route to campaign against Kucha.
translations.idiomatic: During the Longshuo reign Mishshe and Bozhen were again ordered to lead their followers under Circuit Grand Commander Su Haizheng of the Ganghaidao route against Kucha.

sentences.zh: 步真嘗欲並彌射部落，遂密告海政云：「彌射欲謀反，請以計誅之。」

translations.literal: Bozhen had long wished to absorb Mishshe's tribes. He secretly informed Haizheng, saying, "Mishshe is plotting rebellion. Pray use a stratagem to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: Bozhen had long wished to absorb Mishshe's tribes. He secretly told Haizheng, "Mishshe is plotting rebellion. Use a stratagem to kill him.

sentences.zh: 時海政兵才數千，懸師在彌射境內，遂集軍吏而謀曰：「彌射若反，我輩即無噍類。

translations.literal: At that time Haizheng had only a few thousand troops, and his army was deep inside Mishshe's territory. He gathered his officers to plan, saying, "If Mishshe rebels, not one of us will survive.
translations.idiomatic: Haizheng had only a few thousand troops and was deep inside Mishshe's territory. He gathered his officers and said, "If Mishshe rebels, not one of us will survive.

sentences.zh: 今宜先舉事，則可克捷。」

translations.literal: We should strike first — then we can succeed.
translations.idiomatic: We must strike first — then we can prevail.

sentences.zh: 乃偽稱有敕，令大總管賫物數百萬段分賜可汗及諸首領。

translations.literal: He falsely claimed there was an imperial order for the grand commander to distribute millions of bolts of goods among the khan and various chieftains.
translations.idiomatic: He falsely claimed an imperial order for the grand commander to distribute millions of bolts of goods among the khan and the chieftains.

sentences.zh: 由是彌射率其麾下，隨例請物，海政盡收斬之。

translations.literal: Accordingly Mishshe led his followers to request goods according to the stated allocation; Haizheng seized and executed them all.
translations.idiomatic: Mishshe accordingly led his followers to claim their share. Haizheng seized and executed them all.

sentences.zh: 共後西蕃盛言彌射非反，為步真所誣，而海政不能審察，濫行誅戮。

translations.literal: Afterward the western regions widely said Mishshe had not rebelled but had been slandered by Bozhen, and that Haizheng had failed to investigate and had indiscriminately carried out executions.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward the western regions widely held that Mishshe had not rebelled but had been slandered by Bozhen, and that Haizheng had failed to investigate and had slaughtered them without cause.

sentences.zh: 則天臨朝，十姓無主數年，部落多散失。

translations.literal: When Empress Wu assumed the regency, the Ten Surnames were without leaders for several years and many tribes were scattered and lost.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wu assumed the regency, the Ten Surnames went leaderless for years and many tribes were scattered and lost.

sentences.zh: 垂拱初，遂擢授彌射子左豹韜衛翊府中郎將元慶為左玉鈐衛將軍兼昆陵都護，令襲興昔亡可汗，押五咄六部落。

translations.literal: In the early Chuigong period, Mishshe's son Yuanqing, a middle commander in the Left Leopard-Tao Guards Escort Office, was promoted to General of the Left Jade Command Guards and Protector of Kunling, ordered to succeed as Khan Irbis She and given charge of the five Dulu tribes.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Chuigong period Mishshe's son Yuanqing, a middle commander in the Left Leopard-Tao Guards Escort Office, was promoted to General of the Left Jade Command Guards and Protector of Kunling, ordered to succeed as Khan Irbis She, and given charge of the five Dulu tribes.

sentences.zh: 步真子斛瑟羅為右玉鈐衛將軍，兼濛池都護，押五弩失畢部落。

translations.literal: Bozhen's son Husero was made General of the Right Jade Command Guards and Protector of Mengchi, given charge of the five Nishibi tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Bozhen's son Husero was made General of the Right Jade Command Guards and Protector of Mengchi, with charge of the five Nishibi tribes.

sentences.zh: 尋進授元慶左衛大將軍。

translations.literal: Soon Yuanqing was further promoted to Grand General of the Left Guards.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Yuanqing was further promoted to Grand General of the Left Guards.

sentences.zh: 如意元年，為來俊臣誣謀反被害。

translations.literal: In the first year of Ruyi he was falsely accused of plotting rebellion by Lai Junchen and put to death.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Ruyi Lai Junchen falsely accused him of plotting rebellion and had him put to death.

sentences.zh: 其子獻，配流崖州。

translations.literal: His son Xian was sent into exile in Yazhou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xian was exiled to Yazhou.

sentences.zh: 長安三年，召還。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chang'an he was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Chang'an he was recalled.

sentences.zh: 累授右驍衛大將軍，襲父興昔亡可汗，充安撫招慰十姓大使。

translations.literal: He rose through appointments to Grand General of the Right Xiaowei Guards, succeeded his father as Khan Irbis She, and served as Commissioner for Pacification and Solicitation of the Ten Surnames.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through appointments to Grand General of the Right Xiaowei Guards, succeeded his father as Khan Irbis She, and served as Commissioner for Pacification and Solicitation of the Ten Surnames.

sentences.zh: 獻本蕃漸為默啜及烏質勒所侵。

translations.literal: Xian's homeland was gradually encroached upon by Ashina Mochuo and Wuzhile.
translations.idiomatic: Xian's homeland was gradually encroached upon by Mochuo and Wuzhile.

sentences.zh: 遂不敢還國。

translations.literal: He therefore dared not return to his realm.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore dared not return to his realm.

sentences.zh: 開元中，累遷右金吾大將軍。

translations.literal: During the Kaiyuan reign he was repeatedly promoted, eventually to Grand General of the Right Jinwu Guards.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaiyuan reign he rose through repeated promotions to Grand General of the Right Jinwu Guards.

sentences.zh: 卒於長安。

translations.literal: He died in Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 阿史那步真者，在本蕃授左屯衛大將軍。

translations.literal: Ashina Bozhen had been appointed Grand General of the Left Tunwei Guards in his own realm.
translations.idiomatic: Ashina Bozhen had been appointed Grand General of the Left Tunwei Guards in his own realm.

sentences.zh: 與彌射討平賀魯，加授驃騎大將軍、行右衛大將軍、濛池都護、繼往絕可汗，押五弩失畢部落。

translations.literal: Together with Mishshe he helped subdue Helu and was additionally appointed General of Agile Cavalry, Acting Grand General of the Right Guards, Protector of Mengchi, and Khan Jiwangjue, given charge of the five Nishibi tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Mishshe he helped subdue Helu and was further appointed General of Agile Cavalry, Acting Grand General of the Right Guards, Protector of Mengchi, and Khan Jiwangjue, with charge of the five Nishibi tribes.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: He soon died.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died.

sentences.zh: 其子斛瑟羅，本蕃為步利設，垂拱初，授右玉鈐衛將軍兼濛池都護、襲繼往絕可汗，押五弩失畢部落。

translations.literal: His son Husero, who in his own realm had been Bolu She, in the early Chuigong period was appointed General of the Right Jade Command Guards and Protector of Mengchi, succeeded as Khan Jiwangjue, and was given charge of the five Nishibi tribes.
translations.idiomatic: His son Husero, who in his own realm had been Bolu She, in the early Chuigong period was appointed General of the Right Jade Command Guards and Protector of Mengchi, succeeded as Khan Jiwangjue, and was given charge of the five Nishibi tribes.

sentences.zh: 天授元年，拜左衛大將軍，改封竭忠事主可汗，仍賜濛池都護。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianshou he was appointed Grand General of the Left Guards, re-enfeoffed as Khan Jiezhong Shizhu, and again granted the Protector of Mengchi.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianshou he was appointed Grand General of the Left Guards, re-enfeoffed as Khan Jiezhong Shizhu, and again granted the Protector of Mengchi.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: He soon died.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died.

sentences.zh: 子懷道，神龍年累授右屯衛大將軍、光祿卿，轉太仆卿兼濛池都護、十姓可汗。

translations.literal: His son Huaidao, in the Shenlong period, rose through appointments to Grand General of the Right Tunwei Guards and Director of the Imperial Household Service, then was transferred to Director of the Imperial Stud, concurrently Protector of Mengchi and Khan of the Ten Surnames.
translations.idiomatic: His son Huaidao, in the Shenlong period, rose to Grand General of the Right Tunwei Guards and Director of the Imperial Household Service, then became Director of the Imperial Stud, concurrently Protector of Mengchi and Khan of the Ten Surnames.

sentences.zh: 自垂拱已後，十姓部落頻被突厥默啜侵掠，死散殆盡。

translations.literal: From Chuigong onward the Ten Surname tribes were repeatedly raided by the Turk Mochuo; the dead and scattered were nearly wiped out.
translations.idiomatic: From Chuigong onward the Ten Surname tribes were repeatedly raided by the Turk Mochuo until the dead and scattered were nearly wiped out.

sentences.zh: 及隨斛瑟羅才六七萬人，徙居內地，西突厥阿史那氏於是遂絕。

translations.literal: Only about sixty or seventy thousand followed Husero, migrating to settle within the interior. The Ashina clan of the Western Turks thus came to an end.
translations.idiomatic: Only about sixty or seventy thousand followed Husero in migration to the interior. The Ashina line of the Western Turks thus came to an end.

sentences.zh: 突騎施烏質勒者，西突厥之別種也。

translations.literal: Wuzhile of the Tuqishi was a separate branch of the Western Turks.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhile of the Tuqishi was a separate branch of the Western Turks.

sentences.zh: 初隸在斛瑟羅下，號為莫賀達幹。

translations.literal: At first he was subject to Husero and was styled Mohedaghan.
translations.idiomatic: At first he served under Husero and was styled Mohedaghan.

sentences.zh: 後以斛瑟羅用刑嚴酷，眾皆畏之，尤能撫恤其部落，由是為遠近諸胡所歸附。

translations.literal: Later, because Husero administered punishments with harsh severity and all feared him, while Wuzhile was especially able to comfort and care for his tribes, foreign tribes near and far came to attach themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: Later Husero's punishments grew harsh and all feared him, while Wuzhile was especially skilled at comforting and caring for his tribes. Foreign tribes near and far therefore attached themselves to him.

sentences.zh: 其下置都督二十員，各統兵七千人。

translations.literal: Under him he established twenty governors, each commanding seven thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: He established twenty governors under him, each commanding seven thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 嘗屯聚碎葉西北界，後漸攻陷碎葉，徙其牙帳居之。

translations.literal: He had once encamped at the northwestern borders of Suyab; later he gradually captured Suyab and moved his main camp there.
translations.idiomatic: He had once encamped on the northwestern marches of Suyab. Later he gradually captured the city and moved his main camp there.

sentences.zh: 東北與突厥為鄰，西南與諸胡相接，東南至西廷州。

translations.literal: To the northeast he bordered the Turks; to the southwest he adjoined the various foreign peoples; to the southeast his territory reached Western Tingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: To the northeast he bordered the Turks; to the southwest he adjoined the foreign tribes; to the southeast his lands reached Western Tingzhou.

sentences.zh: 斛瑟羅以部眾削弱，自則天時入朝，不敢還蕃，其地並為烏質勒所並。

translations.literal: Husero, his followers depleted, entered court in Empress Wu's time and dared not return to his realm. His lands were all absorbed by Wuzhile.
translations.idiomatic: Husero, his followers depleted, came to court in Empress Wu's time and dared not return west. Wuzhile absorbed all his lands.

sentences.zh: 景龍二年，詔封為西河郡王，令攝御史大夫，解琬就加冊立。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jinglong an edict enfeoffed Wuzhile as Prince of Xihe Commandery, ordered him to serve as Acting Censor-in-Chief, and sent Jie Wan to invest him with the title.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jinglong an edict enfeoffed Wuzhile as Prince of Xihe Commandery, ordered him to serve as Acting Censor-in-Chief, and sent Jie Wan to invest him.

sentences.zh: 未至，烏質勒卒。

translations.literal: Before he arrived, Wuzhile died.
translations.idiomatic: Before he arrived, Wuzhile died.

sentences.zh: 其長子娑葛代統其眾，詔便立娑葛為金河郡王，仍賜以宮女四人。

translations.literal: His eldest son Suoge succeeded to command of the tribes. An edict immediately installed Suoge as Prince of Jinhe Commandery and also bestowed upon him four palace women.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Suoge succeeded to command of the tribes. An edict immediately installed Suoge as Prince of Jinhe Commandery and bestowed four palace women upon him.

sentences.zh: 初，娑葛代父統兵，烏質勒下部將闕啜忠節甚忌之，以兵部尚書宗楚客當朝任勢，密遣使賫金七百兩以賂楚客，請停娑葛統兵。

translations.literal: At first Suoge had taken his father's place commanding the troops. Zhongjie of Que Chuo, a subordinate general under Wuzhile, deeply resented this. Relying on the power that Minister of War Zong Chuke wielded at court, he secretly sent envoys bearing seven hundred taels of gold to bribe Chuke and asked that Suoge be removed from command.
translations.idiomatic: Suoge had taken his father's place in command of the troops. Zhongjie of Que Chuo, a subordinate general under Wuzhile, deeply resented this. Relying on Minister of War Zong Chuke's power at court, he secretly sent envoys with seven hundred taels of gold to bribe Chuke and asked that Suoge be removed from command.

sentences.zh: 楚客乃遣御史中丞馮嘉賓充使至其境，陰與忠節籌其事，並自致書以申意。

translations.literal: Chuke then sent Vice Censor Feng Jiabin as envoy to that region, covertly planning the affair with Zhongjie, and also sent a personal letter to explain his intentions.
translations.idiomatic: Chuke then sent Vice Censor Feng Jiabin as envoy to the region, secretly plotting the affair with Zhongjie, and also sent a personal letter stating his intentions.

sentences.zh: 在路為娑葛遊兵所獲，遂斬嘉賓，仍進兵攻陷火燒等城，遣使上表以索楚客頭。

translations.literal: On the road they were captured by Suoge's patrol troops. Suoge thereupon executed Jiabin, advanced his troops to capture Huoshao and other cities, and sent envoys with a memorial demanding Chuke's head.
translations.idiomatic: On the road they were taken by Suoge's patrol troops. Suoge executed Jiabin, advanced to capture Huoshao and other cities, and sent envoys with a memorial demanding Chuke's head.

sentences.zh: 景龍三年，娑葛弟遮弩恨所分部落少於其兄，遂叛入突厥，請為鄉導，以討娑葛。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jinglong, Suoge's younger brother Zhenu resented receiving fewer tribes than his elder brother had. He rebelled, fled to the Turks, and offered to serve as guide to attack Suoge.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jinglong Suoge's younger brother Zhenu resented receiving fewer tribes than his elder brother. He rebelled, fled to the Turks, and offered to guide them against Suoge.

sentences.zh: 默啜乃留遮弩，遣兵二萬人與其左右來討娑葛，擒之而還。

translations.literal: Mochuo kept Zhenu behind and sent twenty thousand troops with his attendants to attack Suoge, captured him, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Mochuo kept Zhenu behind and sent twenty thousand troops with his attendants against Suoge, captured him, and returned.

sentences.zh: 默啜顧謂遮弩曰：「汝於兄弟尚不和協，豈能盡心於我。」

translations.literal: Mochuo turned to Zhenu and said, "You cannot even live in harmony with your own brothers — how could you serve me with your whole heart?
translations.idiomatic: Mochuo turned to Zhenu and said, "You cannot even live in harmony with your own brothers — how could you serve me with your whole heart?

sentences.zh: 遂與娑葛俱殺之。

translations.literal: He then had both of them killed.
translations.idiomatic: He then had both of them killed.

sentences.zh: 默啜兵還，娑葛下部將蘇祿鳩集余眾，自立為可汗。

translations.literal: When Mochuo's troops withdrew, Suoge's subordinate general Sulu gathered the remaining followers and declared himself khan.
translations.idiomatic: When Mochuo's troops withdrew, Suoge's subordinate general Sulu rallied the remaining followers and declared himself khan.

sentences.zh: 蘇祿者，突騎施別種也。

translations.literal: Sulu was a separate branch of the Tuqishi.
translations.idiomatic: Sulu was a separate branch of the Tuqishi.

sentences.zh: 頗善綏撫，十姓部落漸歸附之，眾二十萬，遂雄西域之地，尋遣使來朝。

translations.literal: He was quite skilled in gentle governance. The Ten Surname tribes gradually submitted to him; his followers numbered two hundred thousand, and he came to dominate the Western Regions. Soon he sent envoys to court.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled at gentle rule. The Ten Surname tribes gradually submitted to him until his followers numbered two hundred thousand, and he came to dominate the Western Regions. Soon he sent envoys to court.

sentences.zh: 開元三年，制授蘇祿為左羽林軍大將軍、金方道經略大使，進為特勒，遣侍御史解忠順賫璽書冊立為忠順可汗。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kaiyuan an imperial decree appointed Sulu as Grand General of the Left Yulin Army and Military Commissioner of the Jinfang Circuit, promoted him to tegin, and sent Remonstrating Censor Jie Zhongshun with an imperial patent of investiture to install him as Khan Zhongshun.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Kaiyuan an imperial decree appointed Sulu Grand General of the Left Yulin Army and Military Commissioner of the Jinfang Circuit, promoted him to tegin, and sent Remonstrating Censor Jie Zhongshun with an imperial patent to install him as Khan Zhongshun.

sentences.zh: 自是每年遣使朝獻。

translations.literal: From then on he sent envoys to court with tribute every year.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he sent envoys to court with tribute every year.

sentences.zh: 上乃立史懷道女為金河公主以妻之。

translations.literal: The emperor then installed the daughter of Shi Huaidao as Princess Jinhe and gave her to him in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then installed the daughter of Shi Huaidao as Princess Jinhe and gave her to him in marriage.

sentences.zh: 時杜暹為安西都護，公主遣牙官賫馬千疋詣安西互市。

translations.literal: At that time Du Xian was Protector-General of Anxi. The princess sent an aide with a thousand horses to Anxi for reciprocal trade.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Du Xian was Protector-General of Anxi. The princess sent an aide with a thousand horses to Anxi for trade.

sentences.zh: 使者宣公主教與暹，暹怒曰：「阿史那氏女，豈合宣教與吾節度耶！」

translations.literal: The envoy proclaimed the princess's instructions to Du Xian. Xian angrily said, "How is it fitting for a woman of the Ashina clan to issue instructions to me, a frontier commissioner!
translations.idiomatic: The envoy proclaimed the princess's instructions to Du Xian. Xian angrily said, "How is it fitting for a woman of the Ashina clan to issue instructions to me, a frontier commissioner!

sentences.zh: 杖其使者，留而不遣，其馬經雪，寒死並盡。

translations.literal: He had the envoy beaten with the rod, detained him without release, and the horses, exposed to snow, all perished of cold.
translations.idiomatic: He had the envoy beaten with the rod and detained him. The horses, caught in snow, all perished of cold.

sentences.zh: 蘇祿大怒，發兵分寇四鎮。

translations.literal: Sulu was furious and dispatched troops to raid the Four Garrisons in separate columns.
translations.idiomatic: Sulu was furious and dispatched troops to raid the Four Garrisons in separate columns.

sentences.zh: 會杜暹入知政事，趙頤貞代為安西都護，城守久之，由是四鎮貯積及人畜並為蘇祿所掠，安西僅全。

translations.literal: Just then Du Xian entered the government and became a chief minister; Zhao Yizhen replaced him as Protector-General of Anxi. The garrison held out in the cities for a long time, and consequently the stored provisions, livestock, and people of the Four Garrisons were all plundered by Sulu. Anxi itself barely survived intact.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Du Xian entered the government as chief minister, and Zhao Yizhen replaced him as Protector-General of Anxi. The garrison held the cities for a long time. The stored provisions, livestock, and people of the Four Garrisons were all plundered by Sulu. Anxi itself barely survived.

sentences.zh: 蘇祿既聞杜暹入相，稍引退，俄又遣使入朝獻方物。

translations.literal: Suolu, having heard that Du Xian had entered the government as minister, withdrew somewhat; soon after he again sent envoys to court to present regional products.
translations.idiomatic: When Suolu learned that Du Xian had entered the government as chief minister, he pulled back somewhat; before long he sent envoys to court again with tribute goods.

sentences.zh: 十八年，蘇祿使至京師，玄宗禦丹鳳樓設宴。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, Suolu's envoys reached the capital; Emperor Xuanzong held a banquet for them from the Hall of Crimson Phoenix.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year, Suolu's envoys arrived at the capital, and Emperor Xuanzong received them with a banquet from the Hall of Crimson Phoenix.

sentences.zh: 突厥先遣使入朝，是日亦來預宴，與蘇祿使爭長。

translations.literal: The Turks had earlier sent envoys to court; on that day they too came to join the banquet and disputed precedence with Suolu's envoys.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks had already sent envoys to court, and on that day they too attended the banquet, quarreling with Suolu's envoys over who should take precedence.

sentences.zh: 突厥使曰：「突騎施國小，本是突厥之臣，不宜居上。」

translations.literal: The Turkish envoy said: "The Turgesh state is small and was originally a subject of the Turks—it is not fitting for them to sit above.
translations.idiomatic: The Turkish envoy said, "The Turgesh are a small state and were originally subjects of the Turks. It is not fitting that they sit in the place of honor.

sentences.zh: 蘇祿使曰：「今日此宴，乃為我設，不合居下。」

translations.literal: Suolu's envoy said: "Today's banquet was arranged for us—it is not fitting that we sit below."
translations.idiomatic: Suolu's envoy replied, "This banquet was held for us. It is not fitting that we sit below."

sentences.zh: 於是中書門下及百僚議，遂於東西幕下兩處分坐，突厥使在東，突騎施使在西。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Secretariat-Chancellery and the hundred officials deliberated, and they arranged seating in two places under the eastern and western awnings—the Turkish envoy in the east, the Turgesh envoy in the west.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat-Chancellery and the officials then deliberated and seated the two parties separately under the eastern and western awnings—the Turkish envoy to the east and the Turgesh envoy to the west.

sentences.zh: 宴訖，厚賫而遣之。

translations.literal: When the banquet ended, they were lavishly rewarded and sent away.
translations.idiomatic: When the feast was over, both parties were richly rewarded and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 蘇祿性尤清儉，每戰伐，有所克獲，盡分與將士及諸部落。

translations.literal: Suolu was by nature especially frugal and plain; whenever he fought and gained spoils, he shared everything with officers, soldiers, and the various tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Suolu was by nature austere and unpretentious. Whenever he fought and took booty, he divided all of it among his officers, soldiers, and the various tribes.

sentences.zh: 其下愛之，甚為其用。

translations.literal: His followers loved him and served him with great loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: His followers loved him and served him with wholehearted devotion.

sentences.zh: 潛又遣使南通吐蕃，東附突厥。

translations.literal: Secretly he also sent envoys south to ally with Tibet and east to attach himself to the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: In secret he also sent envoys south to Tibet and east to the Turks, seeking alliance on both fronts.

sentences.zh: 突厥及吐蕃亦嫁女與蘇祿。

translations.literal: The Turks and Tibet both gave him their daughters in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Both the Turks and the Tibetans gave him their daughters in marriage.

sentences.zh: 既以三國女為可敦，又分立數子為葉護，費用漸廣。

translations.literal: Since he had women from three states as kaghan consorts and had installed several sons as yabghus, his expenses gradually grew vast.
translations.idiomatic: With consorts from three states and several sons installed as yabghus, his expenses steadily mounted.

sentences.zh: 先既不為積貯，晚年抄掠所得者，留不分之。

translations.literal: Earlier he had never built up stores; in his later years what he gained from raids he kept and no longer distributed.
translations.idiomatic: He had never accumulated reserves in the first place, and in his later years he kept what he took in raids and no longer shared it out.

sentences.zh: 又因風病，一手攣縮，其下諸部，心始攜貳。

translations.literal: He also suffered from wind ailment, with one hand contracted and withered; among his subordinate tribes, minds first began to turn divided.
translations.idiomatic: He also contracted a wind ailment that left one hand curled and useless, and among his subordinate tribes loyalty first began to fray.

sentences.zh: 有大首領莫賀達幹、都摩度兩部落，最為強盛。

translations.literal: There were two great chieftains, Mohaganchan and Doumodu, whose tribes were the strongest.
translations.idiomatic: Two great chieftains, Mohaganchan and Doumodu, commanded the strongest tribes.

sentences.zh: 百姓又分為黃姓、黑姓兩種，互相猜阻。

translations.literal: The common people were further split into Yellow-clan and Black-clan factions, mutually suspicious and obstructive.
translations.idiomatic: The people were further divided into Yellow-clan and Black-clan factions, each suspicious of the other and blocking the other's way.

sentences.zh: 二十六年夏，莫賀達幹勒兵夜攻蘇祿，殺之。

translations.literal: In the summer of the twenty-sixth year, Mohaganchan led troops by night to attack Suolu and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the twenty-sixth year, Mohaganchan led his troops in a night attack on Suolu and killed him.

sentences.zh: 都摩度初與莫賀達幹連謀，俄又相背，立蘇祿之子咄火仙為可汗，以輯其余眾，與莫賀達幹自相攻擊。

translations.literal: Doumodu had at first joined Mohaganchan in the plot, but soon turned against him, enthroning Suolu's son Tohuo Xian as khan to gather the remaining hosts, and the two sides attacked one another.
translations.idiomatic: Doumodu had at first plotted with Mohaganchan, but soon broke with him, enthroning Suolu's son Tohuo Xian as khan to rally the remaining tribes, and the two factions turned on each other.

sentences.zh: 莫賀達幹遣使告安西都護蓋嘉運。

translations.literal: Mohaganchan sent envoys to inform Anxi Protector Gai Jiayun.
translations.idiomatic: Mohaganchan sent envoys to notify Anxi Protector Gai Jiayun.

sentences.zh: 嘉運率兵討之，大敗都摩度之眾，臨陣擒咄火仙，並收得金河公主而還。

translations.literal: Jiayun led troops to attack them, inflicted a great defeat on Doumodu's force, captured Tohuo Xian on the battlefield, and also seized Princess Jinhe before returning.
translations.idiomatic: Jiayun marched against them, routed Doumodu's army, captured Tohuo Xian in battle, and returned with Princess Jinhe as well.

sentences.zh: 又欲立史懷道之子昕為可汗以鎮撫之，莫賀達幹不肯，曰：「討平蘇祿，本是我之元謀，若立史昕為主，則國家何以酬賞於我？」

translations.literal: He further wished to install Shi Huaidao's son Xin as khan to pacify and reassure the tribes; Mohaganchan refused, saying: "Suppressing Suolu was originally my primary plan—if Shi Xin is made ruler, how will the state reward me?
translations.idiomatic: Jiayun then proposed to install Shi Huaidao's son Xin as khan to pacify the tribes, but Mohaganchan refused. "Overthrowing Suolu was my plan from the start," he said. "If Shi Xin is made khan, how will the court reward me?

sentences.zh: 乃不立史昕，便令莫賀達幹統眾。

translations.literal: Thereupon Shi Xin was not enthroned, and Mohaganchan was instead put in command of the masses.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xin was not enthroned. Mohaganchan was left in command of the tribes instead.

sentences.zh: 二十七年二月，嘉運率將士詣闕獻俘，玄宗禦花萼樓以宴之，仍令將吐火仙獻於太廟。

translations.literal: In the second month of the twenty-seventh year, Jiayun led officers and soldiers to the court to present captives; Emperor Xuanzong held a banquet for them from the Tower of Flower and Calyx, and ordered Tuhuo Xian presented at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the twenty-seventh year, Jiayun brought his officers and soldiers to court to present captives. Emperor Xuanzong entertained them from the Tower of Flower and Calyx and had Tuhuo Xian offered up at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 俄又黃姓、黑姓自相屠殺，各遣使降附。

translations.literal: Soon the Yellow-clan and Black-clan again slaughtered one another, each sending envoys to surrender and submit.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Yellow-clan and Black-clan were slaughtering one another again, and each faction sent envoys to surrender.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：中原多事，外國窺邊，周獫狁、漢匈奴之後，其類實繁，前史論之備矣。

translations.literal: The historian writes: When the Central Plains are troubled, outer states eye the borders; after the Xianyun of Zhou and the Xiongnu of Han, their kind is indeed numerous—the former histories discuss this fully.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: When the heartland is in turmoil, foreign peoples watch the frontiers. Since the Xianyun of Zhou and the Xiongnu of Han, their kind has been legion, and the earlier histories treat them at length.

sentences.zh: 突厥自隋文修王道，肅軍容，示恩威以羈縻之；

translations.literal: From the time of Emperor Wen of Sui, who cultivated the kingly way and tightened military discipline, showing kindness and awe to keep them on loose reins;
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wen of Sui, who restored the kingly way, tightened military discipline, and held the Turks in check through kindness and awe;

sentences.zh: 煬帝失政教，生戎心，肇亂離以啟發之。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang lost good governance and teaching, bred barbarian hearts, and opened disorder and separation to stir them up.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang abandoned good government and teaching, bred a barbarian will to rebel, and opened the door to chaos that stirred them to rise.

sentences.zh: 高祖借其力而入平京師，群賊附其強而叠據河朔。

translations.literal: Gaozu borrowed their strength to enter and pacify the capital; the bandits attached themselves to their might and seized the territory north of the Yellow River one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu borrowed their strength to enter and pacify the capital; rebel bands clung to their power and seized the north one stronghold after another.

sentences.zh: 高祖同禦榻以延其使，太宗幸便橋以約其和。

translations.literal: Gaozu received their envoys on the same imperial couch; Taizong went to Bian Bridge to bind them in peace.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu received their envoys on the same imperial couch; Taizong went to Bian Bridge to seal a pact of peace.

sentences.zh: 當其時焉，不其盛矣！

translations.literal: In those days—was their glory not at its height!
translations.idiomatic: In those days, was their power not at its zenith!

sentences.zh: 竟滅其族而身死於國者，何也？

translations.literal: Yet in the end their clan was destroyed and they died in our realm—why?
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the end their clan was destroyed and they perished within the empire—why?

sentences.zh: 咸謂太宗有馭夷狄之道，李勣著戡定之功。

translations.literal: All say Taizong possessed the way of controlling barbarians, and Li Ji achieved the merit of pacification.
translations.idiomatic: All say that Taizong knew how to manage the barbarians and that Li Ji won the merit of their subjugation.

sentences.zh: 殊不知突厥之始也，賞罰明而將士戮力。

translations.literal: They little know that at the Turks' rise, rewards and punishments were clear and officers and soldiers exerted united effort.
translations.idiomatic: They do not see that when the Turks rose, rewards and punishments were clear and officers and soldiers fought as one.

sentences.zh: 遇煬帝之亂，亡命蓄怒者既附之，其興也宜哉！

translations.literal: Meeting Emperor Yang's disorder, fugitives nursing grievances all attached to them—their rise was fitting!
translations.idiomatic: When they met Emperor Yang's chaos, every fugitive nursing a grievance rallied to them—their rise was only to be expected!

sentences.zh: 頡利之衰也，兄弟扌勾隙而部族離心。

translations.literal: At Jieli's decline, brothers fell into estrangement and the tribes lost heart.
translations.idiomatic: When Jieli declined, brothers turned on one another and the tribes lost heart.

sentences.zh: 當太宗之理，謀臣猛將討逐之，其亡也宜哉！

translations.literal: Under Taizong's good order, strategists and fierce generals pursued and drove them out—their fall was fitting!
translations.idiomatic: Under Taizong's good order, strategists and fierce generals hunted them down—their fall was only to be expected!

sentences.zh: 洎武後亂朝，默啜犯塞，玄宗纂嗣，傳首京師，東封太山，西戎扈蹕，開元之代，繼踵來降。

translations.literal: Down to Empress Wu's disordering of the court, Moq chuo invaded the frontier; Xuanzong succeeded, heads were sent to the capital; he performed the eastern feng on Mount Tai, and western tribes escorted his carriage—in the Kaiyuan era, submission came in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Down through Empress Wu's disordering of the court, when Moq chuo raided the frontier, to Xuanzong's succession, when severed heads were sent to the capital; when he performed the feng sacrifice on Mount Tai and western tribes escorted his carriage—in the Kaiyuan era, one submission followed another.

sentences.zh: 西突厥諸族，遇其理，則眾心悅附而甲兵興焉；

translations.literal: The various tribes of the Western Turks—when order prevailed, hearts were pleased to attach and armor and weapons flourished;
translations.idiomatic: Among the Western Turkish tribes, when order prevailed, hearts rallied willingly and arms multiplied;

sentences.zh: 遇其亂，則族類怨怒而本根破矣！

translations.literal: when disorder came, clans turned resentful and their root was broken!
translations.idiomatic: when disorder came, clans turned resentful and their foundations were torn apart!

sentences.zh: 理亂二道，華夷一途。

translations.literal: Order and disorder are two paths; Chinese and barbarian follow one way.
translations.idiomatic: Order and disorder follow two paths, but for Chinese and barbarian alike the principle is one.

sentences.zh: 或質言於盛衰倚伏，未為確論。

translations.literal: To speak plainly of rise and fall as depending on fortune or misfortune is not yet a sure conclusion.
translations.idiomatic: To speak only of rise and fall in terms of fortune and misfortune is not yet a sound conclusion.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：中國失政，邊夷幸災。

translations.literal: The eulogy says: When China loses good government, border peoples seize the calamity.
translations.idiomatic: The eulogy says: When China loses good government, the border peoples seize their chance in the calamity.

sentences.zh: 理亂之道，取鑒將來。

translations.literal: The way of order and disorder—take it as a mirror for what is to come.
translations.idiomatic: The way of order and disorder—let it be a mirror for times to come.
